questions: Ellora caves contain temples of which religions?
Ellora (Maharashtra): 34 caves (600-1000 CE) - 12 Buddhist, 17 Hindu, 5 Jain. Kailasa Temple (Cave 16, Hindu, dedicated to Shiva) - carved from single rock, top-down. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
Government of India Act 1935 was based on which report?

GoI Act 1935: based on Simon Commission report + discussions at 3 Round Table Conferences. 321 sections + 10 Schedules - longest Act of British Parliament. Provincial autonomy (elected ministries), diarchy at Centre (never implemented). Federal part never enforced. Basis of Indian Constitution (250+ articles borrowed).
The founder of the Shunga dynasty was:

Pushyamitra Shunga: founded Shunga dynasty (185-73 BCE) by assassinating last Mauryan emperor Brihadratha. Brahmin general. Performed Ashvamedha sacrifice. Patron of Brahmanism (some sources say persecuted Buddhists). Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitra features his son Agnimitra.

Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931): Gandhi agreed to suspend Civil Disobedience + attend 2nd Round Table Conference. Irwin agreed to release prisoners + allow salt making for personal use + restore confiscated property. Gandhi attended 2nd RTC (Sep-Dec 1931, London) - failed. Resumed movement 1932.
Who was the founder of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha?

Bimbisara (c. 543-492 BCE): founder of Haryanka dynasty. Annexed Anga. Capital: Rajagriha (later Pataliputra under Udayin). Contemporary of Buddha. Son Ajatashatru imprisoned him. Strengthened Magadha through marriages + conquest.

Sunita Williams (American astronaut of Indian-Slovenian descent): visited space (NASA astronaut). First Indian-origin astronaut (NASA): Kalpana Chawla. Anousheh Ansari: Iranian-American first female space tourist (2006). Indian space tourist: none yet (ISRO planning Gaganyaan). Rakesh Sharma: first Indian citizen in space (1984, Soyuz T-11, Soviet mission).
First Indian film to win Oscar:

Bhanu Athaiya: first Indian to win Oscar (Best Costume Design for 'Gandhi' 1982, shared with John Mollo). Returned Oscar to Academy in 2012 (after brain tumor diagnosis, requested it be returned to India after death). First Indian film nominated for Best Foreign Language: Mother India (1957, lost to Nights of Cabiria by 1 vote). Satyajit Ray: Honorary Oscar 1992.
Buddha's life events: Born at Lumbini, enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (under Bodhi tree), first sermon at Sarnath (Dharmachakra Pravartana), death (Mahaparinirvana) at Kushinagar (c. 483 BCE).
Father of Indian Nuclear Program is:

Homi Jehangir Bhabha (1909-1966): Father of Indian Nuclear Program. Founded Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR, 1945). Founded Atomic Energy Establishment Trombay (AEET, 1954, renamed Bhabha Atomic Research Centre/BARC after death 1967). Died in plane crash on Mont Blanc (24 January 1966).
The British East India Company was established in:
EIC: founded 31 December 1600 by Royal Charter from Queen Elizabeth I. Originally 'Governor and Company of Merchants of London trading into the East Indies'. First factory at Surat (1613).
The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Gandhi in:

Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22): launched September 1920 at Calcutta session. Goal: Swaraj through non-violence. Boycott of schools, courts, foreign goods, elections. Withdrawn after Chauri Chaura incident (5 Feb 1922).
First Indian American woman astronaut was:

Sunita Williams: first Indian-American woman astronaut (NASA). Born 1965, Euclid, Ohio. Father: Deepak Pandya (Indian-origin neuroanatomist, Gujarat). Mother: Slovenian. ISS Expeditions 14/15 (2006-07), 32/33 (2012). Holds record for longest single spaceflight by woman (195 days). Currently training for Boeing Starliner mission (2024).
Battle of Plassey was fought in:

Battle of Plassey (23 June 1757): Robert Clive (East India Company) defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-Daula of Bengal. Betrayal by Mir Jafar (made new Nawab). Major cause: Company's fortification of Calcutta; Black Hole incident; Nawab's capture of Calcutta. Beginning of British rule in India.
States Reorganization Act was passed in:

States Reorganization Act (1956): created 14 states + 6 UTs on linguistic basis. Fazal Ali Commission (1953) recommended. New states: Andhra Pradesh (1953, first linguistic state - separate creation), Bombay (later split: Maharashtra + Gujarat in 1960), Kerala, Tamil Nadu (renamed from Madras), Karnataka (Mysore, renamed 1973).
Kailash Satyarthi won Nobel Peace Prize in:

Kailash Satyarthi: won Nobel Peace Prize 2014 (shared with Malala Yousafzai, Pakistan). For struggle against suppression of children + young people + right to education. Born 1954, Vidisha (MP). Founded Bachpan Bachao Andolan (Save the Childhood Movement, 1980). Rescued 80,000+ children from bonded labor. First India-born to win Peace Prize.
First Round Table Conference that Gandhi attended was the:

2nd Round Table Conference (7 September - 1 December 1931, London): Gandhi attended (only RTC he attended). Represented Congress. Discussed minority representation, federation, constitution. Failed to reach agreement. MacDonald's Communal Award (1932) followed. Gandhi returned empty-handed, resumed Civil Disobedience.

Subsidiary Alliance (1798, Lord Wellesley): Indian ruler had to keep British army + pay subsidy (or cede territory). Accept British Resident. No foreign relations without British permission. Nizam of Hyderabad first to sign (1798). Tipu, Marathas, Awadh followed. Eliminated French influence.

Bhoodan Movement (Land Gift, 1951): started by Acharya Vinoba Bhave at Pochampally (Telangana). Asked big landlords to gift 1/6th of land for distribution to landless. First donor: Vedire Ramachandra Reddy (100 acres). Resulted in ~47 lakh acres. Sarvodaya movement. Gramdan (village gift) - village donates all land.
Shivaji founded the Maratha Empire in which year?

Shivaji (1630-1680): crowned Chhatrapati 6 June 1674 at Raigad Fort. Founded Maratha Empire. Title: Kshatriya Kulawantas Sinhasanadheeshwar. Used guerrilla tactics. Built ~300+ forts. Ashtapradhan (8 ministers). Navy to fight Sidis + Portuguese. Father: Shahaji. Mother: Jijabai. Guru: Samarth Ramdas.
Which Harappan site has three parts: citadel, middle town, lower town?

Dholavira (Gujarat, Rann of Kutch): unique three-part city plan - citadel (bailey + castle), middle town, lower town. Water management: reservoirs covering ~17 hectares. Unique water conservation. Discovered by J.P. Joshi (1985). Excavated by R.S. Bisht.
Muhammad bin Qasim invaded Sind in which year?

Muhammad bin Qasim (17-year-old Arab general): invaded Sind in 712 CE on behalf of Umayyad Caliph Al-Walid I. Defeated Dahir (Hindu king of Sind) at Battle of Rawar. Captured Debal, Multan. First significant Muslim conquest in India. Umayyad rule extended. Recalled + executed later.
First Indian to win Chess World Championship:

Viswanathan Anand: first Indian Chess World Champion. Won FIDE World Chess Championship 2000 (Teheran) + 2007 (Mexico City). Defended 2008 (vs Kramnik), 2010 (vs Topalov). Lost to Magnus Carlsen 2013. Five-time world champion. Padma Vibhushan. Born: 11 December 1969, Chennai. Tamil Nadu.
Khalsa Panth was founded by which Sikh Guru?

Khalsa (1699, Baisakhi, Anandpur Sahib): founded by 10th Guru Gobind Singh. Created 'Singh' (lion) identity. Five Ks: Kesh, Kanga, Kara, Kachera, Kirpan. Panj Pyare (5 beloved ones). End of personal Guru - Guru Granth Sahib as eternal Guru. Defended against Mughals (Aurangzeb).
The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by:
Harihara I and Bukka Raya I (Sangama dynasty): founded Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE. Capital at Vijayanagara (Hampi). Inspired by sage Vidyaranya. Empire lasted till 1646 CE.
The Gandhara school of art flourished under which dynasty?

Gandhara school: 1st-5th century CE, under Kushans (especially Kanishka). Indo-Greek syncretic style. Blended Hellenistic (Greek) + Indian Buddhist elements. Buddha depicted with Greek features (wavy hair, draped robes, realistic body). Centres: Peshawar, Taxila, Swat.

Swaraj Party (1923): founded by C.R. Das (President) + Motilal Nehru (Secretary). 'Council entry' programme - contest elections to obstruct British from within. Formed after Non-Cooperation suspension. Defeated by 1926. Leaders re-joined Congress. Inspired later 'constructive programme'.
Partition of Bengal was announced on:

Partition of Bengal (16 October 1905, Lord Curzon): divided Bengal into East Bengal+Assam (Muslim majority) + West Bengal (Hindu majority). Claimed administrative efficiency. Real aim: divide Hindus + Muslims. Sparked Swadeshi movement. Annulment: 1911 (Lord Hardinge), capital shifted to Delhi.
The Gupta Era started from which year?
Gupta Era: 319-320 CE, started by Chandragupta I (founder of Gupta Empire). Gupta period (320-550 CE) considered 'Golden Age' of ancient India - art, science, literature flourished.
Charaka, the famous physician, lived during whose reign?

Charaka: physician (~1st-2nd century CE), court physician of Kanishka. Wrote 'Charaka Samhita' - foundational text of Ayurveda (internal medicine). Systematically described diseases, treatments, drugs. Sushruta (Sushruta Samhita - surgery) another ancient physician.
Chaitanya Mahaprabhu was a saint from which region?

Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (1486-1534): Bengali saint. Considered incarnation of Krishna + Radha combined. Founded Gaudiya Vaishnavism. Sankirtan (congregational chanting of Hari's name). Popularized Krishna bhakti. Disciples: Six Goswamis of Vrindavan. ISKCON (Prabhupada) traces to him.
First Factory Act was passed in:

First Factory Act (1881, Lord Ripon): prohibited employment of children under 7. Limited hours for children 7-12 (9 hours/day). 4 holidays/month. Second Factory Act 1891 (under Lord Lansdowne): prohibited child labor <9, limited women to 11 hours/day. British textile lobby opposed.
First non-Congress PM of India was:

Morarji Desai: first non-Congress PM (24 March 1977 - 28 July 1979). Janata Party (merger of Jan Sangh, Congress (O), Bharatiya Lok Dal, Socialist Party). 4th PM. Earlier: Deputy PM + Finance Minister (1967-69 under Indira). Resigned over split in Janata Party. Succeeded by Charan Singh (July 1979 - August 1979, 23 days - shortest PM term until 1996).
The Permanent Settlement (1793) was introduced by:
Permanent Settlement (Zamindari system, 1793): by Lord Cornwallis in Bengal, Bihar, Orissa. Fixed land revenue (89% to Company, 11% to zamindar). Made zamindars hereditary owners. Failed experiment.
First Anglo-Maratha War ended with which treaty?

1st Anglo-Maratha War (1775-1782): Raghunathrao (Raghoba) sought British help vs Maratha confederacy. Ended with Treaty of Salbai (May 1782). Status quo ante. British got Salsette + Bassein. Marathas recognized Sindhia territorial gains. Warren Hastings's diplomatic success.
Mahavira's teachings include the concept of:
Five vows (ahimsa, satya, asteya, brahmacharya, aparigraha)

5 Mahavratas (great vows): Ahimsa (non-violence), Satya (truth), Asteya (non-stealing), Brahmacharya (celibacy), Aparigraha (non-attachment). Triratna (three jewels): Right Faith, Right Knowledge, Right Conduct. Syadvada (anekantavada) - multi-perspectivism.
Mount Everest was first successfully climbed in:

Everest first ascent: 29 May 1953, 11:30 AM. Edmund Hillary (New Zealand) + Tenzing Norgay (Sherpa, Indian citizen later). 9th British Everest Expedition led by John Hunt. Reached summit via South Col. Tenzing later became director of Himalayan Mountaineering Institute (HMI), Darjeeling.
The Battle of Talikota (1565) was fought between:

Battle of Talikota (Rakshasi-Tangadi, 23 January 1565): combined Deccan Sultanates (Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Bidar, Berar, Golconda) defeated Vijayanagara (Ramaraya). Vijayanagara capital Hampi destroyed. End of Vijayanagara as major power. Aravidu dynasty continued but empire declined.

Indian Antarctic Program: started 1981. First expedition: 6 January 1981 (led by Dr. S.Z. Qasim, departed Goa). Reached Princess Astrid Coast (central Dronning Maud Land). Built 3 stations: Dakshin Gangotri (1983, abandoned), Maitri (1988), Bharati (2012). India is consultative member of Antarctic Treaty (since 1983).
First woman President of Indian National Congress was:

Annie Besant: first woman President of INC (1917, Calcutta session). Irish theosophist. Founded Home Rule League (1916). Sarojini Naidu: first Indian woman President (1925, Kanpur). Nellie Sengupta (1933, Indian married to Englishman). Indira Gandhi (1959). Sonia Gandhi (1998-2017, longest serving).
The Chalukya dynasty ruled from which capital?

Chalukyas of Badami (543-757 CE): Western Chalukyas. Capital: Vatapi (Badami, Karnataka). Founded by Pulakeshin I. Famous king: Pulakeshin II (defeated Harsha of Kanauj, 634 CE, Narmada banks). Aihole (first capital experiment), Pattadakal (UNESCO World Heritage site).
Babur established Mughal Empire in India after winning which battle?
First Battle of Panipat (1526): Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi. Used gunpowder + artillery + tulghuma (flanking) tactics. Marked beginning of Mughal Empire in India.
Indian Army's first woman officer to receive Sword of Honour:

Divya Ajith Kumar (2010): first woman to receive Sword of Honour at Officers Training Academy (OTA), Chennai. Top of 244 cadets (154 men + 90 women). Joined OTA 2009. Served in Indian Army (Short Service Commission). Earlier: Priya Jhingan (first woman to join Indian Army as a lawyer, 1992). First woman Lt Gen: Punita Arora (2005).

Dadasaheb Phalke (1870-1944): Father of Indian Cinema. Made India's first full-length feature film 'Raja Harishchandra' (1913, silent film, 40 minutes, 3 May 1913 release). Set up Phalke Films Company. Dadasaheb Phalke Award ( instituted 1969, India's highest film honor). 22 films in 19 years. First film with female actor: 'Bhasmasur Mohini' (Kamla Bai Gokhale).

'Inquilab Zindabad' (Long Live Revolution): coined by Urdu poet Hasrat Mohani in 1921. Popularized by Bhagat Singh and his associates. Became revolutionary slogan. Other slogans: 'Sarfaroshi ki Tamanna' (Bismil Azimabadi).

Gandhi assassination: 30 January 1948, Birla House (now Gandhi Smriti), New Delhi. By Nathuram Godse (Hindu nationalist, editor of Hindu Rashtra). Three bullets to chest. Gandhi's last words: 'Hey Ram' (disputed). Godse + Narayan Apte hanged 15 November 1949. Martyrs' Day: 30 January.
Mother Teresa was awarded Nobel Peace Prize in:

Mother Teresa (1910-1997): born Anjezë Gonxhe Bojaxhiu in Skopje (then Ottoman, now North Macedonia). Founded Missionaries of Charity (1950, Kolkata). Nobel Peace Prize 1979. Indian citizen 1951. Canonized Saint Teresa of Calcutta 4 September 2016 by Pope Francis. Beatified 2003. Served 'poorest of the poor' in Kolkata slums.
Indian Independence Act 1947 received Royal Assent on:

Indian Independence Act (1947): passed by British Parliament. Received Royal Assent 18 July 1947. Came into force 15 August 1947. Ended British rule. Created two dominions: India + Pakistan. British paramountcy over princely states lapsed - they could join either or remain independent.
Which Veda contains the famous Purusha Sukta (cosmic man hymn)?
Purusha Sukta (RV 10.90) describes cosmic man Purusha, whose body parts became the four varnas. Origin of varna system. Rigveda is oldest (1500-1000 BCE), 1028 hymns, 10 mandalas.
Green Revolution in India was led by:

Green Revolution (1960s-70s): M.S. Swaminathan (Indian geneticist) + Norman Borlaug (American, Nobel Peace Prize 1970) developed high-yielding wheat varieties. C. Subramaniam (Union Agriculture Minister). Key: Mexican dwarf wheat + IR8 rice. Made India self-sufficient in food grains by 1970s.
Fatehpur Sikri was Akbar's capital from:

Fatehpur Sikri (1571-1585): Akbar's capital for ~14 years. Built near Sikri (where Sufi saint Salim Chishti lived, predicted Akbar's sons). Buland Darwaza (~54m, after Gujarat conquest 1573). Jama Masjid, Panch Mahal, Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas. Abandoned due to water shortage.

PARAM 8000 (1991): India's first supercomputer. Built by C-DAC (Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, Pune, est. 1988). In response to US denial of Cray X-MP/24 supercomputer (post-1980s nuclear sanctions). 1 GFLOPS. Cost: ₹3.5 crore. Series: PARAM 10000 (1998), PARAM Padma (2003), PARAM Yuva (2008), PARAM Siddhi-AI (2020).
First Indian-origin Booker Prize winner was:

Salman Rushdie: won Booker Prize 1981 for 'Midnight's Children' (also 'Booker of Bookers' 1993 + 'Best of Bookers' 2008 for 40th + 50th anniversary). Born 1947, Bombay (now Mumbai), British-American. Other Indian-origin winners: Arundhati Roy (1997, 'God of Small Things'), Kiran Desai (2006), Aravind Adiga (2008).

Subhas Chandra Bose death: 18 August 1945, plane crash at Taihoku (now Taipei, Taiwan). Going to Tokyo from Saigon. Bose died in Japanese Army hospital. Body cremated, ashes at Renkoji Temple (Tokyo). Multiple conspiracy theories (Gumnami Baba, etc.). Justice Mukherjee Commission (2006) confirmed death. Disputed by some.
Varahamihira (6th century CE, Gupta period): Brihat Samhita (encyclopedia on astronomy, geography, architecture, omens). One of the nine gems (Navaratnas) in Chandragupta II's court.

Krishnadevaraya: greatest Vijayanagara emperor. Tuluva dynasty (3rd of 4). Title: 'Andhra Bhoja', 'Mooru Rayara Ganda' (Lord of 3 Kings). Wrote Amuktamalyada (Telugu). Built many temples. Portuguese traveler Domingo Paes described his reign as golden age.
Rakesh Sharma went to space in:

Rakesh Sharma: first Indian in space. 2 April 1984 (Soyuz T-11, Soviet spacecraft). Stayed at Salyut 7 orbital station for 7 days, 21 hours, 40 minutes. IAF Wing Commander. Asked by Indira Gandhi how India looked from space: 'Saare jahan se achha' (best in the world). Soviet-Indian Interkosmos program. Hero of Soviet Union.

Sabarmati Ashram (1917, Ahmedabad): Gandhi's second ashram in India (first: Kochrab Ashram, 1915). On banks of Sabarmati river. Original name: Satyagraha Ashram. Vows: truth, non-violence, celibacy, control of palate, non-stealing, non-possession, physical labor, swadeshi, fearlessness, equality of religions. From here: Dandi March (12 March 1930).
First PM of India to be assassinated:

Indira Gandhi assassinated: 31 October 1984 by her Sikh bodyguards (Satwant Singh + Beant Singh). Revenge for Operation Blue Star (June 1984). 30 bullets fired. Triggered anti-Sikh riots (1-4 November 1984). ~3000+ Sikhs killed. Succeeded by son Rajiv Gandhi (PM 1984-89). Rajiv assassinated 21 May 1991 (LTTE, Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu).

Kargil War (May-July 1999): Pakistani soldiers + militants infiltrated Indian side of LoC at Kargil (J&K). India's Operation Vijay recaptured peaks. International pressure forced Pakistan to withdraw. PM: Atal Bihari Vajpayee. Kargil Diwas: 26 July (victory). 527 Indian soldiers died. Major battles: Tiger Hill, Tololing.
The Barabar Caves (Bihar) were donated to which sect by Ashoka?

Barabar Caves (~250 BCE, Bihar): oldest surviving rock-cut caves in India. Donated by Ashoka to Ajivika sect (ascetic, founded by Makkhali Gosala, contemporary of Buddha + Mahavira). Known for brilliant polish on granite interior. Lomas Rishi cave famous for its entrance chaitya arch.
Guru Nanak Dev was born in:

Guru Nanak (1469-1539): founder of Sikhism. Born at Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib, Pakistan). Travels: 4 udasis (~24 years). Taught: Ek Omkar (one God), equality, honest living (kirat karo), share (vand chako), nam japo. Successor: Guru Angad. 9 subsequent Gurus. Total 10 Gurus. Adi Granth compiled 1604 by 5th Guru Arjan Dev.

Babri Masjid demolition (6 December 1992): kar sevaks demolished Babri Masjid at Ayodhya, Uttar Pradesh. Disputed site - claimed as Ram Janmabhoomi. Triggered Hindu-Muslim riots across India (Mumbai, Surat, etc.). Liberhan Commission (1992-2009). Supreme Court verdict (9 November 2019): land to Hindus for Ram temple, alternate land to Muslims. Ram Mandir consecration: 22 January 2024.
Battle of Buxar was fought in:

Battle of Buxar (22 October 1764): British (Hector Munro) defeated combined forces of Mir Qasim (Bengal Nawab), Shuja-ud-Daula (Awadh), Shah Alam II (Mughal emperor). More decisive than Plassey. Led to Diwani rights (Bengal revenue) to EIC (Treaty of Allahabad, 1765).
The Kanva dynasty succeeded which dynasty in Magadha?

Kanva dynasty (73-28 BCE): founded by Vasudeva after killing last Shunga ruler Devabhuti. Brahmin dynasty. Last king Susruman killed by Simuka (founder of Satavahana). Brief rule, declined Magadha's importance.
The 'Saptanga Theory' of state was propounded by:
Kautilya's Saptanga: 7 elements of state - Swami (king), Amatya (minister), Janapada (territory), Durga (fort), Kosha (treasury), Danda (army), Mitra (ally). State = organism with 7 angas.
Indian National Congress was founded in:

INC founded: 28 December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay. A.O. Hume (retired British civil servant) was first General Secretary. W.C. Bonnerjee was first President. First session: 72 delegates.
The Gupta king who took the title 'Vikramaditya' was:

Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya, 380-415 CE): defeated Shaka Satraps (Western Kshatrapas) of Gujarat/Malwa. Took title 'Sakari' + 'Vikramaditya'. Navaratnas (nine gems) in court: Kalidasa, Varahamihira, Dhanvantari, etc. Iron Pillar at Mehrauli. Golden Age peak.
Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF) was sent to:

IPKF (1987-1990): Indian Army sent to Sri Lanka under Indo-Sri Lanka Accord (29 July 1987, Rajiv Gandhi + J.R. Jayewardene). Aim: disarm LTTE (Tamil Tigers) + maintain peace. Turned against LTTE, ~1200 Indian soldiers died. Rajiv Gandhi assassinated by LTTE (May 1991). IPKF withdrawn March 1990 under V.P. Singh government.
Qutb-ud-din Aibak (1206 CE): founded Delhi Sultanate (Mamluk/Slave dynasty). Built Quwwat-ul-Islam mosque and Qutub Minar's first floor. Started construction in 1199.
Constituent Assembly adopted the National Flag on:

National Flag adopted: 22 July 1947 by Constituent Assembly. Designed by Pingali Venkayya (with Gandhi's input). Tricolor: saffron (courage/sacrifice), white (truth/peace), green (faith/chivalry) with Dharma Chakra (24 spokes, Ashoka) in center. Ratio: 3:2. Adopted officially 15 August 1947.
First President of India born after independence was:

Droupadi Murmu: first President born after independence (20 June 1958). Born Mayurbhanj, Odisha. 15th President (since 25 July 2022). First tribal + first woman from East India to be President. Earlier: Governor of Jharkhand (2015-2021), MLA + minister Odisha. Santhal tribe. BJP. Second woman President (after Pratibha Patil, 2007-12).
Shivaji killed Afzal Khan (general of Bijapur) at:

Afzal Khan episode (10 Nov 1659, Pratapgad): Afzal Khan (Adil Shahi general) invited Shivaji for meeting. Khan tried to kill Shivaji (concealed dagger). Shivaji killed Khan with bagh nakh (tiger claws, hidden in palm). Khan's army defeated. Famous episode of bravery.
Indian Navy's first nuclear submarine is:

INS Arihant (commissioned August 2016): first Indian nuclear-powered submarine (SSBN). Built under ATV (Advanced Technology Vessel) project. 6000 tonnes, 80 MW nuclear reactor. Carries K-15 (750 km) + K-4 (3500 km) missiles. INS Arighat (2nd SSBN) commissioned 2024. INS Chakra (Akula class) was leased from Russia (2012-2021).
Champaran Satyagraha was Gandhi's first civil disobedience in India, in:

Champaran Satyagraha (1917, Bihar): Gandhi's first civil disobedience in India. Indigo planters (tinkathia system) forced to grow indigo for British landlords (3/20 of land). Raj Kumar Shukla invited Gandhi. Gandhi arrived April 1917. Tinkathia abolished. Other early satyagrahas: Kheda (1918, Gujarat), Ahmedabad Mill (1918).
Megasthenes was the ambassador of which Greek king to Chandragupta Maurya's court?

Megasthenes: Greek ambassador from Seleucus Nicator to Chandragupta Maurya's court (~302 BCE). Wrote 'Indica' - describes Indian society, administration, Pataliputra. Mentioned 7-caste system (possibly inaccurate). Mauryan capital at Pataliputra impressed him.
Kargil Review Committee was headed by:

Kargil Review Committee (29 July 1999): headed by strategic analyst K. Subrahmanyam. Investigated intelligence failures in Kargil War. Submitted report January 2000. Recommended: better intelligence coordination, NSCS (National Security Council System), CDS (Chief of Defence Staff, created 2019), border management reforms.
Gandhi returned to India from South Africa in:

Gandhi returned: 9 January 1915 (Pravasi Bharatiya Divas celebrated 9 January in honor). Ship: SS Arabia. Reached Bombay (Mumbai). Gopal Krishna Gokhale (political guru) guided. Wrote Hind Swaraj (1909, in South Africa, on ship). Took 1 year to understand India (traveled 3rd class). First major satyagraha: Champaran (1917).

Lucknow Pact (1916): agreement between Congress + Muslim League. Congress accepted separate electorates + weightage for Muslims. Both demanded self-government (Swaraj). Brought Moderates + Extremists together (Tilak released 1914). Anne Besant + Tilak prominent. Sarojini Naidu presided Congress session 1918.
Shah Bano case (1985) was related to:

Shah Bano case: Supreme Court (1985) awarded maintenance under Section 125 CrPC to divorced Muslim woman (Shah Bano, 73-year-old). Congress govt (Rajiv Gandhi) passed Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Diversion) Act 1986 - overturned SC verdict, limited maintenance to iddat period. Seen as Muslim appeasement. Triggered conservative Hindu backlash + Babri movement.
Father of Indian Space Program is:

Vikram Sarabhai (1919-1971): Father of Indian Space Program. Founded Physical Research Laboratory (PRL, Ahmedabad, 1947). Established ISRO (1969, chairman till 1971). Set up Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS, 1963). Aryabhata satellite launched 1975 (named after mathematician).
Jainism was founded by whom in 6th century BCE?

Mahavira (599-527 BCE, contemporary of Buddha): 24th + last Tirthankara of Jains. Founded Jainism as organized religion. Earlier 23 Tirthankaras: Rishabhanatha (1st, adinatha) to Parsvanatha (23rd). Born Kundagrama (Vaishali). Nirvana at Pavapuri (~527 BCE).
First PM to be born after independence was:

Narendra Modi: first PM born after independence (17 September 1950, Vadnagar, Gujarat). 14th PM (since 26 May 2014). Three consecutive terms (2014, 2019, 2024) - first non-Congress PM to win 3 consecutive terms. Earlier: BJP general secretary, Gujarat CM (2001-2014). RSS background. Major initiatives: Make in India, Digital India, Demonetization, GST.
The Dancing Girl statue was found at which Harappan site?

Dancing Girl: bronze statuette (~10.5 cm, ~4500 years old) found at Mohenjo-daro in 1926. Lost-wax casting technique. Stands in confident pose, one hand on hip. Now in National Museum, Delhi. Symbol of Harappan art.
National Anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' was first sung at:

Jana Gana Mana (Rabindranath Tagore, 1911): first sung 27 December 1911 at Calcutta session of INC. Adopted as National Anthem 24 January 1950. Originally composed in Bengali (Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata). Hindi version official. 5 stanzas; first stanza = National Anthem. ~52 seconds to sing. English version: 'The Morning Song of India' (translated by Tagore).
First Chief Election Commissioner of India was:

Sukumar Sen: first CEC of India (21 March 1950 - 19 December 1958). Conducted first general elections 1951-52 (over 4 months). ~17.5 crore voters (85% illiterate). Symbol system (for illiterate voters). Set traditions of independent EC. India's first Chief Election Commissioner.
Pokhran II nuclear tests were conducted in:

Pokhran II (11-13 May 1998): India's second nuclear tests. 5 tests - 3 on 11 May (Shakti I, II, III) + 2 on 13 May (Shakti IV, V). Thermonuclear + fission devices. PM: Atal Bihari Vajpayee. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam + R. Chidambaram key scientists. USA, others imposed sanctions. Pakistan responded with tests (28 May 1998).
Which Harappan site is known for its dockyard?
Lothal (Gujarat): had the world's earliest known dockyard, connecting to Sabarmati river. Important maritime trade center. Discovered by S.R. Rao in 1957.
Cabinet Mission to India was led by:

Cabinet Mission (March 1946): Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State), Sir Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander. Plan: federal India, groupings of provinces, Constituent Assembly, Interim Government. Congress accepted, Muslim League initially accepted then rejected (called for Direct Action Day 16 August 1946).
Indo-Pak War of 1971 resulted in creation of:

1971 Indo-Pak War (3-16 December 1971): India intervened in East Pakistan civil war. ~93,000 Pakistani soldiers surrendered (16 December 1971, Dhaka). Bangladesh independent. Sheikh Mujibur Rahman first PM. Shimla Agreement (1972, Indira Gandhi + Bhutto). Pakistan lost half its population.
First war with Pakistan after independence was:

Indo-Pak War 1947-48: started October 1947, after Maharaja Hari Singh signed Instrument of Accession of J&K to India (26 October 1947). Pakistan-backed tribal + army invaded Kashmir. India airlifted troops. Fought till 1 January 1949 (UN-brokered ceasefire). LoC (Ceasefire Line) established.

Nalanda destruction: Bakhtiyar Khalji (~1193 CE, while raiding Bihar). Library burned for months. Thousands of monks killed. End of major Buddhist learning centre. Earlier visited by Hiuen Tsang (7th century), I-Tsing (7th century). UNESCO site 2016. Largest residential university of ancient world (~10,000 students).
Chola king who conquered Sri Lanka was:

Rajaraja I (985-1014 CE): conquered northern Sri Lanka (Anuradhapura, 993 CE). Built Brihadeshvara Temple (Rajarajeshvara) at Thanjavur (1010 CE). Expanded Chola navy - maritime power. Son Rajendra I conquered south Sri Lanka + sailed to Srivijaya (Sumatra, 1025 CE).
First PM from Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) was:

Atal Bihari Vajpayee: first BJP PM. Brief stint (16-31 May 1996, 13 days). Lost no-confidence motion, resigned. PM again: 1998-2004 (NDA government). Pokhran II (May 1998), Kargil (1999), Golden Quadrilateral highway project, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, Pravasi Bharatiya Divas started. Bharat Ratna 2015 (posthumous). Died 16 August 2018.
First Anglo-Mysore War was fought between:

Anglo-Mysore Wars (4): 1st (1767-69): Haidar Ali vs British (Nizam initially British ally, switched). Treaty of Madras (1769). 2nd (1780-84): Haidar died, Tipu continued. Treaty of Mangalore. 3rd (1790-92): Tipu lost half territory. 4th (1799): Tipu died defending Srirangapatna.
Operation Cactus was India's military intervention in:

Operation Cactus (3 November 1988): India intervened in Maldives after coup attempt by Tamil mercenaries (PLOTE). Indian paratroopers (6th Para) restored President Maumoon Abdul Gayoom. Captured mercenaries on ship. Successful operation, ~24 hours. Strengthened Indo-Maldives relations. Rajiv Gandhi PM.
Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram was built by which dynasty?

Shore Temple (Mahabalipuram, ~700 CE): built by Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha Pallava). Earliest significant stone temple in South India. Dedicated to Shiva + Vishnu. Originally 7 temples (called 'Seven Pagodas'), 6 now submerged/eroded. UNESCO World Heritage.
Right to Education Act (RTE) was passed in:

RTE Act 2009: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act. Effective 1 April 2010. Implements Article 21A (added by 86th Amendment 2002). Free + compulsory education for 6-14 years. 25% reservation in private schools for weaker sections. No-detention policy till Class 8 (modified 2019).
Maharana Pratap fought which Mughal emperor?

Maharana Pratap (1540-1597): Rajput king of Mewar (Udaipur). Defied Akbar (didn't submit). Battle of Haldighati (18 June 1576) - tactical draw against Mughal forces (Man Singh + Asaf Khan). Horse Chetak (died). Used guerrilla warfare. Recovered most of Mewar before death.
The Mauryan pillar at Sarnath has four lions and is now India's:

Sarnath Lion Capital: Mauryan period (c. 250 BCE, Ashoka). Adopted as India's National Emblem on 26 January 1950. Four Asiatic lions (only 3 visible at front) standing back-to-back. Dharma chakra (24 spokes) below. Chakra also on Indian flag.
Ashoka's Rock Edict XIII mentions which war as turning point?
Edict XIII: describes Kalinga War (c. 261 BCE) - massive casualties led Ashoka to Buddhism. Rock Edicts (14 major) at places like Girnar, Dhauli, Kalsi, etc. Pillar Edicts (7) at Delhi, Sarnath, etc.
Akbar's religious policy 'Din-i-Ilahi' was promulgated in:
Din-i-Ilahi (1582): syncretic religion propagated by Akbar. Combined elements of Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism, Christianity. Had only ~18 followers. Akbar declared infallible in 1579 (Mahzar).
Buddha delivered his first sermon at:

First sermon (Dharmachakra Pravartana, 'Turning the Wheel of Law'): Sarnath near Varanasi, in deer park (Mrigadava). After enlightenment at Bodh Gaya (~528 BCE). Taught Four Noble Truths + Eightfold Path to five disciples (panchavaggiya).
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar embraced Buddhism along with followers on:

Ambedkar + Buddhism: 14 October 1956 (Deekshabhoomi, Nagpur, on Vijayadashami). Converted with ~3,65,000 followers. Took 22 vows (rejecting Hindu deities). Died 6 December 1956 (sleep, age 65). Cremated at Dadar Chowpatty (now Chaitya Bhoomi). Triggered mass conversions. Navayana Buddhism (Navayana = 'new vehicle').
Kalidasa's most famous Sanskrit play is:

Abhijnanasakuntalam (Recognition of Shakuntala): Kalidasa's masterpiece Sanskrit drama. King Dushyanta + Shakuntala love story. Translated to English by William Jones (1789) - inspired Goethe. Other works: Meghaduta (Cloud Messenger, poetry), Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Ritusamhara, Malavikagnimitra, Vikramorvasiyam.
Sardar Patel's birthday is celebrated as:
National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas, 31 October)

National Unity Day (Rashtriya Ekta Diwas): 31 October (Sardar Patel's birthday). Declared 2014. Run for Unity organized. Patel integrated 562 princely states. Statue of Unity (182m, world's tallest statue) at Kevadia (Narmada dam, Gujarat), unveiled 31 October 2018 (143rd birth anniversary).
First Indian woman to win Olympic medal:

Karnam Malleswari: first Indian woman to win Olympic medal - bronze in weightlifting (69 kg category) at 2000 Sydney Olympics. From Andhra Pradesh. First Indian woman weightlifter + Olympian. Arjuna Award 1994, Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna 1995, Padma Shri 1999, Padma Bhushan 2024.
First general elections of independent India were held in:

First General Elections: October 1951 - February 1952 (over 4 months). Congress won 364/489 Lok Sabha seats (74%). Jawaharlal Nehru first PM. Voter turnout: 45.7%. 17.32 crore voters. ~85% illiterate voters used symbols. 53 parties + 1874 candidates. Sukumar Sen (CEC) organized.
The Indus Script remains undeciphered. Approximately how many symbols does it contain?

Indus Script: ~400-600 distinct symbols (not yet deciphered). Pictographic + logosyllabic. Found on seals, pottery, copper tablets. Bilingual inscriptions (with another script) absent. Asko Parpola, Iravatham Mahadevan worked on it. Direction: right-to-left.
CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act) was passed in:

CAA (Citizenship Amendment Act, 11 December 2019): amends Citizenship Act 1955. Provides citizenship to persecuted minorities (Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, Christians) from Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan (entered India before 31 Dec 2014). Excludes Muslims. Triggered pan-India protests (Shaheen Bagh). Implemented March 2024.
Charminar in Hyderabad was built by:

Charminar (1591, Hyderabad): built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah (5th sultan of Golconda). 4 minarets + 4 arches. Built to commemorate end of plague + founding of Hyderabad. Indo-Islamic architecture. Originally had school on top floor. Char Kaman, Makkah Masjid nearby.
The Hunas invaded India during whose reign?

Skandagupta (455-467 CE): repelled Hunas (Iranian Hunas) invasion. Fought fierce battles. Mentioned in Bhitari inscription. But Hunas eventually invaded again under Toramana (510 CE) + Mihirakula, contributing to Gupta decline.
Total Revolution (Sampoorna Kranti) was coined by:

Total Revolution (Sampoorna Kranti): Jayaprakash Narayan (JP). Started 1974 against Bihar Congress government. Extended nationally against Indira Gandhi's Emergency. Movement: students, workers, opposition parties. JP: 'Jindagi ka antim udeshya' (life's last mission). Led to Emergency (25 June 1975) + Janata Party government (1977).

Chandrayaan-1 (launched 22 October 2008): India's first lunar probe. Discovered water molecules (H₂O) + hydroxyl (OH) on lunar surface (September 2009). Moon Impact Probe (MIP) landed 14 November 2008 (planted Indian flag). NASA's M3 (Moon Mineralogy Mapper) instrument made discovery. Operated 312 days (lost contact August 2009).
Taj Mahal was commissioned by which Mughal emperor?

Taj Mahal: built by Shah Jahan as mausoleum for wife Mumtaz Mahal (Arjumand Banu Begum, died 1631 giving birth to 14th child). Construction: 1632-1653. Architect: Ustad Ahmad Lahauri (Persian). UNESCO World Heritage (1983). White marble + pietra dura inlay. Cost: ~32 million rupees (then).
The Partition of Bengal was carried out by:

Partition of Bengal (1905): by Lord Curzon. Officially: administrative efficiency. Actual: divide Bengali Hindus (Bengal proper) from Muslims (Eastern Bengal+Assam). Led to Swadeshi Movement. Reunited 1911.

Constitution adopted: 26 November 1949 (Constitution Day). Came into effect: 26 January 1950 (Republic Day). Drafting Committee: B.R. Ambedkar (Chairman). Took 2 years, 11 months, 18 days. 395 articles originally.
Alberuni came to India with whom?

Alberuni (Abu Rayhan al-Biruni, 973-1048): Persian polymath. Came with Mahmud of Ghazni (after 1017 Ghaznavid conquest of Khwarezm). Stayed in India. Wrote 'Tahqiq-i-Hind' (c. 1030): comprehensive study of Indian culture, religion, science. Learned Sanskrit. Praised Indian science. Critical of Mahmud's plunder.
First PM of India to die in office:

Jawaharlal Nehru: died 27 May 1964 (age 74, aortic aneurysm rupture). First PM to die in office. Served 17 years (15 August 1947 - 27 May 1964). Succeeded by Lal Bahadur Shastri (June 1964). Shastri died Tashkent (January 1966, mysterious). Indira Gandhi assassinated 31 October 1984. Rajiv Gandhi assassinated 21 May 1991.
First Indian woman to be awarded Bharat Ratna was:

Indira Gandhi: Bharat Ratna 1971 (while PM). First Indian woman to receive. Earlier male recipients: Radhakrishnan (1954), C.V. Raman (1954), Rajagopalachari (1954), Bhagwan Das (1955), Visvesvaraya (1955), Nehru (1955), Govind Ballabh Pant (1957), Dhondo Keshav Karve (1958), B.C. Roy (1961), Zakir Husain (1963).
Ahom kingdom was located in which present-day state?

Ahom kingdom (1228-1826): ruled Assam for ~600 years. Founded by Sukaphaa (Shan prince from Mong Mao). Defeated Mughals multiple times - Battle of Saraighat (1671, Lachit Borphukan defeated Aurangzeb's forces). Saraswati temple at Sivasagar. Mula Gabharu (Ahom princess, fought Mughals).
Venki Ramakrishnan won Nobel Prize in:

Venkatraman 'Venki' Ramakrishnan: Nobel Chemistry 2009 (with Thomas Steitz + Ada Yonath) for studies of structure + function of ribosome. Born 1952, Chidambaram (Tamil Nadu). Indian-American-British. President of Royal Society (2015-2020). Worked at MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Cambridge, UK.
Akbar built Buland Darwaza to commemorate his victory over:

Buland Darwaza (~54m tall, Fatehpur Sikri): built by Akbar in 1576 to commemorate Gujarat conquest (1573). 'Gateway of Magnificence'. Approachable by 42 steps. Persian inscription: 'Jesus, Son of Mary, said: The world is a bridge, pass over it, but build no house upon it.' Highest gateway in the world.
Chandrasekhara Venkata Raman won Nobel Prize for:

C.V. Raman (1888-1970): Nobel Prize Physics 1930 for 'Raman Effect' - inelastic scattering of light (1928). Discovered 28 February 1928 (National Science Day). Worked at IACS Kolkata. First Asian + first non-white to win Nobel in Science. Son: Chandrasekhar (Nobel 1983, Physics, USA citizen).
The Red Fort (Lal Qila) at Delhi was built by:

Red Fort (Lal Qila, Delhi): built by Shah Jahan (1639-1648) when he shifted capital from Agra to Delhi (Shahjahanabad). Red sandstone walls (2.4 km, 18-33m high). Architect: Ustad Ahmad Lahauri. Key buildings: Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Rang Mahal, Moti Masjid. Independence Day speech from ramparts since 1947.
Dr. B.R. Ambedkar's birth place is:
Mhow (now Dr. Ambedkar Nagar, Madhya Pradesh)

Dr. B.R. Ambedkar (14 April 1891 - 6 December 1956): born at Mhow (now Dr. Ambedkar Nagar), Madhya Pradesh. Father: Ramji Maloji Sakpal (Subedar in British Indian Army). Mahars (Mahar caste, Scheduled Caste). Educated: Elphinstone College (Bombay), Columbia University (PhD, 1917), LSE (DSc, 1923). Architect of Indian Constitution. Bharat Ratna 1990 (posthumous).
Mahajanapadas were how many in number?

16 Mahajanapadas (c. 600-321 BCE): Anga, Magadha, Kasi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Matsya, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara, Kamboja. Mentioned in Anguttara Nikaya. Magadha eventually dominated (Bimbisara, Ajatashatru).
The Mathura school of art developed under which dynasty?

Mathura school: 1st-3rd century CE, Kushan period. Indigenous style. Used red sandstone. Buddha in abhaya mudra, happy features, ushnisha. First to depict Buddha in human form (earlier symbols). Also made Jain + Hindu images. Independent from Gandhara school.
Raja Todar Mal: Akbar's finance minister. Implemented 'Zabt system' (standard land revenue based on average produce). Earlier worked under Sher Shah Suri. One of Akbar's Navaratnas.
The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro was made of:
The Great Bath: 12×7×2.4m tank, made watertight with finely fitted burnt bricks and gypsum mortar. Possibly used for ritual bathing. Earliest known public water tank.
Stupa architecture reached its peak at which site?

Sanchi Great Stupa (Madhya Pradesh): oldest stone structure in India. Originally by Ashoka (~3rd century BCE), expanded by Shungas + Satavahanas. Four toranas (gateways) with intricate carvings. UNESCO World Heritage (1989). Discovered by General Taylor (1818), restored by John Marshall.
Cabinet Mission to India came in:

Cabinet Mission (March 1946): Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps, Alexander. Proposed: federal India with groupings of provinces, Constituent Assembly, Interim Government. Rejected by Muslim League later. Led to partition.
Right to Information Act was passed in:

RTI Act 2005: enacted 15 June 2005, effective 12 October 2005. Replaced weaker 2002 Act. Allows citizens to request information from public authorities (within 30 days, 48 hours if life/liberty). Aruna Roy, Anna Hazare, MKSS movement. Penalty for non-compliance. Resulted in transparency, exposed corruption.
The Civil Disobedience Movement began with:

Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha): 12 March - 6 April 1930. Gandhi walked 240 miles (384 km) from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi with 78 followers. Made salt, broke Salt Law. Started Civil Disobedience Movement.
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was born at:

Dr. Rajendra Prasad (3 December 1884 - 28 February 1963): born at Zeradei (Siwan district, Bihar). First President of India (26 January 1950 - 13 May 1962, 2 terms). President of Constituent Assembly (1946-49). Minister of Food + Agriculture in Interim Government (1946). Bharat Ratna 1962. Refused to take salary while in office.

Operation Flood (1970-1996): 'White Revolution' - made India world's largest milk producer. Verghie Kurien ('Father of White Revolution' + 'Milkman of India'). AMUL founded 1946 (Tribhuvandas Patel + Kurien). Anand Milk Union Limited (Gujarat cooperative model). Kurien first chairman of NDDB.

Liberhan Commission: formed 16 December 1992 to investigate Babri Masjid demolition. Headed by Justice M.S. Liberhan (longest serving commission in India). Submitted report 30 June 2009 (17 years). Report (1029 pages) tabled in Parliament November 2009. Indicted: L.K. Advani, Murli Manohar Joshi, Uma Bharti, Kalyan Singh, etc.
The earliest evidence of rice cultivation in India comes from:

Lahuradewa (Sant Kabir Nagar, UP): evidence of rice cultivation from ~7000 BCE (mid-Holocene). Excavated by Rakesh Tewari. Pushed back Indian agriculture timeline. Earlier rice evidence also at Koldihwa (UP, Belan valley).
First Indian to climb Mount Everest was:

Tenzing Norgay (Sherpa): first Indian to summit Everest (29 May 1953, with Edmund Hillary of New Zealand). Tenzing later got Indian citizenship. Born Nepal/Sikkim. Bachendri Pal: first Indian woman to climb Everest (23 May 1984). First Indian (independent expedition): Avtar Singh Cheema (1965, with Tenzing's son).
Surdas was a devotee of which deity?

Surdas (1478-1561, approximate): blind Hindu devotional poet + singer. Krishna bhakti. Wrote 'Sursagar' (Ocean of Melody) - 100,000+ poems (some say), ~8000 survive. Surdas's Krishna: child + lover (Braj Bhasha language). Court poet of Akbar (legend). One of Navaratnas (disputed).
Wood's Despatch of 1854 is known as:
Magna Carta of English Education in India

Wood's Despatch (19 July 1854, Charles Wood, President of Board of Control): 'Magna Carta of English Education in India'. Recommended: English medium higher education, vernacular primary, department of public instruction in each province, universities at Calcutta, Bombay, Madras (1857).
First Indian-origin woman to win Nobel Prize in Science:
Esther Duflo (2019, Economics, French-American with Indian-origin husband)

Esther Duflo: French-American economist. Won Nobel Economics 2019 (with Abhijit Banerjee, her husband, + Michael Kremer). Youngest Nobel Economics laureate (46). Second woman to win Nobel Economics (after Elinor Ostrom 2009). MIT professor. Did extensive field studies in India (Rajasthan, Bihar). Co-founded J-PAL.
Fa-Hien, the Chinese pilgrim, visited India during whose reign?

Fa-Hien (Faxian, 399-414 CE): Chinese Buddhist monk. Visited India during Chandragupta II's reign. Came to collect Buddhist texts. Wrote 'Fo-kwo-ki' (Record of Buddhist Kingdoms). Described Gupta administration, peaceful society. Mentioned first evidence of untouchables (Chandala).
Chanakya (Kautilya) was a professor at which university?

Chanakya: professor at Takshashila (Taxila, in modern Pakistan). Later became Chandragupta Maurya's mentor. Wrote Arthashastra at Taxila. Ancient university: ~7th century BCE to 5th century CE (destroyed by White Huns). Famous for medicine, politics, mathematics.
Ilbert Bill controversy (1883) was related to:
Trial of Europeans by Indian judges

Ilbert Bill (1883, Lord Ripon + Courtenay Ilbert): proposed to allow Indian judges to try European accused. European community strongly opposed ('white mutiny'). Compromise: European accused got right to jury with half Europeans. Showed racial attitudes. Strengthened Indian nationalism.
Brihadeshvara Temple was built by which Chola king?

Brihadeshvara (Rajarajeshvara) Temple: Thanjavur, built by Rajaraja I (1003-1010 CE). Tallest in world at time (216 ft vimana). Dedicated to Shiva. Massive Nandi (13 ft × 16 ft, single stone). UNESCO World Heritage (1987). Excellent Dravidian architecture. Inscriptions detail temple administration.
Kabir was a disciple of which saint?

Kabir (1440-1518 CE): mystic saint-poet. Disciple of Ramananda (Varanasi). Bijak, Sakhi Granth collections. Criticized both Hindu + Muslim rituals. Nirguna bhakti (formless God). Spoke in vernacular (Sadhukkari). Kabir Panth followers. Famous dohas ('Dukh mein sumirana sab kare').
Doctrine of Lapse was used to annex which kingdom first?

Doctrine of Lapse (Lord Dalhousie): if Indian ruler died without natural male heir, kingdom 'lapsed' to British. First applied: Satara (1848). Others: Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Baghat, Udaipur, Jhansi (1853), Nagpur, Tanjore, Carnatic. Awadh annexed on grounds of misgovernance (1856).

Independence: 15 August 1947. Power transferred from British to India and Pakistan (partition). Lord Mountbatten last Viceroy, first Governor-General. Jawaharlal Nehru first PM. Rajendra Prasad first President (1950).

Lahore Session (December 1929, Jawaharlal Nehru president): declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as goal. Resolution: 26 January 1930 to be celebrated as Independence Day (Purna Swaraj Day). Civil Disobedience Movement announced (launched 12 March 1930 with Dandi March).
Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) was launched in:

Mangalyaan (MOM, Mars Orbiter Mission): launched 5 November 2013 by PSLV-C25. Entered Mars orbit 24 September 2014. India became first country to succeed on first attempt. ISRO became 4th space agency (after USSR, NASA, ESA) to reach Mars. Cost: ~$74 million (cheapest Mars mission). Operated for 8 years (lost contact April 2022).

August Declaration (Montagu Declaration, 20 August 1917): Edwin Montagu (Secretary of State for India). Promised 'gradual development of self-governing institutions' in India + 'progressive realization of responsible government'. Aim: win Indian support during WWI. Disappointed radicals (no timeline).
Article 1 of Constitution declares India as:

Article 1: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States'. Two names: 'India' (English) + 'Bharat' (Hindi). 'Union' preferred over 'Federation' (no right of secession, indestructible Union of destructible states). Originally debate: India, Bharat, Hindustan, Bharatvarsha. Final: India + Bharat.
Hunter Committee was set up to investigate:

Hunter Committee (1919, Lord Hunter): investigated Jallianwala Bagh massacre. Condemned Dyer but didn't punish severely (only censured). Indian National Congress formed parallel inquiry (Motilal Nehru, C.R. Das, M.K. Gandhi, Abbas Tyabji) - more critical. Dyer retired but received £26,000 from British public.
Tolkappiyam is the earliest extant Tamil grammar, written by:

Tolkappiyam: oldest extant Tamil grammar (~3rd century BCE to 1st century CE). Author: Tolkappiyar. Three parts: Ezuttu (letters), Sol (words), Porul (subject matter). Defines Tamil grammar + poetics. Earliest Tamil literature. Source for Sangam era society.
Mohan Das Karamchand Gandhi was born at:

M.K. Gandhi (2 October 1869 - 30 January 1948): born at Porbandar (Gujarat). Father: Karamchand Gandhi (Diwan of Porbandar). Mother: Putlibai (4th wife). Married Kasturba (1883, age 13+14). Educated: Alfred High School, Rajkot; Samaldas College, Bhavnagar; London (law, 1888-91). South Africa: 1893-1914. Returned to India: January 1915.
Potti Sreeramulu died on hunger strike in 1952 demanding:

Potti Sreeramulu: 58-day hunger strike (October - December 1952). Demanded separate Andhra state for Telugu speakers (out of Madras state). Died 15 December 1952 (58 days). Within days, Andhra State formed (1 October 1953). Triggered States Reorganization (1956) on linguistic basis.
First Indian-origin winner of Nobel Economics after Amartya Sen:

Abhijit Banerjee (2019): Nobel Economics (with wife Esther Duflo + Michael Kremer) for experimental approach to alleviating global poverty. Born 1961, Mumbai. Professor at MIT. Co-founded J-PAL (Abdul Latif Jameel Poverty Action Lab). Member of NAC (National Advisory Council) under UPA government. Mother: Nirmala Banerjee (economist).
First Five Year Plan was launched in:

1st Five Year Plan (1951-56): focus on agriculture + irrigation (Bhakra Nangal, Damodar Valley, Hirakud). Modeled on Soviet planning. PC Mahalanobis - architect of 2nd plan (heavy industries). Planning Commission formed 15 March 1950 by Cabinet Resolution. Replaced by NITI Aayog (1 Jan 2015).
Gandhi's Salt March (Dandi March) was in:

Dandi March (Salt Satyagraha): 12 March - 6 April 1930. Gandhi + 78 followers walked ~384 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi (Gujarat coast). Gandhi made salt, broke Salt Law. Started Civil Disobedience Movement. ~60,000 arrested including Gandhi, Nehru, Patel. Round 2: Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931.

Satavahanas (~1st century BCE - 3rd century CE): also called Andhras in Puranas. Capital: Pratishthana (Paithan, Maharashtra). Founder: Simuka. Greatest: Gautamiputra Satakarni. First to give land grants to Brahmans. Matronymics (mother's name) - unique.
The Quit India Movement was launched in:

Quit India Movement (8 August 1942): launched by INC at Bombay session (Gowalia Tank, now August Kranti Maidan). Slogan: 'Do or Die' (Gandhi). Response to Cripps Mission failure. Mass arrests, underground activities.
Chauri Chaura incident took place on:

Chauri Chaura (4 February 1922, Gorakhpur, UP): protesters set police station on fire, 22 policemen burnt alive. Part of Non-Cooperation Movement. Gandhi shocked - immediately withdrew movement (11 Feb 1922). Considered violence betrayal of ahimsa. Gandhi went on 5-year fast + prison (6 years sentence, served 2).
Ibn Battuta, the famous traveler, visited India during whose reign?

Ibn Battuta (Moroccan traveler, 1304-1377): visited India 1333-1342 CE during Muhammad bin Tughlaq's reign. Appointed as Qazi of Delhi. Wrote 'Rihla' (Travelogue). Mentions Tughlaq's eccentric reforms.
Mahmud of Ghazni invaded India how many times?

Mahmud of Ghazni (998-1030 CE): invaded India 17 times (1000-1026 CE). Famous attack: Somnath Temple (1025 CE). Other targets: Kangra, Mathura, Kannauj, Thanjavur (no). Aimed at plunder, not annexation. Took wealth to Ghazni. Patronized Alberuni (wrote Tahqiq-i-Hind).
Amaravati school of art flourished under which dynasty?

Amaravati school (~2nd century BCE - 3rd century CE): under Satavahanas + Ikshvakus. White marble limestone. Famous for narrative panels on stupa. Dynamic figures. Influenced later South Indian + SE Asian sculpture. Style spread to Sri Lanka, Java.
Lal Bahadur Shastri gave which slogan during 1965 Indo-Pak war?

'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' (Hail Soldier, Hail Farmer): Lal Bahadur Shastri's slogan during 1965 Indo-Pak war + food crisis. Tashkent Declaration (10 January 1966, signed with Ayub Khan, USSR brokered). Shastri died same day (heart attack, mysterious). PM 1964-66. Earlier: 'Jai Hind' (Subhas Bose).

MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act): passed September 2005, effective 2 February 2006 (200 districts, expanded nationally 2008). 100 days of wage employment per rural household per year. Legal right. Minimum wage. Women's participation (~57%). Largest social security program worldwide. ~15 crore active workers.
Who founded the Forward Bloc in 1939?

Forward Bloc (22 June 1939): founded by Subhas Chandra Bose after resigning from INC presidency. Goal: complete independence through armed struggle. Bose later formed INA (Indian National Army) in 1942 in Singapore with Japanese help.
The Allahabad Pillar inscription describes whose achievements?

Allahabad Pillar (Prayagraj): Ashokan pillar with later Samudragupta inscription (composed by Harisena, court poet). Describes Samudragupta's conquests - 'digvijaya' across India. Lists kings he defeated/forced to pay tribute. Lists frontier kingdoms, forest kingdoms, etc.

Mountbatten Plan (3 June 1947): announced by Lord Mountbatten. Partition of India into India + Pakistan. Provincial assemblies to vote. Independence Act passed by British Parliament (18 July 1947). Implemented 14-15 August 1947. Boundary Commission (Radcliffe) drew borders in 5 weeks.
Operation Blue Star (1984) was related to:

Operation Blue Star (1-6 June 1984): Indian Army stormed Golden Temple (Harmandir Sahib, Amritsar) to flush out Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale + Sikh militants (fortified inside). Heavy casualties: ~500 militants + civilians, 83 soldiers. Akal Takht damaged. Triggered Indira Gandhi's assassination (31 October 1984, by Sikh bodyguards) + anti-Sikh riots.
First individual Olympic gold for India:

Abhinav Bindra: India's first individual Olympic gold. 10m air rifle, Beijing Olympics 2008 (11 August). Score 700.5 (Olympic record). From Chandigarh. First Indian to hold World + Olympic titles simultaneously. Padma Bhushan 2009. Earlier: Rajyavardhan Rathore silver (2004, double trap), Norman Pritchard 2 silver (1900, Paris).
First Indian to win Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences:

Amartya Sen: won Nobel Economics 1998 for contributions to welfare economics (social choice theory, capabilities approach, famine causes). Indian citizen at time of award. Born 1933, Santiniketan (WB). Taught at LSE, Oxford, Harvard. Master of Trinity College, Cambridge (1998-2004). Bharat Ratna 1999. Books: 'The Argumentative Indian', 'Development as Freedom'.
The Sangam literature was compiled at which city?

Sangam (literary gatherings, 3 Sangams): patronized by Pandya kings of Madurai. 1st: Madurai (no texts survive). 2nd: Kapadapuram (only Tolkappiyam survives). 3rd: Madurai (most surviving texts: Ettuttokai, Pattupattu). Period: ~3rd century BCE to 3rd century CE. Tamil language + culture.
Operation Safed Sagar was the name of:

Operation Safed Sagar: Indian Air Force operations during Kargil War (May-July 1999). First large-scale use of airpower in mountain warfare since WWII. IAF lost 2 fighters + 1 helicopter (shot down by Pakistan). MiG-21s, MiG-23s, MiG-27s, Mirage 2000s, Mi-17 helicopters used. Successful target destruction.
First Indian to reach South Pole:

Col. Inderjit Singh: first Indian to reach South Pole (1960). Indian Army doctor. Wintered at Mirny station (Soviet Antarctic Expedition). Honored by Government of India. India's first Antarctic expedition: 1981 (Goa to Princess Astrid Coast). First Indian station: Dakshin Gangotri (1983, abandoned, now buried). Maitri (1988, still active). Bharati (2012).

Pallavas (4th-9th century CE): capital Kanchipuram (Tamil Nadu). Founder: Simhavishnu. Famous: Mahendravarman I, Narasimhavarman I (defeated Pulakeshin II). Rock-cut architecture (Mahabalipuram, Rathas). Pallavas precursors to Cholas.

INS Vikrant (R11): India's first aircraft carrier. Acquired 1961, served till 1997 (36 years). Originally HMS Hercules (UK, Majestic class). Played key role in 1971 Indo-Pak war (blockaded East Pakistan). Decommissioned 31 January 1997. Scrapped 2014-15. New INS Vikrant (IAC-1) commissioned 2 September 2022 - first indigenous aircraft carrier.
President of India who died in office (first):

Dr. Zakir Husain (8 February 1897 - 3 May 1969): first President of India to die in office. 3rd President (13 May 1967 - 3 May 1969). Former Governor of Bihar, Vice President (1962-67). Co-founder of Jamia Millia Islamia (1920). Bharat Ratna 1963. Followed by V.V. Giri (acting, then elected 1969 - controversial election vs Neelam Sanjiva Reddy).

Bangladesh: independence declared 26 March 1971 by Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (arrested same day). Liberation War 26 March - 16 December 1971. India intervened 3 December 1971 (after Pakistani airstrikes). Pakistani surrender 16 December 1971 (Vijay Diwas). Bangladesh formally independent 16 December 1971.
Vijayanagara Empire's capital Hampi is in which state?

Hampi (Vijayanagara): in Karnataka, on Tungabhadra river banks. UNESCO World Heritage (1986). Founded 1336 by Harihara + Bukka. Empire ended 1565 (Battle of Talikota vs Deccan Sultanates). Sites: Virupaksha Temple, Vittala Temple (stone chariot), Lotus Mahal, Hazara Rama Temple, Mahanavami Dibba.

Simon Commission (1927, Simon, 7 members): all British. Came to review Govt of India Act 1919. Indians boycotted (no Indian member). 'Simon Go Back' demonstrations. Lala Lajpat Rai injured in lathi charge (died 17 November 1928). Bhagat Singh + associates assassinated Saunders (mistakenly).
Alauddin Khilji's market reforms were related to:

Alauddin Khilji (1296-1316): introduced price control (Diyal-e-Razai) for grains, cloth, horses, slaves. Maintained by rationing, spies. Aimed to support large army. Successfully repelled Mongol invasions.
Last Governor-General of independent India was:

C. Rajagopalachari ('Rajaji'): last Governor-General of India (June 1948 - 26 January 1950). First + only Indian GG. Succeeded Mountbatten (returned to UK). When India became Republic 26 January 1950, GG post replaced by President (Rajendra Prasad first). Rajaji: founder of Swatantra Party (1959).

Latur earthquake: 30 September 1993, Maharashtra. Magnitude 6.2 (Mw). Killed ~10,000+ (some estimates 30,000). Intraplate earthquake. Epicenter: Killari village. Destroyed 50+ villages. Worst earthquake in stable continental region. Triggered: better building codes, seismic zonation, disaster management frameworks.
Akbar's navaratnas included how many gems?

Navaratnas (Nine Gems of Akbar's court): 1) Birbal (Mahesh Das - wit/judicial), 2) Tansen (Ramtanu Pandey - music), 3) Todar Mal (revenue), 4) Faizi (poet laureate), 5) Abul Fazl (Akbarnama), 6) Tardas Mal, 7) Mullah Do Piazza, 8) Raja Man Singh (general), 9) Abdul Rahim Khan-i-Khana.

Surat Split (1907): Congress split at Surat session. Extremists (Tilak, Lal-Bal-Pal, Aurobindo) vs Moderates (Gokhale, Pherozeshah Mehta). Extremists wanted Swaraj, boycott, national education. Moderates wanted reforms within constitutional limits. Extremists expelled. Reunited 1916 (Lucknow Pact).
Gol Gumbaz at Bijapur was built as the mausoleum of:

Gol Gumbaz (1656, Bijapur, Karnataka): mausoleum of Mohammed Adil Shah (7th sultan of Bijapur). Architect: Yaqut of Dabul. Largest dome in Asia (44m diameter). Whispering Gallery (echo 7+ times). 2nd largest unsupported dome in world (after St. Peter's Basilica).
Gandhi's first major satyagraha in South Africa was against:

Satyagraha (term coined 1906 by Gandhi, replaced 'passive resistance'): first major satyagraha in South Africa - against Asiatic Registration Act (Transvaal, 1906) requiring Indians to register + carry certificates. Earlier incidents: 1893 train expulsion (Pietermaritzburg, color prejudice). Phoenix Settlement (1904). Tolstoy Farm (1910). Gandhi returned to India: January 1915.
Hiuen Tsang visited India during whose reign?

Hiuen Tsang (Yuan Chwang): Chinese pilgrim, visited India 630-645 CE during Harsha's reign. Came to Nalanda University (studied 5 years). Wrote 'Si-Yu-Ki' (Buddhist Records of Western World). Met Harsha at Kanauj (643 CE). Described India extensively. Stayed 14 years in India.

Emergency (25 June 1975 - 21 March 1977): imposed by President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed on advice of PM Indira Gandhi (after Allahabad HC annulled her election, JP movement). Article 352 (internal disturbance). Political leaders arrested (JP, Morarji, Advani, Vajpayee, etc.). Censorship. 20-point program. 21-month period. Elections March 1977 - Janata Party won.

'Vande Mataram': from Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel 'Anandamath' (1882). Composed by Jadunath Bhattacharya, set to music by Rabindranath Tagore. National song of India (Article 343). Jana Gana Mana is national anthem.
First Round Table Conference was held in:

1st Round Table Conference (12 Nov 1930 - 19 Jan 1931, London): called by Lord Irwin to discuss India's future. Congress boycotted (most leaders in jail post Civil Disobedience). Attended: Muslim League, Hindu Mahasabha, Liberals, princes, depressed classes (Ambedkar). 89 delegates.

Bahmani Kingdom (1347-1527): founded by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (also Hasan Gangu). Rebelled against Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Capital: Gulbarga (later Bidar). Split into 5 Deccan Sultanates (1518-1527): Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Berar, Bidar, Golconda.
The Kushan king Kanishka started which era in 78 CE?

Kanishka's accession (78 CE) started Saka Era (now India's national calendar). Adopted officially by Govt of India (22 March 1957, Chaitra 1). Used for Gazette of India, news broadcasts, calendars. Originally 78 CE = Saka year 0.
First Indian to win Fields Medal (Mathematics Nobel equivalent):

Manjul Bhargava: first Indian-origin winner of Fields Medal (2014). For work in number theory (especially rational points on elliptic curves). Born 1974, Canada, Indian parents. Professor at Princeton. Padma Bhushan 2015. Indian-American + Canadian. Mathematics equivalent of Nobel Prize (awarded every 4 years to under-40 mathematicians).
Quit India Resolution was passed at:

Quit India Resolution: passed 8 August 1942 at Bombay AICC session (Gowalia Tank Maidan, now August Kranti Maidan). Gandhi gave 'Do or Die' slogan (Karo ya Maro). 9 August: Gandhi, Nehru, Patel, Azad arrested (taken to Aga Khan Palace, Pune). Movement became leaderless, violent. British suppressed.
Akbar's regent during his early years was:
Bairam Khan: Akbar's regent (1556-1560) after Humayun's death. Helped Akbar win Second Battle of Panipat (1556) against Hemu. Removed by Akbar at age 18. Killed later in Gujarat.
Bhakti saint Ramanuja was the founder of which philosophy?

Ramanuja (1017-1137 CE): founder of Vishishtadvaita (Qualified Non-dualism). Soul + matter are qualities of Brahman. Bhakti (devotion) as path. Influenced Sri Vaishnavism. Commentaries on Brahma Sutras, Bhagavad Gita. Left Srirangam for Karnataka to escape Shaiva persecution.
First Muslim woman to win Booker Prize:

Arundhati Roy: won Booker Prize 1997 for 'The God of Small Things' (debut novel). Born 1961, Shillong (Meghalaya). Mother: Mary Roy (Syrian Christian). Father: Bengali tea planter. Other works: 'The Ministry of Utmost Happiness' (2017). Activist: Narmada Bachao Andolan, Kashmir, Maoists. Sahitya Akademi Award returned (2015).
Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on:

Jallianwala Bagh (13 April 1919, Baisakhi day): Brig. Reginald Dyer ordered firing on peaceful gathering at Amritsar. 379+ killed (official), ~1000+ actual. Rabindranath Tagore returned knighthood. Hunter Commission investigated.

Alam Ara: India's first talkie film (sound film). Released 14 March 1931, Majestic Cinema, Bombay. Director: Ardeshir Irani. Hindi + Urdu. Cast: Master Vithal, Zubeida. Music: Ferozshah M. Mistry. Lost film (no prints survive). Started era of song-dance in Indian films. First color film: Kisan Kanya (1937).
The 'Doctrine of Lapse' was introduced by:

Lord Dalhousie (1848-1856): Doctrine of Lapse - if Indian ruler died without natural heir, kingdom 'lapsed' to British. Used to annex: Satara (1848), Jaitpur, Sambalpur, Baghat, Udaipur, Jhansi (1853), Nagpur, Awadh (1856).
Kautilya (Chanakya/Vishnugupta): wrote Arthashastra (treatise on statecraft, economics, military strategy). Chandragupta Maurya's minister. Rediscovered by R. Shamasastry in 1905.
Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy of India, served as Governor-General of India until:

Mountbatten: last Viceroy (March-August 1947), first Governor-General of independent India (August 1947 - June 1948). Succeeded by C. Rajagopalachari (June 1948 - January 1950) - last GG + first Indian GG. India became Republic 26 January 1950 - President replaced GG.
Alexander invaded India in which year?

Alexander the Great invaded India in 326 BCE. Crossed Indus, fought Battle of Hydaspes (Jhelum) vs King Porus (Purushottama). Porus impressed Alexander ('treat me like a king'). Macedonian army refused to cross Beas (mutiny). Alexander returned, died 323 BCE in Babylon.
The first war of Indian Independence took place in:

Revolt of 1857 (Sepoy Mutiny/First War of Independence): started 10 May 1857 at Meerut. Causes: greased cartridges (pig/cow fat), Doctrine of Lapse, social reforms. Leaders: Bahadur Shah Zafar, Rani Lakshmibai, Tatya Tope, Nana Saheb, Begum Hazrat Mahal.
The 'Painted Grey Ware' (PGW) culture is associated with which period?

PGW: ~1100-500 BCE. Iron Age culture in Ganga-Yamuna doab. Associated with later Vedic Aryans, Mahabharata period. Sites: Hastinapura, Ahichchhatra, Mathura. Wheel-made grey pottery with black/red painted designs. B.B. Lal excavated.
The Great Granary of Harappa was approximately what size?

Great Granary (Harappa): massive structure ~45m × 15m. Multiple rooms with raised floors for grain storage. Indicators of surplus agricultural production, central authority, taxation system. Mohenjo-daro also had granary + warehouse.

Rowlatt Act (March 1919): based on Rowlatt Committee recommendations. Allowed British government to imprison without trial (up to 2 years), no appeal, no lawyer. Aim: control revolutionary activities. Indian outrage: 'Black Act'. Gandhi called Hartal (6 April 1919). Led to Jallianwala Bagh.
The Regulating Act of 1773 made which office Governor-General of Bengal?
Regulating Act 1773: made Warren Hastings first Governor-General of Bengal (1773-1785). Established Supreme Court at Calcutta (1774). Centralized administration. Response to corruption.
Interim Government of India (1946) was headed by:

Interim Government (2 September 1946): formed from Constituent Assembly. Headed by Jawaharlal Nehru (Vice President with Viceory as President). Portfolio distribution: Nehru (External Affairs + Commonwealth), Patel (Home + Information + Broadcasting), Rajendra Prasad (Food + Agriculture), etc. Muslim League joined October 1946.
First Indian American US Congressman was:

Dalip Singh Saund: first Asian American, first Indian American, first Sikh American US Congressman. Elected 1956 (California's 29th district). Served 1957-1963 (3 terms). Born 1899, Chhajulwadi (Punjab). Came to USA 1920 (UC Berkeley PhD mathematics). Lost re-election 1962 (stroke). Bobby Jindal: second Indian American (2004).
Indian Universities Act (1904) was passed by:

Indian Universities Act (1904, Lord Curzon): reduced university senates (governors). Increased government control over universities. Periodic inspection. Curzon seen as restricting higher education. Indian National Congress criticized. Initiated Swadeshi movement (1905).

Tirukkural: classic Tamil text (~500 CE, debatable). Author: Thiruvalluvar. 1330 couplets (kural) in 133 chapters, 3 books (Aram/Virtue, Porul/Wealth, Inbam/Love). Universal ethics. Translated to 80+ languages. Called 'Tamil Veda' or 'Universal Veda'. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan translated to English.

Tansen (c. 1500-1586): original name Ramtanu Pandey. Born at Gwalior. Disciple of Swami Haridas (Vrindavan). Court musician of Ram Chand (Baghel king, Rewa). Akbar heard about him, brought to his court. One of Navaratnas. Created new ragas (Miyan ki Malhar, Miyan ki Todi). Dargah at Gwalior.
Sant Tukaram was a saint of which tradition?

Tukaram (1608-1649): Varkari saint from Dehu (Maharashtra). Disciple of Sant Namdev. Abhangas (devotional poetry in Marathi). Worshipped Vithoba (Vitthala) of Pandharpur. Criticized caste. Other Varkari saints: Dnyaneshwar (1275-1296, first), Namdev, Eknath, Tukaram.
Goa was liberated from Portuguese in:

Goa Liberation: Operation Vijay (17-19 December 1961). Indian Army annexed Goa, Daman, Diu from Portuguese (last European colony in India). 451-year Portuguese rule ended (1510-1961). Portuguese offered UN Security Council seat, USSR vetoed. Goa statehood 30 May 1987. Operation: 36 hours.

Kalpana Chawla (1962-2003): first Indian woman in space. Born Karnal, Haryana. First flight: STS-87 (November 1997, Columbia). Died 1 February 2003 in Space Shuttle Columbia disaster (STS-107) during reentry over Texas. Sunita Williams (also Indian-origin astronaut, father from India) - longest spacewalk by woman.
Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel was born in:

Sardar Patel (31 October 1875 - 15 December 1950): born Nadiad, Gujarat. 'Iron Man of India', 'Bismarck of India'. First Deputy PM + Home Minister (1947-50). Integrated 562 princely states into Indian Union (using 'privy purse' + 'Police Action' in Hyderabad). Title 'Sardar' from women of Bardoli Satyagraha (1928). Bharat Ratna 1991.
Buddha attained enlightenment under which tree?

Bodhi tree at Bodh Gaya (Bihar): Buddha attained enlightenment under this peepal (Ficus religiosa) tree after 49 days of meditation (~528 BCE, age 35). Original tree destroyed; current tree descendant (~130 years old). Mahabodhi Temple UNESCO site.
First Indian to win Nobel Prize was:

Rabindranath Tagore: first Indian Nobel (1913, Literature, for 'Gitanjali'). Translated himself into English (1912). Other early: C.V. Raman (1930, Physics - Raman Effect). Hargobind Khorana (1968, Medicine - USA citizen). Mother Teresa (1979, Peace - Albanian-Indian). Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar (1983, Physics - USA).
The Third Buddhist Council was held at:
3rd Council: Pataliputra (c. 250 BCE), under Ashoka, presided by Moggaliputta Tissa. Led to split into Sthaviravadins (orthodox) and Mahasanghikas. Sthaviravada later evolved into Theravada.
The Priest-King statue was found at which site?

Priest-King: soapstone statue (~17.5 cm) found at Mohenjo-daro (1927, Mackay). Bearded figure with robe decorated with trefoil patterns. Possibly a religious or political leader. Now in National Museum, Karachi, Pakistan.

Article 370 abrogation (5 August 2019): Government of India revoked special status of Jammu & Kashmir (Article 370). J&K Reorganization Act (31 October 2019): split into 2 UTs - J&K + Ladakh. Statehood of J&K promised (not yet restored). Internet suspended for months. Political leaders arrested. Supreme Court upheld (December 2023).
The Pashupati Seal found at Mohenjo-daro depicts which figure?
A seated figure surrounded by animals

Pashupati Seal: steatite seal at Mohenjo-daro depicting horned figure seated in yogic posture, surrounded by animals (elephant, tiger, rhino, buffalo, deer). John Marshall (1931) identified as proto-Shiva (Pashupati, 'Lord of Animals'). Controversial interpretation.
First Indian American US Senator was:

Kamala Harris: first Indian American US Senator (2016, California). Mother from India (Tamil), father from Jamaica. Elected Vice President of USA 2020 (first woman, first African American, first Asian American VP). Sworn in 20 January 2021. Lost 2024 presidential election to Donald Trump.
Razia Sultan was the daughter of:

Razia Sultan (Raziya al-Din): ruled 1236-1240 CE. First woman ruler of Delhi Sultanate. Daughter of Iltutmish (who chose her as successor over her brothers). Deposed by nobles, killed by her brother's army.

Vernacular Press Act (1878, Lord Lytton): imposed restrictions on vernacular Indian language press. No prior censorship for English press. Required printers to give undertaking not to publish seditious material. Could be confiscated without trial. Repealed 1881 by Ripon.

Khilafat Movement (1919-1924): ended when Turkey abolished Caliphate (March 1924, Mustafa Kemal Atatürk). Initially against British weakening of Ottoman Caliph after WWI. Ali Brothers led. Gandhi supported (Hindu-Muslim unity). Merged with Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22).
The Mauryan Empire was founded by:
Chandragupta Maurya (322-298 BCE): founded Mauryan Empire with help of Chanakya (Kautilya). Overthrew Nanda dynasty. Established first major Indian empire. Mentions in Megasthenes' Indica.
First session of Indian Constituent Assembly was presided by:

Constituent Assembly first session: 9 December 1946. Interim President: Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (oldest member). Permanent President elected 11 December 1946: Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Vice Presidents: H.C. Mookherjee, V.T. Krishnamachari. Constitutional Advisor: B.N. Rau.
Ajanta caves are famous for which type of art?

Ajanta (Maharashtra): 30 Buddhist caves (2nd century BCE - 5th century CE). Murals (frescoes) depicting Jataka tales. Under Vakatakas (5th c.). UNESCO World Heritage Site. Discovered 1819 by British hunters.
Tulsidas wrote Ramcharitmanas in which language?

Tulsidas (1532-1623): wrote Ramcharitmanas (~1574) in Awadhi (vernacular, accessible). Translation/adaptation of Valmiki's Sanskrit Ramayana. Other works: Vinaya Patrika, Kavitavali, Hanuman Chalisa (most recited Hindu text). Lived in Varanasi. Established Sankat Mochan Temple.

Bhopal Gas Tragedy (2-3 December 1984): world's worst industrial disaster. Union Carbide India Limited (UCIL) pesticide plant leaked ~42 tonnes of methyl isocyanate (MIC) gas. ~3,800+ immediate deaths, 5,00,000+ affected. 2nd + 3rd December night. CEO Warren Anderson fled India. Settlement 1989 ($470 million). Site still contaminated. Curative petition in Supreme Court (2023 onwards).
Vande Mataram was adopted as National Song on:

Vande Mataram (Bankim Chandra Chatterjee, from Anandamath 1882): adopted as National Song of India on 24 January 1950 (same day as Jana Gana Mana as National Anthem). Equal status with Jana Gana Mana (constitutionally). First 2 stanzas have status. Sanskritized Bengali. Singing time: ~1 minute 5 seconds. Rabindranath Tagore first sang.
Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) belongs to which period?

NBPW: ~700-200 BCE. Characteristic glossy metallic black slip pottery. Mauryan + Shunga period. Luxury ware, pan-Indian distribution. Indicators of urbanization, trade, second urbanization. Sites: Taxila, Pataliputra, Ujjain.

Aadhaar Act 2016 (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services): passed as Money Bill in March 2016. Provides legal backing to Aadhaar (UIDAI formed 2009). Mandatory for various services (PAN, bank, mobile - some relaxed by SC). SC upheld validity 2018, with restrictions. ~135 crore Aadhaar holders.
Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded which reform movement in 1828?
Brahmo Samaj (1828): founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy ('Father of Indian Renaissance'). Opposed Sati, idolatry, caste rigidity. Advocated women's rights, modern education. Tagore later joined.
The famous iron pillar at Mehrauli (Delhi) belongs to which period?

Mehrauli Iron Pillar: Gupta period (4th century CE), under Chandragupta II. Sanskrit inscription mentions 'Chandra'. Rust-resistant for 1600+ years - metallurgical marvel. Originally at Udayagiri, moved to Delhi.
Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in:
Vasco da Gama (Portuguese): reached Calicut (Kozhikode, Kerala) on 20 May 1498. Welcomed by Zamorin. Opened sea route from Europe to India. Founded Portuguese trading empire.
Meerabai was a devotee of which deity?

Meerabai (1498-1546): Rajput princess (Marwar, Jodhpur). Devotee of Krishna (called him 'Giridhar Gopal'). Married Bhoj Raj (Mewar prince, eldest son of Rana Sanga). Rejected traditional role. Bhajans in Rajasthani/Hindi. Guru: Raidas (leather worker saint). Her in-laws tried to kill her multiple times.

Basavanna (1106-1168 CE): founder of Lingayat/Virashaiva sect (Karnataka). Rejected caste, idol worship, Sanskrit. Worshipped Shiva as Ishtalinga (worn on body). Vachana literature (Kannada). Anubhava Mantapa - first Parliament-like body. Equality of women.
Qutub Minar: started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (1199), completed by Iltutmish (1220). 72.5m tall, 5 stories. Firoz Shah Tughlaq repaired after lightning. UNESCO World Heritage Site.
The Fourth Buddhist Council was held under whose patronage?

4th Buddhist Council: ~72 CE, Kashmir, under Kanishka (Kushan emperor). Presided by Vasumitra + Ashvaghosha. Result: split into Hinayana (Sthaviravada/Theravada) and Mahayana. Mahayana more inclusive, Bodhisattva ideal. Sanskrit became canonical language.

Nehru Report (1928): drafted by committee chaired by Motilal Nehru. First Indian attempt at constitution. Recommended: dominion status, federal structure, joint electorates (with reserved seats for minorities), fundamental rights. Jinnah rejected (later proposed his 14 points). Radicals (Nehru, Bose) wanted complete independence.
Madhvacharya, founder of Dvaita philosophy, lived during which period?

Madhvacharya (1238-1317 CE): founder of Dvaita (dualism). God (Vishnu) + souls + matter are eternally distinct. Born near Udupi (Karnataka). Established Krishna temple at Udupi. Ashtottara mathas. Purnaprajna, Anandatirtha. Strong critic of Shankara's Advaita.
Shankaracharya, propounder of Advaita Vedanta, was born in:

Adi Shankaracharya (788-820 CE, traditional dates): born at Kaladi (Kerala). Propounded Advaita Vedanta (non-dualism - Brahman alone is real). Restored Hinduism against Buddhism. Established 4 mathas (Sringeri, Dwarka, Puri, Jyotirmath). Wrote commentaries on Upanishads, Brahma Sutras, Gita.
The Harappan Civilization flourished during which period?
