The mature Harappan/Indus Valley Civilization period is dated approximately 2500-1900 BCE (mature phase). Discovered in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni at Harappa. Major sites: Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan.

Swadeshi Movement (1905-1908): started against Partition of Bengal. Use of Indian goods, boycott of British. Leaders: Surendranath Banerjee, Aurobindo Ghosh, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai (Lal-Bal-Pal). National Council of Education (1906) - Bengali institute. First major mass movement.

Khilafat Movement (1919-1924): by Ali Brothers (Shaukat Ali, Muhammad Ali) to protest abolition of Ottoman Caliphate after WWI. Gandhi supported it (Hindu-Muslim unity). Merged with Non-Cooperation Movement 1920-22.
Indian Ocean Tsunami (2004) was triggered by earthquake of magnitude:

Indian Ocean Tsunami: 26 December 2004 (Boxing Day). Earthquake off Sumatra, Indonesia (9.1-9.3 Mw, 3rd largest ever recorded). Triggered tsunamis up to 30m high. Killed ~2,30,000+ across 14 countries. India: ~18,000+ deaths (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Andaman & Nicobar). Tamil Nadu worst hit. Nagapattinam district: ~6,000+ deaths. Early Warning System set up at INCOIS, Hyderabad.
Aurangzeb spent the last ~25 years of his life fighting which revolts?

Aurangzeb (1658-1707): last 25 years spent in Deccan fighting Marathas. Also faced revolts: Jats (Mathura, Gokula), Satnamis (Narnaul), Sikhs (Guru Tegh Bahadur executed 1675, Guru Gobind Singh), Rajputs (Mewar, Marwar). Died 1707 at Ahmednagar. Empire declined rapidly after.
India's first indigenous communication satellite was:

INSAT-1A: India's first indigenous communication satellite (multipurpose). Launched 10 April 1982 (Delta rocket, USA). Failed after 4 months (power issues). INSAT-1B (1983) more successful. Series: INSAT-2, 3, 4. Used for telecom, TV, weather. Aryabhata (1975) was India's first satellite (experimental).
India's first nuclear test was conducted in:

Smiling Buddha (18 May 1974): India's first nuclear test. Pokhran (Rajasthan), desert. Peaceful nuclear explosion (PNE). Yield: ~12 kt. PM Indira Gandhi. Led to Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) formation 1975. USA imposed sanctions. Second tests: 11-13 May 1998 (Pokhran II, Vajpayee govt).

Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, Sukhdev: hanged 23 March 1931 in Lahore jail (smuggled out at night, cremated at Hussainiwala on Sutlej). Convicted for killing J.P. Saunders (1928) and Assembly bombing (1929). Hanged at age 23.
Financial Emergency under Article 360 has been imposed how many times?

Article 360 (Financial Emergency): never imposed in India. Allows President to declare if financial stability threatened. Salaries of judges, government employees can be reduced. Lasts 2 months unless approved by Parliament (6 months renewable).
Under the amended Protection of Human Rights Act, 2019, the Chairperson of the NHRC is:
A person who has been Chief Justice of India OR a Judge of the Supreme Court
Only a retired Chief Justice of India
The Chief Justice of India in office
A retired Judge of a High Court
The Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019 broadened the eligibility - the Chairperson of the NHRC is now a person who has been a CJI OR a Judge of the SC (earlier only retired CJI).
The GST Council is constituted under which Article of the Constitution?

Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment, 2016, provides for the GST Council, a joint forum of the Centre and the States. Chaired by the Union Finance Minister, it has the Union Minister of State for Finance and State Finance Ministers as members.
The 31st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1972 is significant for:
Raising the strength of Lok Sabha from 525 to 545 members

31st Amendment (1972) raised the maximum strength of Lok Sabha from 525 to 545 and of State Assemblies proportionally. Currently Lok Sabha has 543 elected + 2 nominated (Anglo-Indian nominations discontinued from 2020 by the 104th Amendment), totalling 545 constitutional seats.
Article 262 of the Constitution deals with:
Adjudication of inter-State river water disputes
Article 262 empowers Parliament to provide for adjudication of any dispute or complaint with respect to use, distribution or control of waters of an inter-State river or river valley.
The Finance Commission is constituted under which Article?

Article 280: Finance Commission. Constituted by President every 5 years. Recommends distribution of tax revenue between Centre and States. Chairman + 4 members. 16th FC (2026-30): Arvind Panagariya (Chairman). 15th FC (2021-26): N.K. Singh.
Anti-Defection Law was added by which amendment?

Anti-Defection Law: 52nd Amendment (1985), added Tenth Schedule. Disqualification of MPs/MLAs if they defect from party. Presiding officer decides. Exceptions: merger (2/3 of party), split. Strengthened by 91st Amendment (2003).
The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 relates to:

74th Amendment (1992) inserted Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG) and the 12th Schedule with 18 functional items, giving constitutional status to urban local bodies - Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils and Municipal Corporations.
Article 19(1) of the Constitution guarantees how many fundamental freedoms to citizens?

Article 19(1) guarantees six freedoms: (a) speech and expression; (b) assemble peaceably without arms; (c) form associations or unions; (d) move freely throughout India; (e) reside and settle in any part of India; (f) practise any profession, or carry on any occupation, trade or business.
Failure to comply with Union directions authorizes President's Rule in a State

Article 365 provides that where any State fails to comply with, or to give effect to, any direction given in the exercise of the executive power of the Union under any provision of the Constitution (e.g.
Untouchability and its practice in any form
Article 17 abolishes 'untouchability' and forbids its practice in any form. It declares enforcement of any disability arising out of untouchability an offence punishable by law.
Article 356 of the Constitution deals with:

Article 356: President's Rule in State (State Emergency). Imposed when constitutional machinery fails (Governor's report or otherwise). State Assembly dissolved or suspended. Used controversially many times. SR Bommai case (1994) laid guidelines.
The Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV of the Constitution resemble mainly the principles of which country?
The concept of DPSP is borrowed from the Irish Constitution (Article 45). They are non-justiciable directions to the State. Dr. Ambedkar called them 'instruments of instructions'.
The legislative relations between the Union and the States are dealt with in:

Articles 245 to 255 (Chapter I of Part XI) deal with legislative relations between Union and States. Article 245 provides that Parliament makes laws for whole or part of India, and State Legislatures for the State.
The 11th Schedule of the Constitution, added by the 73rd Amendment, contains:
Subject lists of Union, State, Concurrent
The 11th Schedule, inserted by the 73rd Amendment, 1992, contains 29 functional items that may be transferred to Panchayats for implementation as institutions of self-government.
The Ninth Schedule was added to the Constitution by:

1st Amendment (1951) added the Ninth Schedule via new Article 31B to protect certain land reform laws from judicial review on grounds of violating Fundamental Rights. Originally 13 laws; now 284 entries. SC in I.R. Coelho (2007) held post-1973 entries open to basic-structure review.
The Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution contains subjects like:
Criminal Law, Marriage and Divorce, Education, Forests, Trade Unions
The Concurrent List (List III) has subjects on which both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate. Presently 52 entries (after 42nd Amendment transferred some entries from State List).
A Money Bill under Article 110 can be introduced:
Only in the Lok Sabha and only with the President's prior recommendation
In the Lok Sabha without any prior recommendation

A Money Bill (Article 110) can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha and only on the prior recommendation of the President. The Speaker certifies it as a Money Bill. Rajya Sabha cannot amend or reject; it can only recommend amendments within 14 days, which Lok Sabha may accept or reject.
Freedom of conscience and free profession, practice and propagation of religion

Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the right freely to profess, practise and propagate religion, subject to public order, morality, health and other Part III provisions. Permits State regulation of secular activity associated with religion and social welfare/reform.
Panchayati Raj was first adopted by which state?

Panchayati Raj first adopted: Rajasthan (Nagaur district, 2 October 1959) by Pt. Nehru. Andhra Pradesh soon after. Three-tier (Balwantrai Mehta Committee 1957): Gram Panchayat (village), Panchayat Samiti (block), Zilla Parishad (district).
The Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission holds office for a term of:
Six years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier

Article 316 provides that the Chairman and members of UPSC hold office for 6 years or until 65 years of age, whichever is earlier. For Joint Public Service Commission, the term is 6 years or 62 years.
The Inter-State Council is established under which Article of the Constitution?

Article 263 empowers the President to establish an Inter-State Council if at any time it appears that public interests would be served by its establishment. First established in 1990 on the recommendation of the Sarkaria Commission (1988).
The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 added which new Part to the Constitution?
Part IVA relating to Fundamental Duties

73rd Amendment (1992) inserted Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and the 11th Schedule, giving constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions. Compulsory three-tier system, five-year term, State EC under Article 243K, State FC under Article 243I, reservation for SC/ST and one-third women.
The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes is provided for under which Article?
The 89th Amendment, 2003 inserted Article 338A providing for a separate NCST. The Commission consists of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three members appointed by the President.
The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is established under which Article?

Article 315: UPSC established. Conducts civil services examinations (Civil Services, Engineering, Medical, CDS, NDA, etc.). Chairman + members appointed by President. Tenure: 6 years or 65 years. Independent constitutional body.
The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act deals with:

86th Amendment (2002): made Right to Education a Fundamental Right under Article 21A. Free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years. Added Fundamental Duty for parents (51A(k)). RTE Act passed in 2009.
Money Bills can be introduced only in:

Money Bills (Article 110): introduced only in Lok Sabha with President's prior recommendation. Rajya Sabha can only recommend changes within 14 days; Lok Sabha may accept/reject. Speaker's certificate needed. Rajya Sabha cannot reject.
Voting age was reduced from 21 to 18 by which amendment?
61st Amendment (1988, Rajiv Gandhi): reduced voting age from 21 to 18 years. First applied in 1989 elections. Aimed at youth participation. Article 326 amended.

74th Amendment (1992): Urban local bodies. Part IXA (Articles 243P-243ZG). Three types: Nagar Panchayat (transitional area), Municipal Council (small town), Municipal Corporation (large urban area). Reservation for women, SC/ST.
The minimum age to contest for Lok Sabha is:
Lok Sabha MP: minimum 25 years. Rajya Sabha MP: 30 years. Voter: 18 years (61st Amendment, 1988, reduced from 21). MLA: 25 years. MLC: 30 years.
How many members signed the original Constitution?
284 members signed the original Constitution on 24 January 1950. Total members: 389 initially (later reduced to 299 after partition). Assembly had 11 sessions over 2 years 11 months 18 days.
Article 39A of the Constitution (added by 42nd Amendment) deals with:
Equal justice and free legal aid

Article 39A, inserted by the 42nd Amendment (1976), directs the State to ensure that the legal system promotes justice and provides free legal aid, so that opportunities for securing justice are not denied to any citizen by reason of economic or other disabilities.
The scheme of 'Cooperative Federalism' in India emphasizes:
Centre and States working together as partners in development
Cooperative federalism refers to a relationship of partnership and cooperation between the Union and the States. The Inter-State Council (Article 263), GST Council (Article 279A), Zonal Councils.
Under the 73rd Amendment, reservation of seats for women in Panchayats is:
At least one-third of the total seats (including chairpersons)
Article 243D mandates reservation of not less than one-third (including one-third of seats reserved for SC/ST women) of total seats for women in Panchayats, including the offices of Chairpersons.
Which amendment clarified that nothing in Article 13 shall apply to any amendment made under Article 368?

24th Amendment (1971) was enacted to neutralize the Golak Nath (1967) judgment which held that Fundamental Rights could not be amended. It amended Articles 13 and 368 to clarify that an amendment under Article 368 is not a 'law' under Article 13.
The term 'Zero Hour' in Indian Parliament refers to:
The hour between 12 noon and 1 pm for Question Hour
The time immediately following Question Hour when members can raise matters without prior notice
The time allotted for financial Bills
The time for private members' Bills

Zero Hour is the time immediately following Question Hour (normally 12 noon) during which members can raise matters of urgent public importance without prior notice (which is required for other businesses).
The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in:

DPSP: Part IV, Articles 36-51. Borrowed from Irish Constitution. Non-justiciable but fundamental to governance. Aimed at establishing 'welfare state'. Categories: Socialist, Gandhian, Liberal-Intellectual. Article 39A (equal justice), 44 (Uniform Civil Code), 48 (cow protection).
The 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 is associated with:
Lowering the voting age from 21 to 18 years

61st Amendment (1988) amended Article 326 to lower the voting age for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections from 21 to 18 years. First elections with the new age were held in 1989. Aimed at politically empowering the youth; expanded the electorate by ~5 crore voters.
The Model Code of Conduct comes into force from:

MCC: comes into force immediately on announcement of election schedule by ECI. Binding on government, ruling party, candidates. Restricts new schemes, transfers, ad appointments. ECI enforces. Violation can lead to disqualification.
The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is provided for under:

Article 315 provides for PSCs for the Union (UPSC) and for the States (SPSCs). UPSC conducts examinations for recruitment to All-India Services and Central Services Group A & B. Articles 315-323 deal with composition, appointment, removal, functions etc.
The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education was inserted as a Fundamental Right through:

86th Amendment (2002) inserted Article 21A making free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years. Also amended Article 45 (early childhood care) and added a Fundamental Duty under Article 51A(k). The enabling RTE Act was passed in 2009.
The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was accorded constitutional status through:

102nd Amendment (2018) inserted Article 338B granting constitutional status to NCBC for safeguarding interests of the socially and educationally backward classes. Earlier a statutory body under a 1993 Act; now has a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three Members.
President's Rule under Article 356 is imposed when:
A State fails to comply with Union directions on any matter
The constitutional machinery of a State fails or breaks down
The ruling party loses majority in the Assembly
The Governor recommends dissolution of State Assembly

Article 356 empowers the President to assume State executive functions when satisfied that governance cannot be carried on in accordance with the Constitution. The State Assembly is either suspended or dissolved. Approved by Parliament within 2 months; lasts max 6 months per proclamation.
Article 32 has been described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as:
The heart and soul of the Constitution

Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) empowers a citizen to move the SC directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights through five writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto. Dr.
The NITI Aayog replaced which body in 2015?

NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India): formed 1 January 2015, replaced Planning Commission (1950-2014). Think-tank, advisory body. CEO: B.V.R. Subrahmanyam (2025). Governing Council: PM + CMs + LGs. No financial powers (unlike PlanCom).
The residuary powers of legislation (subjects not mentioned in any List) vest in:

Article 248 vests residuary legislative powers (including the power to make laws imposing tax not mentioned in any List) in Parliament. This marks a tilt towards the Centre in India's federal scheme, unlike in the USA where residuary powers vest with the States.
The Finance Commission is constituted under which Article of the Constitution?

Article 280 provides for the constitution of a FC by the President every five years (or earlier). It recommends distribution of net proceeds of taxes between Union and States and among States, principles governing grants-in-aid from Consolidated Fund of India to States.
The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2019 is significant because it:
Abolished the nomination of Anglo-Indians to Lok Sabha and State Assemblies

104th Amendment (effective 25 January 2020) discontinued the nomination of two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha under Article 331 and one each to State Assemblies under Article 333, originally meant for 10 years but extended repeatedly.
The National Commission for Scheduled Castes is provided for under which Article?

Article 338 provides for the NCSC, with a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three other members appointed by the President. The 89th Amendment, 2003 bifurcated the erstwhile combined Commission for SCs and STs into two separate Commissions - NCSC (Article 338) and NCST (Article 338A).
Reservation of seats in Lok Sabha for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes is based on:
Their population ratio as ascertained at each Census, with seats re-allocated after each Census
Fixed numbers specified in the Constitution
Number of reserved constituencies decided by States

Articles 330 and 332 provide for reservation of seats for SCs and STs in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies respectively based on their population ratio. Originally meant for 10 years but extended periodically - now till 25 January 2030 by the 104th Amendment (2019).
The Speaker of the Lok Sabha is elected:
By the Lok Sabha from among its own members under Article 93
By members of both Houses jointly

Article 93 provides that the Lok Sabha shall choose two members to be Speaker and Deputy Speaker from among its own members. Usually the Speaker is from the ruling party/coalition and the Deputy from the opposition by convention.
Traffic in human beings, begar and similar forms of forced labour

Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings, begar (forced labour without payment) and other similar forms of forced labour, and makes these offences punishable by law. Also prohibits conscription for involuntary work except for public purposes.

73rd Amendment (1992): Panchayati Raj. Part IX (Articles 243-243O). Three-tier system: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zilla Parishad. Direct elections (5-year). SC/ST/OBC/women reservations. State Election Commission conducts elections.
A joint session of Parliament can be called by:

Joint session (Article 108): called by President. Held in Central Hall. Presided by Speaker of Lok Sabha. Convened for: ordinary bills deadlocked between houses, address by President. Used 4 times: Dowry Prohibition (1961), Banking Service Commission (1977), Prevention of Terrorism (2002), Land Acquisition (2015).
The Representation of the People Act, 1951 deals with:
Conduct of elections to Parliament and State Legislatures and qualifications/disqualifications of members

The Representation of the People Act, 1951 (RPA) is a comprehensive statute dealing with conduct of elections to Parliament and State Legislatures, qualifications and disqualifications for membership, corrupt practices, election disputes and electoral offences.
Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) were first used on a large scale in India during:

EVMs were first used experimentally in 1982 (Parur by-election, Kerala). After legal validation, large-scale use began in 1998 State elections. The 2004 Lok Sabha general elections were the first all-EVM general elections. EVMs were manufactured by BEL and ECIL.
The Fundamental Duties were added to the Constitution by:

Fundamental Duties: added by 42nd Amendment (1976, Indira Gandhi era, 'mini-Constitution'). Originally 10 duties, 11th added by 86th Amendment (2002). Article 51A, Part IVA. Inspired by USSR Constitution.
Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) is a device that:
Prints a slip visible to the voter for 7 seconds before falling into a sealed box, allowing audit verification
Acts as a substitute for the EVM

The Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail (VVPAT) is an independent verification printer attached to EVMs, manufactured by BEL and ECIL. When a voter casts a vote, the VVPAT prints a slip bearing the candidate's name.
Consider the following: 1. Introduced as the 122nd Amendment Bill 2. Created the GST Council 3. Came into force in 2017. This refers to:

The Constitutional (122nd Amendment) Bill, 2014 was passed by Parliament in 2016. After ratification by more than half the State Legislatures and Presidential assent, it was formally notified as the 101st Amendment, 2016. Came into force on 1 July 2017 with GST launch.
Article 324 of the Constitution vests the superintendence, direction and control of elections to:
Parliament, State Legislatures, President and Vice-President

Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections to Parliament, State Legislatures, the office of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission. Established on 25 January 1950 (now National Voters' Day).
The Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners are appointed by:
The President on the advice of a committee of PM, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and a Cabinet Minister (post-2023 law)

The CEC and Election Commissioners are appointed by the President. The CEC and Other Election Commissioners (Conditions of Service) Act, 1991 was amended in 2023 to mandate selection by a Committee of the PM.
A Chairman and four other members appointed by the President
Article 280(2) provides that the FC consists of a Chairman and four other members appointed by the President. The Chairman must be a person having experience in public affairs.
The Directive Principles of State Policy are:

Article 37 declares that Directive Principles in Part IV are not enforceable in any court. They are nevertheless fundamental in the governance of the country and it is the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.
The 12th Schedule of the Constitution, added by the 74th Amendment, contains:
Allocation of seats in Rajya Sabha

The 12th Schedule, inserted by the 74th Amendment, 1992, contains 18 functional items that may be transferred to Municipalities for implementation. These include urban planning, regulation of land use, roads and bridges, water supply, public health, sanitation, solid waste management.
The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) is appointed by:

CAG: appointed by President (Article 148). Guardian of public finances. Tenure: 6 years or 65 years. Removable like Supreme Court judge. CAG reports to President, laid before Parliament. Public Accounts Committee examines CAG reports. Current: K. Sanjay Murty (2025).
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is provided for under which Article?

Article 148 provides for the CAG, appointed by the President, who audits all receipts and expenditures of the Union and States. Holds office for 6 years or until 65 years, whichever is earlier; removable only like a SC Judge.
The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) was given constitutional status through the:
The 102nd Amendment, 2018 inserted Article 338B, granting constitutional status to the NCBC. It consists of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three other members appointed by the President.
The 'NOTA' (None Of The Above) option was introduced following a Supreme Court judgment in:
Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013)

In People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India (27 September 2013), the SC directed the Election Commission to introduce a 'None Of The Above' (NOTA) button on EVMs to allow voters to reject all candidates while maintaining secrecy.
The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to:

Article 75(3): Council of Ministers collectively responsible to Lok Sabha (lower house). If no-confidence motion passed against government, entire council must resign. Principle of collective responsibility - cornerstone of parliamentary democracy.
The Chief Justice of India is appointed by:

CJI appointed by President. Convention: senior-most judge of Supreme Court. Other judges: appointed by President on advice of CJI + 4 senior-most judges (Collegium system). Judges removable only by impeachment (Article 124).
Which amendment removed the Right to Property from the category of Fundamental Rights?

44th Amendment (1978) by the Janata Government deleted Article 31 and Article 19(1)(f) so Right to Property ceased to be a Fundamental Right. It was re-cast as a legal/constitutional right under new Article 300A.
The Governor of a State in India is appointed by:
The Chief Minister of the State

Article 155 provides that the Governor of a State shall be appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. The Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President (Article 156). Normally a term of 5 years, but no fixed tenure.
Right to Education as a Fundamental Right is provided under:

Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment, 2002, makes free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years. The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 operationalises this right.
Equality before law and equal protection of laws

Article 14 declares that 'the State shall not deny to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India'. Equality before law (British concept, Dicey) is negative; equal protection of laws (American concept) is positive.
Article 168 of the Constitution provides for:
Legislature of States (Vidhan Sabha and Vidhan Parishad)

Article 168 deals with the Constitution of Legislatures in States. For some States (Bihar, UP, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, J&K) the Legislature is bicameral - Assembly + Legislative Council. For other States it is unicameral - Assembly only.
The National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) consists of:
A Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three other Members

Under Article 338B inserted by the 102nd Amendment (2018), the NCBC consists of a Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three other Members, all nominated by the President. Their conditions of service and tenure are prescribed by the President.
The voting age for elections to Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies in India was reduced from 21 to 18 years by the:

The 61st Amendment, 1988 amended Article 326 to lower the voting age from 21 to 18 years for Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections. The first general elections with the new age were the 9th Lok Sabha elections held in November 1989.

Concurrent List (List III, originally 47 items, now 52 after GST): education (added by 42nd Amendment 1976), marriage, criminal law, bankruptcy, forests, economic planning, electricity. Both Centre and State can legislate; Centre prevails in case of conflict.
Which Fundamental Right was described by Dr. Ambedkar as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?

Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'heart and soul of the Constitution' because without an effective remedy, Fundamental Rights would be mere paper guarantees.
National Emergency under Article 352 has been imposed how many times in India?

Article 352 (National Emergency) imposed 3 times: 1962 (China war), 1971 (Indo-Pak war), 1975 (internal disturbance - controversial). 44th Amendment (1978) added safeguards: written recommendation of Cabinet, parliamentary approval within 1 month.
The maximum strength of Rajya Sabha is:

Rajya Sabha: max 250 (238 elected + 12 nominated by President). Currently 245 (233 elected + 12 nominated). Permanent house (1/3 retires every 2 years). Term: 6 years per member. Vice President is ex-officio Chairman.
The Chief Election Commissioner is appointed by:

CEC appointed by President. Election Commission (Article 324) - 3 members (1 CEC + 2 ECs) since 1989. Tenure: 6 years or until 65 years. Removed only by impeachment (like Supreme Court judge). First CEC: Sukumar Sen (1950).
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime was introduced by which amendment?

GST was introduced by the 101st Amendment, 2016 (originally introduced as the 122nd Amendment Bill, 2014, but renumbered after enactment). Inserted Article 246A and the GST Council under Article 279A. Subsumed indirect taxes like excise, service tax, VAT, CST. Launched on 1 July 2017.
The GST was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment?

101st Amendment (2016): introduced GST. Created GST Council (Article 279A). Concurrent powers of taxation (Article 246A). Integrated GST (IGST) for inter-state. GST launched 1 July 2017. Replaced multiple indirect taxes.
The writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 32 is:
Wider in scope than the High Court's under Article 226
Identical to the High Court's under Article 226
Narrower than the High Court's under Article 226
Article 32 empowers the SC to issue five writs - Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari and Quo Warranto - but only for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
The State Finance Commission is constituted under which Article?

Article 243I, inserted by the 73rd Amendment, 1992, requires the Governor of a State to constitute a State FC every five years to review the financial position of Panchayats and recommend: (a) distribution of taxes, duties, tolls etc.
The ordinance making power of President is in which Article?

Article 123: President's ordinance power. Promulgate when Parliament not in session. Same force as Act of Parliament. Must be approved within 6 weeks of Parliament reassembly. Maximum life: 6 months + 6 weeks. Governor's power: Article 213.
The superintendence, direction and control of elections to Panchayats and Municipalities is vested in:
The State Election Commission under Article 243K

Article 243K vests the superintendence, direction and control of preparation of electoral rolls and conduct of elections to Panchayats and Municipalities in the State EC, headed by the State Election Commissioner appointed by the Governor.
A No-Confidence Motion against the Council of Ministers under Article 75 can be moved:
Only in the Lok Sabha, with support of at least 50 members
In Lok Sabha without any minimum support

Article 75(3) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. A No-Confidence Motion can be moved only in the Lok Sabha (not in Rajya Sabha) and needs the support of at least 50 members to be admitted (Rule 198 of Lok Sabha).
Article 31C, which protects laws giving effect to certain DPSP from challenge on grounds of Fundamental Rights, was inserted by:

25th Amendment (1971) inserted Article 31C which initially shielded laws implementing Articles 39(b) and 39(c) from challenge under Articles 14, 19 and 31. The 42nd Amendment (1976) expanded it to all DPSP, but the expanded portion was struck down in Minerva Mills (1980).
The Anti-Defection Law was added through the:
52nd Amendment (1985), popularly the Anti-Defection Law, inserted the Tenth Schedule laying down grounds for disqualification of MPs and MLAs on grounds of defection.
Under the 74th Constitutional Amendment, three types of urban local bodies are mentioned:
Nagar Panchayat (transitional area), Municipal Council (smaller town), Municipal Corporation (larger urban area)
Gram Sabha, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad

Article 243Q of the 74th Amendment provides for three types of urban local bodies depending on the area: (1) Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area (from rural to urban); (2) Municipal Council for a smaller urban area; (3) Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area.
The concept of 'Concurrent List' in Indian Constitution is borrowed from:

Concurrent List borrowed from Australia. Has 52 items originally (now ~52). Subjects like education, marriage, forest, criminal law, economic planning. Both Centre and State can legislate; Centre prevails in conflict.
Panchayat Extension to Special Areas Act
Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996

The Provisions of the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996 (PESA) extends Part IX of the Constitution (Panchayats) to the Fifth Schedule Areas (tribal areas in 10 States: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra.
Public Interest Litigation (PIL) in India was pioneered by:
Justice P.N. Bhagwati and Justice V.R. Krishna Iyer

PIL concept: relaxed locus standi rule - any public-spirited person can file on behalf of disadvantaged. Hussainara Khatoon case (1979) - first PIL (undertrials' rights). SP Gupta case (1981) formalized. Made judiciary accessible to poor.
The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is provided for under which Article?

Article 350B, inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956, provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities. He is appointed by the President to investigate all matters relating to safeguards provided for linguistic minorities under the Constitution and report to the President.
Who is the ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha?

Vice President of India is ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Article 64). Not a member of either house but has casting vote in case of tie. Deputy Chairman elected from among members. Current VP: Jagdeep Dhankhar.
The discretionary powers of the Governor under the Constitution include:
Reserving Bills for President's consideration under Article 200; recommending President's Rule under Article 356

Article 163(1) provides for a Council of Ministers to aid and advise the Governor, except insofar as he is required to act in his discretion. Discretionary powers include: reserving Bills for President's consideration (Article 200); recommending President's Rule (Article 356); seeking info.
The maximum strength of Lok Sabha is:
Lok Sabha: max 552 members (530 states + 20 UTs + 2 Anglo-Indians). 104th Amendment (2020) abolished Anglo-Indian seats. Currently 543 elected members. Term: 5 years. First Lok Sabha: 1952.
The President of India is elected by an Electoral College consisting of:
Elected MPs of both Houses and elected MLAs of States and UTs (Delhi, Puducherry, J&K)

The President is elected under Article 54 by an Electoral College of elected MPs of both Houses of Parliament and elected MLAs of State Assemblies and the Assemblies of NCT of Delhi and UT of Puducherry (added by 70th Amendment, 1992; J&K after 2019 reorganization).
The Election Commission of India is established under which Article?

Article 324: ECI established. Superintendence, direction, control of elections to Parliament, State Legislature, President, Vice President. CEC + 2 Election Commissioners. T.N. Seshan (1990-96) revolutionized ECI's role.
Article 44 of the Constitution directs the State to:
Endeavour to secure a Uniform Civil Code for citizens

Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure for citizens a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) throughout India. It is a Directive Principle, not enforceable in courts. Codification of Hindu personal law began in the 1950s (Hindu Marriage Act 1955, Hindu Succession Act 1956).
The Attorney General of India is mentioned in which Article?

Article 76: Attorney General of India. First law officer of Government. Appointed by President. Must be qualified for Supreme Court judge. Has right of audience in all courts. Not a government servant. Can address Parliament but no vote.
The Supreme Court in Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) expanded the scope of:
Article 21 (Right to life and personal liberty)

In Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978), SC held that the right to travel abroad falls within Article 21, and any procedure depriving a person of life or liberty must be 'just, fair and reasonable'.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 is often described as the 'Mini-Constitution' because:
It was passed without parliamentary debate
It made widespread changes to the Preamble, Fundamental Rights, DPSP and emergency provisions

Enacted in 1976 during Emergency by the Indira Gandhi government. Added words 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' to the Preamble; added Fundamental Duties (Part IVA, Article 51A); curtailed judicial review; extended Lok Sabha/Assembly tenure to 6 years.
The Panchayati Raj system was given constitutional status through the:

The 73rd Amendment, 1992 (effective 24 April 1993) gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions by inserting Part IX (Articles 243 to 243O) and the 11th Schedule. It made three-tier Panchayati Raj (Gram, Block, Zila) mandatory in all States with population above 20 lakh.
The quorum required for a sitting of Lok Sabha is:
Quorum: 1/10 of total members (55 for Lok Sabha, 25 for Rajya Sabha). Without quorum, no business can be transacted. Speaker adjourns house or suspends meeting until quorum is met.
Which Article of the Constitution deals with Fundamental Rights?

Fundamental Rights: Articles 12-35 (Part III). Originally 7 rights, now 6 (Right to Property removed by 44th Amendment 1978, made legal right under Article 300A). 6 rights: Equality, Freedom, Against Exploitation, Religion, Cultural/Educational, Constitutional Remedies.
The 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) was provided by:

103rd Amendment (2019) amended Articles 15 and 16 to permit 10% reservation in education and public employment for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) of unreserved category. Upheld by SC in Janhit Abhiyan v. UoI (2022) by 3:2 majority, excluding EWS 'creamy layer'.
The ordinance-making power of the President is provided under:
Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session, if satisfied that circumstances exist requiring immediate action.
Which Schedule of the Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha to the States and UTs?

The Fourth Schedule deals with allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) to States and UTs (Article 80). Total 245 members: 233 elected by elected members of State Assemblies (and UTs with Legislatures) using single transferable vote; 12 nominated by the President for exce.
Under the Anti-Defection Law in the Tenth Schedule, disqualification of a member is decided by:
The High Court of the State
The Presiding Officer of the House (Speaker/Chairman)

The Tenth Schedule, inserted by the 52nd Amendment (1985), provides that the Speaker of Lok Sabha/State Assembly or the Chairman of Rajya Sabha/State Council decides on disqualification of a member on grounds of defection.
The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) can be removed from office:
By the President at any time
Only in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court (impeachment)

Article 148(1) provides that the CAG can be removed from office only in the manner provided for removal of a SC Judge under Article 124(4) - i.e. impeachment by Parliament on grounds of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
The Attorney General of India is provided for under which Article?

Article 76 provides for the AG (AG), the highest law officer in the country, appointed by the President. Must be qualified to be a Judge of the SC. The AG advises the Government of India on legal matters, performs duties conferred by the President.
The President of India possesses which of the following veto powers?

The President has three veto powers over Bills: (a) Absolute veto - directly refusing assent; (b) Suspensive veto - returning the Bill for reconsideration (becomes law if re-passed); (c) Pocket veto - neither assenting nor returning, keeping the Bill pending indefinitely.
Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution?

Drafting Committee: formed 29 Aug 1947, Chairman Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. Other members: Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau, T.T. Krishnamachari. Ambedkar = 'Father of Indian Constitution'.
Article 32 of the Constitution is associated with:

Article 32: 'Right to Constitutional Remedies' (heart and soul of Constitution - Ambedkar). Allows citizens to directly approach Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. 5 writs: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, Prohibition, Quo Warranto.
The residuary powers (subjects not in any list) under Indian Constitution are with:

Residuary powers (Article 248): with Union Parliament. Includes power to legislate on subjects not in Union List, State List, or Concurrent List. Different from USA (with states) - reflects strong Centre. Examples: Cyber law, AI regulation.
The impeachment process of the President under Article 61 can be initiated:
By either House of Parliament on ground of 'violation of the Constitution'
Only by the Council of Ministers

Article 61 provides that impeachment can be initiated by either House of Parliament for 'violation of the Constitution' (a quasi-judicial ground). Notice signed by at least 1/4th members of the House and 14 days' notice required.
EVMs (Electronic Voting Machines) were first used in India in:
EVMs first used: 1982 in 50 polling stations of Paravur by-election (Kerala). Developed by BEL/ECIL. VVPAT (Voter Verifiable Paper Audit Trail) added 2013 onwards. All-EVM elections: 2004 Lok Sabha.
Reservation for women in Panchayats is:

73rd Amendment (1992): at least 1/3rd (33%) reservation for women in Panchayats (including 1/3rd women Chairpersons). Many states (Bihar first in 2006) increased to 50%. SC/ST/OBC reservations also. ~14 lakh women elected representatives in PRIs.
The 'Basic Structure Doctrine' was propounded by the Supreme Court in:
Golak Nath v. State of Punjab (1967)
Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980)
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973)

In Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973), a 13-judge bench of SC by 7:6 majority held that Parliament can amend any part of the Constitution under Article 368, but cannot alter its 'basic structure'.
The Fundamental Duties in the Constitution were added by:

Fundamental Duties were added as Part IVA (Article 51A) by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee. Originally 10 duties; an eleventh (51A(k), duty of parent/guardian to provide education opportunities) was added by the 86th Amendment (2002).
The quorum required to hold a meeting of the Lok Sabha is:
One-tenth of the total number of members of the House

Article 100(3) provides that the quorum to constitute a meeting of either House of Parliament is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House. For Lok Sabha (543 members), quorum is 55; for Rajya Sabha (245 members), quorum is 25.
The Constituent Assembly of India was formed under which plan?

Constituent Assembly formed under Cabinet Mission Plan (1946). First meeting 9 Dec 1946. Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha (interim President), then Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected permanent President (11 Dec 1946).
Sikkim became a full-fledged State of the Indian Union through:

35th Amendment (1974) gave Sikkim the status of an 'Associate State' with a Regent. Following a 1975 referendum in which people voted overwhelmingly to join India, the 36th Amendment (1975) made Sikkim the 22nd State of the Indian Union and abolished the office of the Chogyal (monarch).
The three tiers of the Panchayati Raj system as mandated by the 73rd Amendment are:
Gram Panchayat at village level, Panchayat Samiti at block level, Zila Parishad at district level

The three-tier Panchayati Raj system, made mandatory for States with population above 20 lakh by Article 243B, comprises: (1) Gram Panchayat at the village level; (2) Panchayat Samiti at the block/intermediate level; (3) Zila Parishad at the district level.

Indian Constitution: federal in form, unitary in spirit. Features: written, rigid, supremacy, bicameral Parliament, independent judiciary (federal). Strong Centre: single Constitution, emergency provisions, single citizenship, Governor's appointment (unitary).
Which amendment clarified that amendments under Article 368 are not 'laws' under Article 13, but later subjected to the basic structure doctrine?

24th Amendment (1971) clarified that amendments under Article 368 are not 'laws' under Article 13, thus enabling Fundamental Rights amendments. In Kesavananda Bharati (1973), SC propounded the 'basic structure' doctrine limiting Parliament's amending power.
Which amendment made it mandatory for the President to act only on the written advice of the Council of Ministers?

42nd Amendment (1976) added the clause to Article 74(1) that the President shall act 'in accordance with such advice' of the Council of Ministers. The 44th Amendment (1978) added a safeguard permitting the President to require reconsideration once, but binding advice remains the rule.
A joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament can be called by the President under Article 108:
To resolve a deadlock over an Ordinary Bill (not Money/Constitutional Amendment Bill)

Article 108 permits the President to summon a joint sitting of both Houses to break a deadlock over an Ordinary Bill. Deadlock arises if: (a) the second House rejects the Bill; (b) the Houses disagree on amendments; or (c) six months elapse without the second House returning the Bill.
The Supreme Court of India was inaugurated on:

Supreme Court: inaugurated 28 January 1950 (replaced Federal Court). Originally 8 judges (including CJI), now 34 (Sanjeev Khanna CJI in 2025). Seat: New Delhi. Article 124-147. Originally Federal Court (1937-1950) at Delhi.
Article 48 of the Constitution directs the State to take steps to:
Prohibit the slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle

Article 48 directs the State to organise agriculture and animal husbandry on modern and scientific lines, and in particular to take steps for prohibiting slaughter of cows, calves and other milch and draught cattle, and to preserve and improve breeds.
The Electoral Bond Scheme, introduced in 2018, was struck down by the Supreme Court in:
Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India, 15 February 2024

In Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (15 February 2024), a five-judge Constitution Bench of the SC unanimously struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme and the related amendments to the Companies Act, Income Tax Act and Representation of the People Act as unconstitutional.

State List (List II, 61 items originally, now 62 after GST changes): police, public order, public health, sanitation, agriculture, local government, fisheries. States can legislate. Governor's assent needed. Centre cannot normally legislate on State List.
Article 44 of the Constitution deals with:

Article 44: 'State shall endeavor to secure Uniform Civil Code for citizens'. DPSP (non-justiciable). Supreme Court has repeatedly urged implementation. Goa has UCC-like code. Personal laws (Hindu, Muslim, Christian) currently separate.
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) was established in the year:
1993 (under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993)
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) of India was established on 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 (amended 2006 and 2019).
The strength of the Supreme Court of India (including the Chief Justice) is currently:

The strength of the SC was raised from 31 (1 CJI + 30) to 34 (1 CJI + 33) by the SC (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019. The sanctioned strength of 34 came into effect in September 2019. The original strength (1950) was 8 (1 CJI + 7).
The pardoning power of the President under Article 72 includes:
Pardon, reprieve, respite, remit and commute sentences

Article 72 empowers the President to grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment, or to suspend, remit or commute the sentence of any person convicted of an offence in cases where punishment is by court-martial, relates to Union executive power.
Judicial Review in India is based on:

Article 13: pre-Constitution laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights are void. Basis of Judicial Review (Marbury v. Madison concept from US). Article 32 (writs), 131, 132, 133, 134, 136, 143 also relate. Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) established Basic Structure Doctrine.
The 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011 is related to:

97th Amendment (2011) inserted Part IXB (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT) on Cooperative Societies, making them autonomous and democratic. SC in Rajendra N. Thakur (2021) struck down portions on Multi-State Cooperative Societies as beyond Parliament's competence.
The minimum age to contest for President of India is:

President: minimum 35 years, qualified for Lok Sabha, no office of profit. Elected by Electoral College (elected MPs + MLAs). Term: 5 years. Eligible for re-election. First: Rajendra Prasad. Current (2025): Droupadi Murmu (15th President).
A judge of the Supreme Court retires at the age of:

Article 124(2) provides that a Judge of the SC retires at 65 years. A High Court judge retires at 62 (Article 217). A SC judge can be removed only by impeachment (Article 124(4)) on grounds of 'proved misbehaviour or incapacity' by a majority of each House and 2/3rd of members present and .
The Gram Sabha as per Article 243(b) consists of:
All persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of a Panchayat
Only elected members of Gram Panchayat

Article 243(b) defines the Gram Sabha as a body consisting of all persons registered in the electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level. It is the only unit of direct democracy in the constitutional scheme.
The Finance Commission of India is constituted by the President under:
Article 280, every fifth year or earlier

Article 280 mandates the President to constitute a FC every five years or earlier. The Commission recommends: (i) distribution of net proceeds of taxes between Union and States and allocation among States (Article 270); (ii) principles governing grants-in-aid from Consolidated Fund of Indi.
The Zonal Councils were established under:

Zonal Councils are statutory bodies established under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956 (Part III). India is divided into 5 zones: Northern, Central, Eastern, Western, Southern (later, North-Eastern Council under separate 1971 Act).
The National Commission for Women (NCW) was established in the year:
1992 as a statutory body under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990

The National Commission for Women (NCW) is a statutory body established in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990. It consists of a Chairperson, five members and a Member-Secretary, all nominated by the Central Government.

7 continents (traditional): Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia. Asia largest (44.5 million sq km). Africa 2nd (30 million). Australia smallest (8.6 million). Some models: 6 (combining Americas or Europe-Asia). Zeelandia (submerged, near New Zealand): debated 8th continent.
Sanchi Stupa is in which state?

Sanchi Stupa (MP): ~46 km NE of Bhopal. Built by Ashoka (3rd century BCE). Great Stupa (expanded by Shungas). 4 toranas (gateways) with carvings. UNESCO World Heritage (1989). Discovered 1818 by General Taylor. Restored by John Marshall (1912-1919).

Thimphu: capital of Bhutan. Population ~1.2 lakh. World's only capital without traffic lights. Located at 2300m altitude. Tashichho Dzong (seat of government). Paro: international airport (dangerous approach). Bhutan: only carbon-negative country, measures Gross National Happiness.

Sahara: largest hot desert in world (~9.2 million sq km). Covers 11 North African countries: Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, W. Sahara, Sudan, Tunisia. Largest cold desert: Antarctica. Sahara expanding south (desertification).

Mahabalipuram (Mamallapuram, Tamil Nadu): 7th-8th century Pallava dynasty. Shore Temple (~700 CE, Narasimhavarman II). Pancha Rathas (5 chariots). Arjuna's Penance (largest bas-relief in world). UNESCO World Heritage (1984). Asian trading port.
Gangotri, Yamunotri, Kedarnath, Badrinath are collectively called:

Char Dham: 4 sacred Hindu pilgrimage sites in Uttarakhand Himalayas. Adi Shankaracharya established (~8th century). Yamunotri (Yamuna source), Gangotri (Ganga source), Kedarnath (Shiva, Jyotirlinga), Badrinath (Vishnu). Open May-November (snow blocks otherwise).
The Khyber Pass connects India/Pakistan with:

Khyber Pass: historic trade route through Hindu Kush mountains. Connects Peshawar (Pakistan) with Kabul (Afghanistan). ~53 km long. Used by invaders (Alexander, Mughals, Afghans). Silk Road route. British fought Afghan wars.

Hampi (Karnataka): ruins of Vijayanagara Empire capital (1336-1565). UNESCO World Heritage (1986). Tungabhadra river. Sites: Virupaksha Temple, Vittala Temple (stone chariot), Lotus Mahal, Hazara Rama Temple, Mahanavami Dibba. Virupaksha still active.

Panama Canal (1914): ~82 km long. Connects Atlantic (via Caribbean) to Pacific. Saves ~13,000 km vs Cape Horn (South America). Locks lift ships 26m to Gatun Lake. USA built (1904-14, after French failure). Returned to Panama 1999. Expanded 2016 (new locks for bigger ships).
Which is the longest river in India?

Ganga: 2525 km long. Originates at Gangotri glacier (Gomukh) in Uttarakhand. Joins Bay of Bengal at Ganga Sagar (Sundarbans). Main tributaries: Yamuna, Gomti, Ghaghra, Gandak, Kosi, Son. World's 34th longest river.

Sri Jayawardenepura Kotte: legislative capital of Sri Lanka (since 1982, parliament). Suburb of Colombo. Colombo: commercial capital (still has President's House, Supreme Court, ministries). Kandy: hill capital (last Sinhalese kingdom, Temple of Tooth).
Tropical cyclones in India mainly affect which region?

Tropical cyclones: form over warm Bay of Bengal (April-May + Oct-Nov). Hit eastern coast: TN, AP, Odisha, WB. Major cyclones: Phailin (2013), Hudhud (2014), Fani (2019), Amphan (2020), Yaas (2021), Asani (2022). NDRF, IMD's INCOIS provide early warnings.
Mawsynram receives the highest rainfall in the world. It is in:

Mawsynram (Meghalaya): receives ~11,871 mm rainfall annually - highest in world. Replaced Cherrapunji (now 2nd). SW monsoon winds hit Khasi Hills, cause heavy orographic rainfall. Living root bridges (made from Ficus elastica roots).
The Suez Canal connects which two water bodies?
Gulf of Aden and Persian Gulf

Suez Canal (Egypt): 193 km long, opened 1869. Connects Port Said (Mediterranean) to Suez (Red Sea). Reduces Europe-Asia distance by ~7000 km vs Cape of Good Hope. Nationalized by Nasser in 1956 → Suez Crisis.

Ganga origin: Gangotri glacier (Gomukh, Uttarakhand), 4000m altitude. Official source: ice cave at Gomukh. Length: 2525 km. Joins Bay of Bengal at Ganga Sagar (Sundarbans). Main tributaries: Yamuna, Gomti, Ghaghra, Gandak, Kosi, Son.
Which is the highest waterfall in India?

Kunchikal Falls: 455 m (1493 ft) - highest in India. Located in Shimoga district, Karnataka, on Varahi river. After construction of Varahi dam, reduced flow. Jog Falls (253 m, Karnataka) is second highest, on Sharavathi river.
Kaziranga National Park is famous for:

Kaziranga NP (Assam): ~430 sq km. UNESCO World Heritage Site (1985). Two-thirds of world's one-horned rhinos (~2600). Also has tigers (highest density), elephants, wild buffaloes. Flooded annually by Brahmaputra.
Southwest monsoon in India arrives first in:

Southwest Monsoon: arrives Kerala ~1 June (IMD forecast). Branches: Arabian Sea (Mumbai by 10 June), Bay of Bengal (NE India + Bengal). Progresses north, reaches Delhi by 30 June. Withdrawal starts 1 September (NW India). Ends October-November.
Mount Aconcagua is in which country?

Aconcagua: highest peak outside Asia (6961m). Located in Andes, Argentina (near Chile border). Highest peak in Southern + Western Hemispheres. Part of Andes range (longest continental mountain range, ~7000 km). Climbed 1897 (Matthias Zurbriggen).
Indian climate is described as which type?

India: 'Tropical Monsoon Climate' (Köppen Am/Aw). Most of India in tropical zone (north of Tropic of Cancer: subtropical; south: tropical). Monsoon defines seasons: Winter (Dec-Feb), Summer (Mar-May), SW Monsoon (Jun-Sep), Retreating Monsoon (Oct-Nov).
The Thar Desert is located mainly in which state?

Thar Desert (Great Indian Desert): ~200,000 sq km. Mostly in Rajasthan (60%), extends to Gujarat, Punjab, Haryana. Aravalli range east. Luni river. Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Jodhpur are major desert cities. Camels, sand dunes.
Greenland is an autonomous territory of:

Greenland: largest island in world (~2.16 million sq km, excluding Australia). Autonomous territory of Denmark since 1979. Capital: Nuuk. ~80% ice-covered. Population ~57,000 (mostly Inuit). Self-rule 2009. Strategic + mineral resources (rare earths, uranium). Trump tried to buy 2019.
Aizawl: capital of Mizoram (since 1987 statehood). Located ~1132m altitude. Largest city + cultural center of Mizoram. Tropic of Cancer passes through Mizoram. Mizos majority. State Day: 20 February.
Capital of Kazakhstan was renamed in 2019. New name:

Astana (renamed Nur-Sultan 2019, after Nazarbayev; renamed back to Astana September 2022). Capital of Kazakhstan since 1997 (moved from Almaty - earthquake risk + near China). Planned city. Bayterek tower. Population ~12 lakh. Cold winters (-35°C).
Mount Fujiyama is in which country?

Mount Fuji (Fujiyama, Fuji-san): highest mountain in Japan (3776m). Active volcano (last eruption 1707, Hoei). 100 km SW of Tokyo. Three sacred mountains of Japan (with Tate + Haku). UNESCO World Heritage (2013). Climbing season: July-August. ~3 lakh climbers/year.

Gujarat: largest cotton producer (~30% of India). Major districts: Rajkot, Surendranagar, Ahmedabad, Amreli. India: 2nd largest cotton producer (after China), largest cotton grower by area. Bt cotton (GM, 2002): revolutionized. Cotton Corporation of India procures.
Which is the largest state of India by area?

Rajasthan: 342,239 sq km - largest state by area (10.4% of India). MP: 2nd (308,252). Maharashtra: 3rd (307,713). Smallest state: Goa (3,702). Largest UT: Ladakh (59,146, after J&K reorganization 2019). Rajasthan borders Pakistan.
Which river is called 'Sorrow of Bihar'?

Kosi: 'Sorrow of Bihar'. Frequent flooding + course changes. Originates in Tibet (Sankalu), flows through Nepal, enters Bihar. 'River of sorrow' due to shifting course (120 km in last 250 years). Kosi barrage at Bhimnagar (Nepal). Kosi embankment project.
Bombay High offshore oil fields are located in:

Bombay High: India's largest offshore oil field (~176 km NW of Mumbai). Discovered 1974 by ONGC (Oil + Natural Gas Corporation). Production started 1976. Contributes ~50% of India's domestic crude oil production. Sagar Samrat platform (1980s).
The Aravalli range is located mainly in which state?

Aravalli range: ~692 km, oldest fold mountains in India. Runs NE-SW across Rajasthan (Guru Shikhar 1722m, Mt Abu). Continuing erosion makes them low relief. Delhi ridge (northernmost extension). Separates Thar desert from fertile plains.
Western disturbances cause rainfall in which region during winter?

Western disturbances: extra-tropical cyclones from Mediterranean. Travel east via Westerlies. Bring winter rain to NW India (Dec-Feb). Crucial for rabi crops (wheat). Cause snowfall in Himalayas. ~3-4 disturbances per month during winter.
Capital of Indonesia was moved to:

Jakarta: current capital of Indonesia. Sinking + overcrowded (~1 crore). Plans to move capital to Nusantara (East Kalimantan, Borneo) - construction started 2022, target 2024 partial move. Population ~3 lakh planned. Reason: Jakarta sinking (10cm/year in places), floods.
Indian summer (Hot weather season) lasts from:

Summer: March-May. Temperature: 32-45°C (north), 30-35°C (south). Loo winds in northern plains. Dust storms (aandhi). Hottest: Jaisalmer, Bikaner (Rajasthan), Delhi. Pre-monsoon showers: mango showers (Kerala-Karnataka), Kalbaisakhi (Bengal).
Loo is a hot dry wind that blows in which region during summer?

Loo: hot dry wind in northern plains (April-June). Temperature 45-50°C. Strong afternoon winds. Dangerous - can cause heatstroke. Reduces at sunset. Common in Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, UP, Bihar. Dust storms (aandhi) sometimes accompany.
Mango showers (or coffee showers) occur in which region?

Mango showers (mango rainfall, April-May): pre-monsoon showers in Kerala + Karnataka. Help ripen mangoes + coffee berries. Locally called 'mango showers' or 'blossom showers'. Important for mango crop. Early arrival signals monsoon.
The world's largest river delta is:

Sundarbans Delta (Ganges-Brahmaputra-Meghna): world's largest delta (~80,000 sq km). Spans India-Bangladesh. Famous for Sundari trees, Royal Bengal Tigers, mangroves. UNESCO World Heritage. Vulnerable to climate change, sea level rise. ~40% in India, 60% in Bangladesh.
Which state is the largest producer of coal in India?

Top coal producers: Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand. India has 4th largest coal reserves (after US, Russia, China, Australia). Major coal fields: Jharia (Jharkhand - oldest), Raniganj (WB), Bokaro, Korba (Chhattisgarh), Talcher (Odisha).

Ottawa: capital of Canada (Ontario province). Population ~10 lakh. Located on Ottawa River. Parliament Hill. Toronto: largest city + financial hub. Montreal: largest French-speaking city outside France. Vancouver: Pacific coast. Bilingual country (English + French).
Antarctica is governed by which treaty?

Antarctic Treaty (1 December 1959, Washington, effective 23 June 1961): governs Antarctica. Demilitarized, no nuclear waste, scientific cooperation, no sovereignty claims recognized. India joined 1983. 54 parties (2024). Headquarters: Buenos Aires. Secretariat established 2004.
Brahmaputra is known by which name in Tibet?

Brahmaputra: known as Yarlung Tsangpo in Tibet. Enters India through Arunachal Pradesh (Dihang). Flows SW through Assam valley (Brahmaputra). Joins Padma in Bangladesh, becomes Meghna, then Ganga-Brahmaputra-Meghna (GBM) delta.

Tokyo: capital of Japan. World's largest metropolitan area (~3.7 crore population). Tokyo Imperial Palace. Tokyo Tower, Tokyo Skytree (634m). 1964 + 2020 Olympics. Earlier capital: Kyoto (794-1868). Edo renamed Tokyo (1868, Meiji Restoration).
The October Heat in India is caused by:

October Heat: high temperature + humidity in October-November. Caused by retreating monsoon. Cloud-free sky → high insolation. High humidity from Bay of Bengal. Worst in northern plains (Delhi, UP, Bihar). Relief comes with winter monsoon (NE).
The Deccan Plateau is bounded by which rivers?

Deccan Plateau: ~5 lakh sq km, triangular plateau. Bounded by Narmada-Tapi rivers (north, Satpura range), Krishna-Tungabhadra (south), Western Ghats (west), Eastern Ghats (east). Formed by volcanic basalt lava flows (Cretaceous-Eocene).
The Southwest Monsoon in India arrives first at:

SW Monsoon: arrives Kerala around 1 June (declared by IMD). Splits into Arabian Sea branch (Mumbai by 10 June) and Bay of Bengal branch (moves north-east). Reaches Delhi by 30 June, entire country by 15 July. Withdrawal starts September.

Angel Falls (Venezuela): highest waterfall in world (979m, 15x Niagara). Located on Auyán-tepui (table mountain) in Canaima National Park. UNESCO World Heritage. Named after Jimmy Angel (American aviator, discovered 1933). Pemon name: Kerepakupai Merú. Drops into Kukenán river.
Which is the largest producer of rice in India?
West Bengal: largest rice producer (~15% of India's output). Other major: UP, Punjab, Andhra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu. India is world's 2nd largest rice producer (after China), largest exporter.
Which is the largest state in India by area?

Rajasthan: 342,239 sq km - largest state by area (10.4% of India). MP second (308,252), Maharashtra third (307,713). Smallest state: Goa (3,702). Largest UT: Ladakh (59,146, after J&K reorganization 2019).
The Himalayas extend approximately how many kilometers in India?

Himalayas: ~2400 km from Indus (west) to Brahmaputra (east). Width varies 150-400 km. Three parallel ranges: Himadri (Greater), Himachal (Lesser), Shivalik (Outer). Highest peak: Mt Everest (8849m). India's highest: Kanchenjunga (8586m).
India's longest coastline is in which state?

Gujarat: ~1600 km coastline (longest in India). Total Indian coastline: 7516.6 km (mainland + islands). Other long coastlines: Andhra Pradesh (~974 km), Tamil Nadu (~906 km), Maharashtra (~652 km), Kerala (~569 km).
The Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through which state?

Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram. Does NOT pass through: Odisha, Maharashtra, Andhra, etc. India lies mostly north of Equator, in Northern Hemisphere.

Dhaka: capital of Bangladesh. Population ~2.3 crore (metro, world's most densely populated city). Buriganga river. Founded 17th century (Mughal). Jute + textile industries. Traffic congestion severe. 1971: capital of independent Bangladesh (after Liberation War).
Amazon River flows through which country mainly?

Amazon River: ~6400 km (longest or 2nd after Nile, disputed). Origin: Andes (Peru, ~5000m). Flows east across Brazil to Atlantic. Largest drainage basin (~7 million sq km). Amazon rainforest: 'lungs of Earth', ~5.5 million sq km, ~10% of world's biodiversity.
Which is the largest river delta in India?

Sundarbans Delta (Ganga-Brahmaputra): largest in India, world's largest (80,000+ sq km, including Bangladesh). Spans India-Bangladesh. Famous for Royal Bengal Tigers, mangroves, Sundari trees. UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Nile (~6650 km): traditionally considered longest. Amazon (~6400 km): disputed, some Brazilian scientists claim longer. Flows north through 11 African countries. Egypt's lifeline. Aswan High Dam (1970) controls floods. Source: Lake Victoria (debated).
Which is the highest peak of the Karakoram range?

K2 (8611m): 2nd highest peak in world after Everest. Located in Karakoram range, on China-Pakistan border (Gilgit-Baltistan, PoK). 'Savage Mountain' due to difficulty. First climbed 1954 by Italian expedition (Achille Compagnoni, Lino Lacedelli). K2 is in Pakistani-administered Kashmir.
Capital of Myanmar was moved in 2005 to:

Naypyidaw: capital of Myanmar since 6 November 2005 (military junta moved from Yangon). Located in central Myanmar. Population ~9 lakh (mostly government employees). Ghost city - low population density. Wide 20-lane roads. Reason for move unclear (astrology, defense).
Which is the highest peak of the Himalayan range in India?

Kanchenjunga (8586m): 3rd highest peak in world. Located on Sikkim-Nepal border. India's highest peak (K2 in PoK is higher but disputed). Sacred to Sikkimese. First climbed 1955 by Joe Brown + George Band. Kanchenjunga National Park UNESCO site.
Ajmer Sharif Dargah is dedicated to:

Ajmer Sharif (Dargah Sharif): in Ajmer, Rajasthan. Tomb of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti (1141-1236, Sufi saint, founder of Chishti Order in India). Built by Mughal Emperor Humayun. Annual Urs (death anniversary): 6 days. Pilgrimage site for all religions.
Which country has the most time zones?

France: most time zones (12, including overseas territories like French Polynesia, New Caledonia, Réunion, Guadeloupe, etc.). Russia: 11 (consecutive). USA: 11 (with territories). China: 1 (Beijing time, despite spanning 5 geographical zones). India: 1 (IST, UTC+5:30).
The Caspian Sea is the largest:

Caspian Sea: largest lake (enclosed body of water) - 371,000 sq km. Surrounded by 5 countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan. Saline water. Largest sturgeon fishery (caviar). Rich in oil, gas.
Which is the most populous state of India?

Uttar Pradesh: ~24 crore population (most populous, ~17% of India). Maharashtra: 2nd (~12.5 crore). Bihar: 3rd. Total India: ~144 crore (2024, world's most populous, surpassing China). UP sends 80 MPs to Lok Sabha (highest).
Gulf of Aden and Persian Gulf

Suez Canal (Egypt): 193 km long, opened 17 November 1869. Connects Port Said (Mediterranean) to Suez (Red Sea). Reduces Europe-Asia distance ~7000 km (vs Cape of Good Hope). Nationalized 1956 by Nasser → Suez Crisis. Ever Given got stuck 2021 (blocked canal 6 days).
Vaishno Devi shrine is in which state/UT?

Vaishno Devi (Katra, Jammu & Kashmir): dedicated to Vaishno Devi (Mother Goddess, Mahalakshmi/Mahakali/Mahasaraswati). Pilgrimage ~13 km trek from Katra base. ~1 crore pilgrims annually. Shri Mata Vaishno Devi Shrine Board (SMVDSB) manages.
Most populous country without a river is:

Saudi Arabia: largest country without a permanent river. Wadis (dry riverbeds) fill temporarily after rains. Wadi al-Rummah (longest, ~1200 km, mostly dry). Wadi as-Sirhan. Desalination provides drinking water (world's largest producer). No lakes either. Aquifers being depleted.

Malé: capital of Maldives. One of world's most densely populated cities (~2 lakh in 9 sq km). At sea level - vulnerable to climate change. Velana International Airport (Hulhule island, nearby). Artificial island Hulhumalé being built to reduce overcrowding.

South Africa has 3 capitals: Pretoria (executive, government), Cape Town (legislative, Parliament), Bloemfontein (judicial, Supreme Court). Unique arrangement. Johannesburg: largest city (financial center). Cape Town: legislative + tourist destination (Table Mountain).
Hussain Sagar Lake connects which two cities?

Hussain Sagar: artificial lake built 1562 by Ibrahim Quli Qutb Shah. Connects Hyderabad + Secunderabad (Twin Cities). Buddha statue (18m, 1992) on Gibraltar Rock in middle. Built on River Musi tributary. Bund (dam) was heart of city's water supply.

Riyadh: capital of Saudi Arabia. Population ~75 lakh. Financial + political center. King Khalid International Airport. Jeddah: 2nd largest, Red Sea port, gateway to Mecca. Mecca + Medina: holy cities (Islam). Hajj pilgrimage. Vision 2030: NEOM megacity, tourism push.

Kabul: capital of Afghanistan. Population ~50 lakh (largest city). Located in eastern Afghanistan, Hindu Kush mountains. Kabul river. 3500+ years old. Major trade route (Silk Road). Taliban recaptured 15 August 2021 (after US withdrawal).
The Indo-Gangetic Plain is formed by sediments from which rivers?

Indo-Gangetic Plain: ~3.75 lakh sq km, formed by alluvial deposits of Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra river systems. Fertile, densely populated. Three sections: Punjab Plain (Indus), Ganga Plain, Brahmaputra Plain (Assam). World's most extensive alluvial tract.
The retreating monsoon causes cyclones in which region?

Retreating Monsoon (Oct-Nov): SW monsoon withdraws, NE monsoon picks up moisture from Bay of Bengal. Causes heavy rainfall + cyclones on eastern coast (TN, Andhra, Odisha). Tropical cyclones: Phailin (2013), Hudhud (2014), Fani (2019).

Kunchikal Falls (455m): highest waterfall in India. Located in Shimoga district, Karnataka, on Varahi river. Reduced flow after Varahi dam construction. Jog Falls (253m, Karnataka, on Sharavathi river): second highest, more famous.
Highest tea-producing state in India is:

Assam: largest tea producer (~50% of India's output). Famous for Assam tea (CTC method). Major tea districts: Dibrugarh, Tinsukia, Sivasagar. India: 2nd largest tea producer (after China), largest tea exporter. Darjeeling tea (WB): famous, GI tag.

Strait of Malacca: ~800 km long, between Malay Peninsula (Malaysia) and Indonesian island of Sumatra. Connects South China Sea (Pacific) to Andaman Sea (Indian Ocean). One of world's busiest shipping lanes (especially oil). Piracy concerns. Singapore at southern end.

Cairo: capital of Egypt. Population ~2.2 crore (largest in Arab world). Nile river. Pyramids of Giza nearby (last surviving ancient wonder). Sphinx. Egyptian Museum (Tutankhamun's treasures). Al-Azhar University (970 CE, oldest). Tahrir Square.
Madagascar is separated from Africa by which channel?

Madagascar: 4th largest island in world (~587,000 sq km). Located off SE African coast. Mozambique Channel (400 km wide) separates from mainland Africa. Biodiversity hotspot: lemurs, baobab trees, 90% endemic species. Gondwana remnant. Capital: Antananarivo. French + Malagasy speaking.
Which Indian state has the longest coastline?

Gujarat: longest coastline (~1600 km, 1/3rd of India's). India's total coastline: 7516.6 km (mainland + islands). Other long coastlines: Andhra (974), Tamil Nadu (906), Maharashtra (652), Kerala (569).

Raipur: capital of Chhattisgarh (since 2000 statehood, separated from MP). Largest city. New planned capital: Naya Raipur (Atal Nagar, renamed 2018). Chhattisgarh State Day: 1 November. Tribal population ~30%. Rice bowl of central India.

Bering Strait: separates Russia (Chukotka) from USA (Alaska). ~85 km wide at narrowest. International Date Line passes through Diomede Islands (Big = Russia, Little = USA). Once joined Asia-America (Bering land bridge during Ice Age - first humans crossed).

Strait of Gibraltar: separates Spain (Europe) from Morocco (Africa). ~13 km wide at narrowest. Connects Mediterranean Sea to Atlantic Ocean. Rock of Gibraltar (British territory). Pillars of Hercules (ancient name).Ceuta + Melilla (Spanish territories in Africa).
The world's largest river by discharge volume is:

Amazon River: largest by discharge (~209,000 m³/s, 20% of world's river discharge). 2nd longest (~6400 km, after Nile). Drainage basin: ~7 million sq km (largest). Flows through 9 South American countries. Amazon rainforest: 'lungs of Earth'.
Which river is called 'Sorrow of Bengal'?

Damodar: 'Sorrow of Bengal' (frequent flooding, ravaging Bengal). Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC, 1948): first multipurpose river valley project of independent India (modeled on Tennessee Valley Authority). Dams: Tilaiya, Konar, Maithon, Panchet.

Odisha: largest iron ore producer (~50% of India). Major mines: Keonjhar, Sundargarh. India: ~25 billion tonnes iron ore reserves (5th globally). Bellary-Hospet (Karnataka): major. Bailadila (Chhattisgarh): high-grade. NMDC, Tata Steel, SAIL major producers.

Antarctica: largest desert (cold desert, ~14 million sq km). Sahara: largest hot desert (~9.2 million sq km). Antarctica receives <200 mm precipitation/year. Covered by ice (~98% area). Continent without native population or sovereign states.

Chilika Lake (Odisha): largest brackish water lagoon in Asia (~1165 sq km). Ramsar site (1981, India's first). Famous for Irrawaddy dolphins (endangered), migratory birds. Connected to Bay of Bengal. Nalabana bird sanctuary inside. Threatened by siltation.
Horn of Africa includes which countries?

Horn of Africa: easternmost part of Africa. Includes: Somalia, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Djibouti (sometimes Kenya). ~2 million sq km. Strategic location (Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Indian Ocean). Frequent droughts, conflicts. Bab-el-Mandeb strait nearby (Red Sea entry).
Which is the most populous state in India?

Uttar Pradesh: ~24 crore population (most populous). Maharashtra second (~12.5 crore), Bihar third. Smallest population: Sikkim (~7 lakh). Total India population: ~144 crore (2024, world's most populous).
Mount Vesuvius is famous for destroying which city in 79 CE?

Mount Vesuvius (Italy): erupted 24 August 79 CE. Buried Pompeii + Herculaneum (Roman cities) under volcanic ash. ~2000-3000 killed. Pliny the Younger described eruption (Plinian eruption type). Still active + dangerous (last eruption 1944). Vesuvius Observatory (1841, world's oldest volcano observatory).

Islamabad: capital of Pakistan since 1960 (replaced Karachi). Planned city (Greek firm Doxiadis). Population ~11 lakh. Margalla Hills nearby. Faisal Mosque (largest in South Asia, 1986). Diplomatic enclave. Adjacent to Rawalpindi (military HQ).
Sun Temple at Konark is in which state?

Konark Sun Temple (Odisha): built 1250 CE by King Narasimhadeva I (Eastern Ganga dynasty). Designed as chariot of Sun God (Surya) - 12 pairs of wheels, 7 horses. UNESCO World Heritage (1984). Magnet legend destroyed idol + temple (legend, unverified).

Lakshadweep: UT in Arabian Sea. Smallest UT by area (32 sq km), 36 islands, only 10 inhabited. Capital: Kavaratti. Coral atolls. Predominantly Muslim population (Malayalam-speaking). Earlier Laccadive, Minicoy, Amindivi.

Lake Baikal (Russia): deepest lake in world (1642m). Oldest (~25-30 million years). Largest freshwater by volume (~20% of world's unfrozen freshwater). ~1700 species (2/3 endemic). UNESCO World Heritage. Biodiversity: nerpa (only freshwater seal), omul fish. ~636 km long.

Amarnath cave (J&K): dedicated to Lord Shiva. Famous for natural ice stalagmite (Shiva lingam), forms + waxes with moon. Annual pilgrimage (July-August, Shravan month). Located ~3888m altitude. Managed by Shri Amarnath Shrine Board (SASB).
The highest peak of Western Ghats is:

Anamudi (2695 m): highest peak of Western Ghats, in Eravikulam National Park, Kerala. Also called 'Everest of South India'. Means 'elephant's forehead'. Endangered Nilgiri Tahr habitat. South of Palghat Gap.

Buenos Aires: capital of Argentina. 'Paris of South America' (European architecture). Tango birthplace. Population ~30 lakh (metro ~1.5 crore). Río de la Plata (river). Football: Boca Juniors, River Plate. Pope Francis born here (1936).

Gobi Desert: ~1.3 million sq km, in northern China + southern Mongolia. Largest desert in Asia. Cold desert (snow in winter, -40°C). 5th largest desert. Trade route: Silk Road. Famous dinosaur fossil finds. Expanding due to desertification (China planting 'Green Wall').

Moscow: capital of Russia (since 1918). Population ~1.3 crore. Kremlin, Red Square, Saint Basil's Cathedral. Largest city in Europe. Saint Petersburg: 2nd largest, former capital (1712-1918, Peter the Great founded). Trans-Siberian Railway ends at Vladivostok.

Top coal producers (2023-24): Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand. India: 2nd largest coal producer (after China), 4th largest reserves. Major coal fields: Jharia (Jharkhand - oldest, burning for ~100 years), Raniganj (WB), Korba (Chhattisgarh), Talcher (Odisha).
Black soil is most suitable for cultivation of:

Black soil (Regur): dark color, high water retention, suitable for cotton ('black cotton soil'). Found in Deccan Plateau (Maharashtra, Gujarat, MP, Telangana). Also good for sugarcane, tobacco, jawar, pulses. Expands when wet, contracts when dry (self-plowing).
