The Equator passes through which continent?

Equator (0° latitude): passes through 13 countries across 3 continents - Africa (Gabon, Congo, DR Congo, Uganda, Kenya, Somalia, São Tomé), South America (Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil), Asia (Indonesia, Maldives).

West Bengal: largest rice producer (~15% of India's output). India: 2nd largest rice producer (after China), largest rice exporter. Major rice states: WB, UP, Punjab, AP, Telangana. Paddy cultivation: Kharif crop (Jun-Oct), some Rabi (boro rice).

Uttar Pradesh: largest wheat producer (~30% of India). India: 2nd largest wheat producer (after China). Major wheat states: UP, Punjab, MP, Haryana. Wheat: rabi crop (sown Oct-Dec, harvested Mar-Apr). Major varieties: HD-2967, PBW-343, Shatabdi.
The highest tea-producing state in India is:
Assam: largest tea producer (~50% of India's output). Famous for Assam tea (CTC). Other major: WB (Darjeeling, Dooars), Tamil Nadu (Nilgiris), Kerala. India = 2nd largest tea producer (after China).
The Andaman and Nicobar Islands are located in:

Andaman & Nicobar: UT in Bay of Bengal. 572 islands, ~38 inhabited. Port Blair (capital). Northern Andamans closer to Myanmar (190 km) than to Chennai (1190 km). Indira Point (Pygmalion Point) - southernmost point of India.
The smallest continent in area is:

Australia: smallest continent (~7.69 million sq km). Often called 'island continent'. Includes mainland Australia + Tasmania + smaller islands. Country + continent. Surrounding Indian Ocean (west), Pacific (east), Southern Ocean (south). Capital: Canberra.
Which strait separates India from Sri Lanka?

Palk Strait: ~53-80 km wide. Separates Tamil Nadu (India) from northern Sri Lanka. Adam's Bridge (Rama Setu): chain of limestone shoals, ~48 km, mostly submerged. Hindutva belief: built by Lord Rama's army. Sethusamudram project controversy.

Canberra: capital of Australia. Planned city (1913). Population ~4.5 lakh. Located between Sydney + Melbourne (rivalry resolved by capital between them). Lake Burley Griffin (artificial). Parliament House, Old Parliament House, National Gallery. Sydney: largest city.
Siachen Glacier is in which region?

Siachen Glacier: ~76 km long, in eastern Karakoram, Ladakh. Highest battlefield in world (~5400-7700m altitude). India controls since Operation Meghdoot (1984). Pakistan claims. Disputed. Highest battlefield casualties due to extreme cold + altitude. ~$1 million/day cost.
Sambhar Lake is famous for production of:

Sambhar Lake (Rajasthan): largest inland salt lake in India (~230 sq km). Salt production since ancient times. Sambhar Salts Limited (Hindustan Salts subsidiary). Wetland of international importance (Ramsar). Migratory birds: flamingos. Located ~80 km SW of Jaipur.
Sahyadri is another name for which mountain range?

Western Ghats (Sahyadri): ~1600 km long. Runs parallel to western coast (Gujarat-Tamil Nadu). UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012). Older than Himalayas. Source of major rivers: Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Tungabhadra. Highest: Anamudi (2695m).

Uttar Pradesh: largest sugarcane producer (~40% of India). Major districts: Meerut, Saharanpur, Bareilly, Lakhimpur Kheri. India: 2nd largest sugarcane producer (after Brazil). Sugar industry: largest agro-based industry in UP. Western UP is sugarcane belt.
The largest iron ore producing state in India is:

Odisha: largest iron ore producer (~50% of India). India has ~25 billion tonnes of iron ore reserves (5th globally). Major mines: Keonjhar, Sundargarh (Odisha), Bellary-Hospet (Karnataka), Bailadila (Chhattisgarh).
The Cape of Good Hope is located in:

Cape of Good Hope: southern tip of Africa (South Africa). Mistakenly thought to be southernmost point of Africa (actual: Cape Agulhas, ~150 km SE). Discovered 1488 by Bartolomeu Dias. Important before Suez Canal (Europe-Asia route).
The Amazon River flows through which continent?

Amazon: largest river by discharge, second longest (after Nile, debatable). Originates in Andes (Peru), flows east across South America to Atlantic. ~6400 km. Drains Amazon rainforest (largest, ~5.5 million sq km, 'lungs of Earth').
Mount McKinley (Denali) is in which country?

Denali (Mount McKinley): highest peak in North America (6190m). Located in Denali NP, Alaska (USA). Renamed 2015 (from McKinley back to Denali - Athabaskan name meaning 'high one'). 3rd most prominent peak in world (after Everest + Aconcagua). K2: 2nd prominent.
Cape of Good Hope is at the southern tip of:

Cape of Good Hope: southern tip of Africa (South Africa, ~50 km south of Cape Town). Often mistaken as Africa's southernmost point (actual: Cape Agulhas, ~150 km SE). Discovered 1488 by Bartolomeu Dias. Important before Suez Canal (Europe-Asia route).
Russia-Ukraine war started in which year (current phase)?

Russia invaded Ukraine 24 February 2022 (after 2014 Crimea annexation). Largest European war since WWII. India maintained neutral stance, purchased Russian oil at discount. NATO expanded (Finland 2023, Sweden 2024). Sanctions on Russia. UN General Assembly resolutions condemned.
Digboi oil refinery is in which state?

Digboi (Assam): India's oldest oil refinery (1901). 'Dig, boy, dig' - folklore origin of name. Discovered 1867 (first oil well). Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) operates. Assam Oil Company (established 1899) merged with IOC. Heritage refinery.
Most populous country in the world (2024) is:

India: most populous country (~144 crore, 2024). Surpassed China in 2023 (UN estimate). China: ~141 crore (declining, low birth rate). USA: ~33.5 crore. India: 17.7% of world population. Median age ~28 years (demographic dividend phase). UN projects peak ~170 crore around 2064.
Neyveli Lignite is mined in which state?

Neyveli (Tamil Nadu): largest lignite (brown coal) mines in India. NLC India Limited (formerly Neyveli Lignite Corporation, founded 1956). Lignite-fired thermal power plants. Lignite: low-grade coal, ~30-50% moisture. Mine: 1956. Major source for Tamil Nadu power.
Khajuraho temples are in which state?

Khajuraho (MP): group of Hindu + Jain temples (~25 survive of 85). Built 950-1050 CE by Chandela dynasty. Famous for erotic sculptures + nagara architecture. UNESCO World Heritage (1986). Light + Sound show. Western, Eastern, Southern groups.
The 'Ring of Fire' is associated with:

Ring of Fire: horseshoe-shaped belt around Pacific Ocean. ~75% of world's active volcanoes, ~90% of earthquakes. Subduction zones: Pacific plate diving under surrounding plates. Countries: Japan, Philippines, Indonesia, Chile, Peru, USA (west coast).
Mariana Trench is in which ocean?

Mariana Trench: deepest part of world's oceans (~10,984m at Challenger Deep). Located in western Pacific, east of Mariana Islands. Formed by subduction. Trieste (1960): first manned descent (Jacques Piccard + Don Walsh). James Cameron solo dive 2012. Victor Vescovo: deepest 2019.
Largest coffee-producing state in India is:

Karnataka: largest coffee producer (~70% of India). Mainly: Chikmagalur, Hassan, Coorg. Two varieties: Arabica + Robusta. India produces ~3-4 lakh tonnes coffee/year. Baba Budan brought coffee seeds to India (~1600 CE). Indian coffee: shade-grown, premium.
Which is the longest river that flows entirely within India?

Godavari: 1465 km, longest river entirely within India (Ganga flows through Bangladesh). Originates at Trimbakeshwar (Maharashtra), flows to Bay of Bengal. Also called 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Vridha Ganga'. Drains 10 states, basin ~3 lakh sq km.

Beijing: capital of China. Population ~2.2 crore. Forbidden City (Ming + Qing palaces), Great Wall access (Badaling). Tiananmen Square. 2008 Summer Olympics. 2022 Winter Olympics (first dual-Olympic city). Shanghai: largest city, financial hub.

Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD): 'Indian Niño'. Difference in SST between western (Arabian Sea) + eastern (Bay of Bengal/Indonesia) Indian Ocean. Positive IOD (warmer west): stronger monsoon. Negative IOD: weaker monsoon. Discovered by Saji et al. 1999.
Which is the highest peak of the Western Ghats?

Anamudi (2695m): highest peak of Western Ghats + South India. Located in Eravikulam NP, Kerala. 'Everest of South India'. Endangered Nilgiri Tahr habitat. South of Palghat Gap. Western Ghats UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012).
Tirupati temple is in which state?

Tirupati (Tirumala Venkateswara Temple): in Andhra Pradesh (Tirumala hills). Dedicated to Lord Venkateswara (Vishnu). Richest temple in world. ~3-5 crore pilgrims/year. Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) manages. On top of 7 hills (Seshachalam). Hundi offerings.
Kilimanjaro: highest mountain in Africa (5895 m, Uhuru Peak). Located in Tanzania. Dormant volcano. Highest free-standing mountain in world. Decreasing glaciers due to climate change.
Mount Elbrus is in which country?

Mount Elbrus: highest peak in Europe (5642m). Located in Caucasus Mountains, Russia (near Georgia border). Dormant volcano. Twin summits (West + East). Highest peak of Caucasus. 7 Summits (highest of each continent): Everest, Aconcagua, Denali, Kilimanjaro, Elbrus, Vinson, Puncak Jaya (Kosciuszko debated).
The Vindhya range separates which two regions?

Vindhya range: traditional boundary between North India (Aryavarta) + South India (Dakshinapatha). Runs east-west ~1050 km across MP, UP, Bihar. Average elevation 300-650m. Narmada flows along southern foot. Amarkantak is highest point.
The longest mountain range in the world is:

Andes: longest continental mountain range (~7000 km, South America, Venezuela to Chile). Highest peak: Aconcagua (6961m, Argentina). Himalayas: highest mountain range. Rockies (North America, ~4800 km). Alps (~1200 km, Europe).
India has how many states + Union Territories (as of 2024)?

India (2024): 28 states + 8 UTs. Changes: J&K reorganization (Oct 2019): J&K state → 2 UTs (J&K + Ladakh). Dadra & Nagar Haveli + Daman & Diu merger (Jan 2020): 1 UT. States: 28 (after Telangana 2014, last state added). UTs: Delhi, Puducherry, J&K (have assemblies), Chandigarh, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, A&N, DNH&DD.
The longest river of South India is:

Godavari: 1465 km - longest river in South India. Also called 'Dakshin Ganga' or 'Vridha Ganga'. Origin: Trimbakeshwar (Maharashtra). Flows through Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha. Drains 10 states. Basin ~3.1 lakh sq km.
Cape Horn is the southernmost point of:

Cape Horn: southernmost point of South America (Chile). 56°S latitude. Tierra del Fuego archipelago. Infamous for treacherous waters (Drake Passage). Before Panama Canal, ships rounded Cape Horn. Now mostly used by sailboats + adventurous cruises.

Kathmandu: capital of Nepal. Population ~15 lakh (valley ~50 lakh). Located in Kathmandu Valley (UNESCO World Heritage - 7 monuments). Pokhara: tourist city (lakes, Annapurna views). Bhaktapur + Lalitpur: nearby historical cities. Mt Everest (8849m) in Nepal.
World's largest coral reef system is:

Great Barrier Reef: world's largest coral reef system (~2300 km, ~900 islands). Off Queensland coast, Australia. Coral Sea. Visible from space. UNESCO World Heritage (1981). Threatened by climate change, coral bleaching (2016, 2017, 2020, 2022 mass bleachings). ~1500 fish species.
Mawsynram in Meghalaya is known for:

Mawsynram (Meghalaya): receives ~11,871 mm rainfall annually - highest in world. Replaced Cherrapunji (now second). In East Khasi Hills. SW monsoon winds hit Khasi Hills, cause heavy orographic rainfall.
Loktak Lake is famous for which unique feature?

Loktak Lake (Manipur): largest freshwater lake in NE India. Famous for phumdis (floating islands of vegetation, soil, organic matter). Keibul Lamjao NP (only floating NP) on phumdis - habitat of endangered Sangai (brow-antlered deer). Ramsar site.
Srinagar is situated on the banks of which river?

Srinagar (summer capital of J&K): on banks of Jhelum (Vitasta). Dal Lake, Nishat Bagh, Shalimar Bagh. Jhelum flows through Kashmir Valley. One of 5 Punjab rivers (Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Sutlej) - all Indus tributaries.
Capital of Turkey was moved in 1923 to:

Ankara: capital of Turkey since 1923 (Mustafa Kemal Atatürk moved from Istanbul). Central Anatolia, safer + more Turkish. Population ~50 lakh (Turkey's 2nd largest). Istanbul: largest city, historical Byzantium/Constantinople (Ottoman capital 1453-1922).

Golden Temple (Sri Harmandir Sahib): in Amritsar, Punjab. Built 1588-1604 by 5th Sikh Guru Arjan Dev. Gold plating added by Maharaja Ranjit Singh (early 19th century). Holiest shrine of Sikhism. Open to all (4 doors). Akal Takht (highest Sikh seat) adjacent.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through how many Indian states?

Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through 8 Indian states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram. India lies mostly in Northern Hemisphere, tropics + subtropics.
Gir National Park is famous for:

Gir NP (Gujarat, Junagadh): only place outside Africa with wild lions (Asiatic, ~670). ~1412 sq km. Maldharis (pastoralists) co-exist with wildlife. Successful conservation - lions increased from ~180 (1974) to 670+ (2020).
Northeast monsoon brings rainfall to which Indian region?

NE monsoon (Retreating monsoon, Oct-Dec): picks up moisture from Bay of Bengal. Brings rain to TN coast (60% of TN rainfall), parts of AP, Kerala. Tamil Nadu's main rainy season. Cyclones in Bay of Bengal also bring rain.
El Niño effect on Indian monsoon:

El Niño (warm phase ENSO): warming of eastern Pacific. Correlates with weaker Indian SW monsoon → drought. La Niña (cold phase): stronger monsoon. IMD monitors Pacific for monsoon forecast. Significant El Niño years: 2002, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2015.
Winter season in India lasts from:

Winter: December-February. Cold, dry (NE monsoon). Temperature: 10-15°C (north), 20-25°C (south). Western disturbances bring rain to NW India. Snowfall in Himalayas. Coldest: Dras (Ladakh, -60°C). Winter crops: wheat, barley, mustard, gram (rabi).
Which state is the largest producer of wheat in India?
Uttar Pradesh: largest wheat producer (~30%). Other major: Punjab, MP, Haryana. India is 2nd largest wheat producer (after China). Wheat is rabi crop (sown Oct-Dec, harvested Mar-Apr).
Which is India's only active volcano?

Barren Island (Andaman & Nicobar): India's only active volcano. First recorded eruption 1787. Last erupted 2022. Located ~135 km NE of Port Blair. 354m high. Submarine type. Narcondam: dormant, nearby. Both in Andaman Sea.
Kanchenjunga, the third highest mountain in the world, is located in:

Kanchenjunga (8586 m): 3rd highest peak in world (after Everest 8849m, K2 8611m). Located at Sikkim-Nepal border. Sacred to Sikkimese. India's highest peak (since K2 is in PoK). First climbed 1955 by Joe Brown + George Band.
The Western Ghats are also known as:

Western Ghats (Sahyadri): ~1600 km long, runs parallel to western coast (Gujarat to Tamil Nadu). UNESCO World Heritage Site (2012). Older than Himalayas. High biodiversity - Western Ghats hotspot. Major rivers originate: Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri.
World's largest lake by area is:

Caspian Sea: largest lake in world (371,000 sq km). Saline. Largest enclosed body of water. Surrounded by 5 countries: Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran, Azerbaijan. Status: sea or lake (legal disputes). Rich in sturgeon (caviar), oil, gas. Russia + Iran opposed to divide among 5.
The Sahara Desert is located in:

Sahara: largest hot desert in world (~9.2 million sq km). Covers 11 North African countries (Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, W. Sahara, Sudan, Tunisia). Largest cold desert: Antarctica.

Naypyidaw: capital of Myanmar since 6 November 2005 (military junta moved from Yangon). Located in central Myanmar, ~320 km north of Yangon. Population ~9 lakh (mostly government employees). Ghost city - low density. Wide 20-lane roads. Reason for move unclear (astrology, defense, centralization).
Pacific Ring of Fire is associated with:

Pacific Ring of Fire: ~40,000 km horseshoe-shaped belt. ~75% of world's active volcanoes + ~90% of earthquakes. Subduction zones around Pacific plate. Countries: Japan, Philippines, Indonesia, Chile, Peru, USA (west coast), Mexico, Russia (Kamchatka).
Largest country in the world by area is:

Russia: largest country (1.71 crore sq km, 11% of world's landmass). Spans 11 time zones (Kaliningrad to Chukotka). Capital: Moscow. 2nd: Canada (99.8 lakh sq km). 3rd: China (97 lakh sq km). 4th: USA (98.3 lakh sq km). India: 7th (32.9 lakh sq km).
Pangong Tso lake is located in:

Pangong Tso: endorheic lake at 4350m altitude, Ladakh. 134 km long, 60% in China (Tibet), 40% in India. Saltwater. Featured in '3 Idiots' film. Disputed between India + China (extends across Line of Actual Control). Freezes completely in winter.
Tropic of Cancer does NOT pass through:

Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N) passes through 8 states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, MP, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura, Mizoram. Does NOT pass through Maharashtra (south of Tropic). Mahabaleshwar (~17.9°N) is south of Tropic.
The Great Barrier Reef is located in:

Great Barrier Reef: world's largest coral reef system (~2300 km). Off Queensland coast, Australia. UNESCO World Heritage Site (1981). Threatened by climate change, coral bleaching. Visible from space.
Silent Valley National Park is located in:

Silent Valley NP (Kerala, Palakkad district): tropical rainforest, ~90 sq km. Saved from hydroelectric project (1980s, environmental movement). Famous for Lion-tailed Macaque. UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
Bodh Gaya is sacred to which religion?

Bodh Gaya (Bihar): Buddha attained enlightenment (~528 BCE, age 35) under Bodhi tree (Ficus religiosa). Mahabodhi Temple (5th-6th century CE, rebuilt). UNESCO World Heritage (2002). Buddhist pilgrimage site - one of 4 main Buddhist sites (others: Lumbini, Sarnath, Kushinagar).
Kalbaisakhi is a violent storm in which region?

Kalbaisakhi (Nor'wester): violent thunderstorm in Bengal + Assam during summer (April-May). Causes heavy rain, hail, strong winds. Brings relief from heat. Localized storms. Sometimes cause damage to crops + property. Named from Bengali 'kal' (time) + 'baisakh' (month).
Kudremukh iron ore mines are located in:

Kudremukh (Karnataka): known for iron ore mines (KIOCL - Kudremukh Iron Ore Company). 'Kudre' = horse, 'mukh' = face (mountain resembles horse face). UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves. Mining stopped 2005 (environmental concerns, NP status).
Which strait separates Asia from North America?

Bering Strait: separates Russia (Chukotka) from Alaska (USA). ~85 km wide. Diomede Islands (Big = Russia, Little = USA) in middle. International Date Line passes between. Once joined Asia-America (Bering land bridge during Ice Age).
Mount St. Helens is in which country?

Mount St. Helens (USA, Washington state): erupted 18 May 1980. 57 killed. Earthquake-triggered landslide + lateral blast (rare). Reduced elevation from 2950m to 2550m. Most destructive volcanic event in US history. Active stratovolcano. Cascade Range. Part of Pacific Ring of Fire.
Mount Kilimanjaro is in which country?

Kilimanjaro: highest mountain in Africa (5895m, Uhuru Peak). Located in Tanzania. Dormant volcano. Highest free-standing mountain in world. Three volcanic cones: Kibo, Mawenzi, Shira. Decreasing glaciers due to climate change. Popular climbing destination (~7-day trek).
Sabarimala temple is in which state?

Sabarimala (Kerala): dedicated to Lord Ayyappa. Pilgrimage season: mid-November to mid-January (Mandala Makaravilakku). Men + women of menstruating age traditionally restricted (controversial, SC allowed entry 2018). 41-day vrata (penance) required. ~5 crore pilgrims annually.

Indira Point (Pygmalion Point): southernmost point of India. Located in Great Nicobar Island (Andaman & Nicobar). Renamed 1984 (after Indira Gandhi visit). 6°45'N latitude. Submerged partially after 2004 tsunami (1.5m subsidence). Lighthouse damaged.

Seoul: capital of South Korea. Population ~1 crore (metro ~2.5 crore). 1988 Summer Olympics, 2002 FIFA World Cup. Han River. Gyeongbokgung Palace (Joseon dynasty). K-pop, K-drama hub. Gangnam district. Incheon International Airport. Border with North Korea (DMZ 50km north).
Capital of Brazil was moved from Rio de Janeiro to:

Brasília: capital of Brazil since 21 April 1960. Planned city (Lucio Costa + Oscar Niemeyer). Built in 41 months. UNESCO World Heritage. Located in interior (central Brazil). Reduced coastal concentration. Federal District. Population ~30 lakh.
Which is the largest freshwater lake in India?

Wular Lake (Jammu & Kashmir): largest freshwater lake in India. ~30 sq km (varies seasonally). Formed by tectonic activity. River Jhelum flows through. Threatened by willow plantations + pollution. Ramsar site. Vembanad (Kerala): longest lake (96 km).
Strait of Hormuz connects which water bodies?
Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman (Indian Ocean)

Strait of Hormuz: ~33 km wide. Connects Persian Gulf (north) to Gulf of Oman + Arabian Sea (south). Critical for oil shipments (~20% of world's oil passes). Iran on north, Oman/UAE on south. Tanker wars (Iran-Iraq war 1980s). Strategic importance.
Atacama Desert is in which continent?

Atacama Desert (Chile): driest non-polar desert in world. Some areas no rain for centuries. Pacific coast (west of Andes). Rich in copper + nitrates. Astronomical observatories (clear skies): ESO's Paranal, ALMA. ~1000 km long (north-south).
Sundarbans is the natural habitat of:

Sundarbans: mangrove forests at Ganga-Brahmaputra delta (India-Bangladesh). Home to Royal Bengal Tigers (~100 in Indian Sundarbans). Tigers swim, eat fish, crabs. UNESCO World Heritage (1987). Threatened by climate change, sea-level rise.
Which country has the longest coastline?

Canada: longest coastline (~2.02 lakh km). Includes mainland + 36,000+ islands. Country with most lakes (~2 million, 60% of world's lakes). 2nd: Norway (~58,000 km, fjords). 3rd: Indonesia (~54,000 km, archipelago). India: 19th (~7,517 km).
Köppen climate classification for most of India is:

India: mostly Köppen Aw (tropical savanna) + Am (tropical monsoon). NW India: BWh/BSh (arid, desert/steppe). Himalayas: Dfb/Cfb (humid continental). NE India: Cfa/Cwa. Köppen system: based on temperature + precipitation patterns.
Smallest Union Territory of India by area is:

Lakshadweep: smallest UT (32 sq km). 36 islands (only 10 inhabited). Capital: Kavaratti. Coral atolls. Predominantly Muslim (Malayalam-speaking). Earlier name: Laccadive, Minicoy, Amindivi. Arabian Sea.

El Niño (warm phase of ENSO - El Niño Southern Oscillation): warming of eastern Pacific Ocean. Correlates with weaker Indian SW monsoon (drought years). La Niña (cold phase) brings heavier monsoon. IMD monitors Pacific for monsoon forecast.
Pradhan Mantri Gramin Digital Saksharta Abhiyan (PMGDISHA) is for:

PMGDISHA (August 2017): digital literacy in rural India. Target: 6 crore rural households (1 person per household). Training: 20 hours. Course: computer basics, internet, digital payments, government apps. ~6 crore certified (2024). Implemented by CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. Goal: digitally empower rural India.
Real GDP growth rate is calculated using:

Real GDP: calculated at constant prices (using base year prices, removes inflation effect). India's base year: 2011-12 (revision to 2017-18 under consideration). Nominal growth = real growth + inflation. Real GDP growth: ~6-8% (India), ~5% (China), ~2% (USA).
Aadhaar, UPI, and DBT together helped India save how much in leakages as per government claims?

Government claims ~₹3.5 lakh crore saved through DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) using Aadhaar-linked payment. Reduced ghost beneficiaries in MGNREGA, LPG subsidy, PDS. World Bank praised JAM trinity (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile).
FRBM Act (Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management) was passed in:

FRBM Act 2003 (effective 2004): fiscal discipline. Targets: fiscal deficit 3% of GDP, debt 60% (Centre) + 40% (states) by 2024-25 (extended). NK Singh Committee (2016): recommended debt-to-GDP ratio 60% by 2022-23, fiscal deficit 2.5% (later revised).
Wholesale Price Index (WPI) in India is published by:
Office of Economic Adviser (Ministry of Commerce)

WPI: published by Office of Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce + Industry. Base year: 2011-12 (revised from 2004-05). 697 items (manufacturing 64%, primary 22%, fuel 14%). Released monthly. Excludes services. Used for inflation adjustment in contracts, wages.
Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched in:

PMGSY (25 December 2000, Vajpayee): rural roads. Goal: connect all habitations with population 500+ (250+ in hills, tribal, desert). ~7 lakh km roads constructed (2024). Cost: ~₹2 lakh crore. 1.6+ lakh habitations connected. PMGSY-II: consolidate (50,000 km). PMGSY-III (2019): focus on routes connecting markets + hospitals.
MSP (Minimum Support Price) is announced for how many crops?

MSP: 23 crops + FRP (Fair and Remunerative Price) for sugarcane = 24. Crops: 7 cereals (paddy, wheat, jowar, bajra, maize, ragi, barley), 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds, 4 commercial crops. C2+50% formula (Swaminathan). CACP recommends.
Digital service delivery points in rural areas

CSCs (2006, earlier; expanded 2014): access points for digital services in rural areas. Run by Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs). ~5 lakh CSCs (2024). Services: Aadhaar, PAN, banking, insurance, telemedicine, e-education, digital payments, e-stamps. CSC e-Governance Services India Ltd. manages.
GST has how many tax slabs currently?

GST slabs: 0% (essential), 5% (mass consumption), 12%, 18% (most goods), 28% (luxury, sin goods like tobacco). Special: 0.25% (rough precious stones), 3% (gold, jewelry). Compensation cess on 28% items (sin + tobacco + luxury + cars) for states' revenue loss.
Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority (IRDAI) was established in:

IRDAI: established 1999 (IRDA Act). HQ Hyderabad. Chairman: Debasish Panda (2025). Regulates insurance industry (life + general + health). Insurance penetration: ~4% (vs world ~7%). FDI limit: 74% (raised from 49% in 2021). LIC: largest life insurer. IPO 2022.
International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched in:

ISA (30 November 2015, COP21, Paris): launched by PM Modi + French President Hollande. HQ: Gurugram, India (first treaty-based international org in India). 120+ member countries (solar-rich between Tropics of Cancer + Capricorn). 7th General Assembly September 2024 (New Delhi). President: India.
Aadhaar was launched as a 12-digit unique identity number in:

Aadhaar: launched 28 January 2009 (UIDAI formed). 12-digit unique identity number. First Aadhaar: 29 September 2010 (Ranjana Sonawane, Maharashtra). Nandan Nilekani first Chairman. Now world's largest biometric ID system (>135 crore).

India forex reserves (October 2024): $704.9 billion (record). 4th largest after China (~$3.3 trillion), Japan (~$1.2 trillion), Switzerland (~$0.9 trillion). Components: FCA, gold, SDR, IMF reserve tranche. Provides ~12 months import cover, supports rupee stability.
PM-KISAN scheme provides income support of how much to farmers?

PM-KISAN (24 Feb 2019): income support ₹6000/year to small + marginal farmer families (up to 2 hectares land). Paid in 3 installments of ₹2000. Direct benefit transfer (DBT) to bank accounts. ~8 crore beneficiaries.
RBI's inflation target under flexible inflation targeting is:
RBI Monetary Policy Framework (2016): target 4% CPI inflation, range 2-6%. Reviewed every 5 years. Monetary Policy Committee (MPC, 6 members) decides rates. Repo rate adjusted to control inflation.

SDR: international reserve asset created by IMF (1969). Not a currency, but potential claim on freely usable currencies of IMF members. Value: basket of USD (43%), EUR (29%), RMB (12%), JPY (7%), GBP (7%). India has SDR ~12.5 billion (part of forex reserves).
Open Market Operations (OMO) by RBI involve:

OMO: RBI buys/sells govt securities (G-Secs) in open market. Buy → injects liquidity, sell → absorbs. Used for liquidity management. G-Sec: tradable govt debt (Treasury bills short-term, dated securities long-term). RBI conducts OMO through auctions.
National Solar Mission (Jawaharlal Nehru NSM) was launched in:

NSM (11 January 2010): originally 20 GW solar by 2022. Revised (June 2015): 100 GW by 2022 (60 GW utility, 40 GW rooftop). Achieved ~64 GW (2023, missed). Components: large solar parks (Bhadla - world's largest, 2245 MW), rooftop (40 GW target), off-grid. India: 5th largest solar capacity globally. Targets: 500 GW non-fossil by 2030.
Per capita income of India (2023-24) is approximately:

India per capita income (2023-24): ~₹2.1 lakh (~$2,500-2,800). Low compared to developed (USA $70,000+, Japan $40,000). World Bank classifies India as 'lower-middle income'. Target: developed country by 2047 (per capita ~$18,000). Currently ~$2,500-3,000.
Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya) was launched to:
Provide electricity connection to all households

Saubhagya (11 September 2017): universal household electrification. Free connection for BPL households. ₹500 in instalments for APL. Earlier DDUGJY (Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana, 2014 - rural feeder separation). 2.8 crore connections. 100% village electrification: 28 April 2018 (Leisang village, Manipur). Household electrification: ~100% (some gaps).
AMRUT (Atal Mission for Rejuvenation + Urban Transformation) is for:

AMRUT (25 June 2015, replaced JNNURM): urban infrastructure. Components: water supply, sewerage + septage, drainage, green spaces, urban transport. 500 cities (with population 1 lakh+). AMRUT 2.0 (1 November 2021): ₹2.87 lakh crore, focus on universal water supply, sewage. 'Pey Jal Sevek' app.
Ayushman Bharat - PMJAY provides health cover up to:

PM-JAY (PM Jan Arogya Yojana, launched 23 Sep 2018): world's largest government-funded health insurance. ₹5 lakh per family per year. Covers 10.74 crore families (bottom 40% population). Free secondary + tertiary care. Cashless at empanelled hospitals.
Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) was launched in:

DBT (1 January 2013, Gaya, Bihar): direct transfer of subsidies/benefits to beneficiary bank accounts (using Aadhaar). ~310 schemes (Centre + State). ~₹38 lakh crore transferred (cumulative, 2024). Saved ~₹3.5 lakh crore (govt estimate) by removing ghost beneficiaries. PAHAL (LPG subsidy), MGNREGA payment.
Priority Sector Lending (PSL) target for banks is:

PSL: 40% of ANBC (for domestic + foreign banks with 20+ branches). Sub-targets: Agriculture 18% (within: small/marginal farmers 10%), Micro enterprises 7.5%, Weaker sections 12%, SCs/STs ~7.5%. Categories: agriculture, MSMEs, export credit, education, housing, social infrastructure, renewable energy, weaker sections.
Agriculture contributes approximately what percentage to India's GDP?

Agriculture: ~18% of GDP (2023-24). Employs ~46% of workforce. Major contributor: agriculture, forestry, fishing. Allied sectors growing faster. Services: ~53% GDP, ~30% workforce. Industry: ~29% GDP.
Repo rate is the rate at which:

Repo Rate: RBI lends to commercial banks against government securities. Current (Dec 2024): 6.5%. Reverse Repo: banks lend to RBI. MSF (Marginal Standing Facility): banks borrow overnight from RBI. Repo + 0.25% = MSF.
National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 aims to increase GER in higher education to:

NEP 2020 (29 July 2020, replaces 1986 NEP): increases Higher Education GER target to 50% by 2035 (current ~28%). 5+3+3+4 structure. Multi-disciplinary, multiple exit options. Mother tongue as medium till Class 5. PhD changes.

JAM Trinity: Jan Dhan Yojana (bank accounts) + Aadhaar (biometric identity) + Mobile (telecom). Enables DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer). Saved ~₹3.5 lakh crore (govt estimate) by removing ghost beneficiaries. World Bank praised. Used in: LPG subsidy, MGNREGA payment, food distribution (PDS), pensions, scholarships.
National Infrastructure Pipeline (NIP) was launched with target of:

NIP (31 December 2019): ₹111 lakh crore infrastructure investment (2020-25). ~6,845 projects. Sectors: roads (39%), energy (24%), urban (16%), railways (12%). 70% govt (Centre+State), 30% private. Task Force headed by Atanu Chakraborty. PM Gati Shakti (2021) integrates + expands NIP. Mid-term review: ~₹80 lakh crore spent (2024).

PM Vishwakarma Yojana (PM-VIKAS, 17 Sep 2023, Vishwakarma Jayanti): traditional artisans/craftspeople (18 trades - carpenter, mason, blacksmith, goldsmith, potter, etc.). Recognition, collateral-free loan ₹1+2 lakh, 5% interest subvention, skill training, toolkit, digital empowerment. ~5 crore beneficiaries target.
National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency (NMEEE) was launched under:
National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC, 2008)

NMEEE (2008, under NAPCC): 4 initiatives - 1) PAT (Perform Achieve Trade, energy efficiency in industry), 2) MTEE (Market Transformation for Energy Efficiency), 3) EEFP (Energy Efficiency Financing Platform), 4) FEED (Framework for Energy Efficient Economic Development). BEE implements.
The 'Make in India' initiative was launched on:

Make in India: launched 25 September 2014 by PM Modi. Goal: transform India into global manufacturing hub. 25 sectors (auto, textiles, defense, electronics, etc.). Target: 25% GDP from manufacturing (currently ~17%). 'Zero Defect, Zero Effect'.

Gini coefficient: 0-1 (or 0-100). 0 = perfect equality, 1 = perfect inequality. India: ~35-47 (varies by source). South Africa: ~63 (highest). Brazil: ~53. USA: ~39. Scandinavian countries: ~25-28 (lowest). India less unequal than Brazil but more than Europe.
The MUDRA Yojana provides loans up to:

PM Mudra Yojana (8 April 2015): loans to micro/small businesses (non-corporate, non-farm). Three categories: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001-5 lakh), Tarun (₹5-10 lakh). No collateral. PM Jan Dhan Yojana (2014) preceded.
Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY) aims for:

PMKSY (29 June 2015): 'Per drop more crop'. Components: AIBP (Aaccelerated Irrigation Benefit Programme - large projects), Har Khet Ko Pani (water to every farm), Watershed Development, Micro Irrigation (drip + sprinkler). ~10 million hectares micro-irrigated. Subsidy 55% (Centre 45%, State 10%).

RNBC: type of NBFC. Accepts public deposits (regulated by RBI). Major: Peerless General Finance (closed in 2016, transferred to bank). Sahara India Financial Corporation. RBI tightened rules post-Sahara scam. New RNBC licenses not granted since 1990s.
Banking Ombudsman scheme was launched by RBI in:

Banking Ombudsman: launched 1995 (RBI). Resolves customer complaints vs banks (free service). 22 Ombudsman offices (centres). Awards up to ₹20 lakh (compensation + ₹1 lakh for harassment). Online: RBI Complaint Management System. Integrated Ombudsman Scheme 2021 - one portal, one email, one app.
Startup India Seed Fund Scheme provides:
Financial assistance for proof of concept

SISFS (April 2021-Jan 2026): financial assistance up to ₹50 lakh for proof of concept, prototype development, product trials, market entry. SIDBI manages. ₹1000 crore corpus. For DPIIT-recognized startups. Eligibility: <2 years old, <50 lakh turnover. Incubators as implementing partners.
India's largest trading partner in 2023-24 was:

USA: India's largest trading partner 2023-24 (~$118 billion). 2nd: China (~$118 billion). UAE, Russia, Saudi Arabia other major. India's total trade: ~$1.1 trillion (2023-24). Trade deficit with China: ~$85 billion.
National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG) is registered as:

NMCG: registered 12 August 2011 under Societies Registration Act 1860. Implementation arm of National Ganga River Basin Authority (NGRBA). 'Namami Gange' programme (May 2015, ₹20,000 crore). NMCG authority under Environment (Protection) Act 1986. Director General: Rajeev Kumar Mital (2025).

SIDBI (Small Industries Development Bank of India): established 2 April 1990. HQ Lucknow. Apex institution for MSME financing. Subsidiary of SIDBI: SMCGF (Credit Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro + Small Enterprises). SIDBI Ventures, SMILE fund. Refinances banks, NBFCs for MSME lending.
Demonetization of ₹500 and ₹1000 notes was announced on:

Demonetization (8 Nov 2016, Modi): ₹500 and ₹1000 notes ceased legal tender. Replaced with new ₹500 and ₹2000 notes. Goal: curb black money, counterfeit, terror funding. Impact: cash shortage, GST introduced 1 July 2017.
Personal Data Protection (PDP) Act was passed in:

PDP Act 2023 (Digital Personal Data Protection Act): enacted 11 August 2023. Based on Justice BN Srikrishna Committee (2017). Rights: access, correction, erasure. Consent for personal data. Significant data fiduciaries (higher obligations). Data Protection Board of India. DigiLocker, Aadhaar integration. Late implementation: rules pending.
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY) aims to provide:

PMAY (25 June 2015): 'Housing for All' (originally by 2022, extended). PMAY-Urban + PMAY-Gramin. ~4 crore houses sanctioned (3+ crore completed). Interest subsidy on home loans (CLSS). Target: 2 crore more houses (2024-29).
NHB (National Housing Bank) was established in:

NHB: established 9 July 1988. Apex institution for housing finance. wholly owned by RBI (100%). Regulates + supervises Housing Finance Companies (HFCs). Promotes housing finance institutions. PruBoN (Prudential Regulation on Net Owned Funds). Refinances HFCs.
National Logistics Policy was launched on:

National Logistics Policy (17 September 2022, complement to PM Gati Shakti): reduce logistics cost (~13% of GDP to 8%, target by 2030). Components: Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP), Integration of Digital System (IDS), Ease of Logistics (E-Log), System Improvement Group (SIG). India's logistics cost ~13-14% of GDP (vs USA 8%, China 10%).

BharatNet (2011, earlier NOFN - National Optical Fibre Network): connect 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats with broadband. Originally target 2015, extended multiple times. ~2 lakh GPs connected (2024, optic fibre). ~6 lakh km optic fibre. Fibre-to-the-Home (FTTH) extended to ~6 lakh villages (Aug 2024). Modes: PPP, CPS, State-led.
Public sector banks hold what share of India's banking assets?

PSBs (Public Sector Banks): ~60% of banking assets (12 PSBs after consolidation 2020 - reduced from 27). SBI largest (~25% market share). Pvt banks: ~30% (HDFC, ICICI, Axis, Kotak). Foreign banks: ~5%. RRBs + cooperative banks: ~5%. Lending mostly by PSBs.
Bank nationalization in India happened in phases:

Bank nationalization: 19 July 1969 (14 banks - Indira Gandhi), 15 April 1980 (6 more). Total 20 nationalized. Goal: social control, financial inclusion, agriculture credit. SBI: nationalized 1955 (separate - Imperial Bank). Allied: 7 SBI associates (merged with SBI 2017).
UPI (Unified Payments Interface) was launched by:

UPI: launched 11 April 2016 by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India). Real-time inter-bank transfer. Built on IMPS. Currently handles billions of transactions/month (Sept 2024: 16+ billion, ~₹20 lakh crore). Adopted by many countries.
Deposit Insurance covers deposits up to:

Deposit Insurance + Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC): deposit insurance up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (raised from ₹1 lakh in Feb 2020, after PMC Bank crisis). Covers all commercial banks + cooperative banks. Premium: banks pay.(insured deposits, max 0.15%). Insures principal + interest.
MSP (Minimum Support Price) covers how many crops?

MSP: 23 crops + FRP (Fair + Remunerative Price) for sugarcane = 24. Crops: 7 cereals (paddy, wheat, jowar, bajra, maize, ragi, barley), 5 pulses, 7 oilseeds, 4 commercial crops. CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs + Prices) recommends. C2+50% formula (Swaminathan, asked by farmers' unions).
Co-operative banks in India are regulated by:

Cooperative banks: dual control. RBI: banking regulation (Banking Regulation Act, 1966 amendment). State/Central Registrar: Cooperative Societies Act. UCBs (Urban Cooperative Banks), RRBs (Rural Cooperative Banks - State + Centre + Sponsor commercial bank). Amendments (2020) - more RBI powers.

REER: weighted avg of bilateral exchange rates vs major trading partners, adjusted for inflation differentials. NEER: nominal (not adjusted). REER > 100: overvalued. India REER (36-currency): ~105-110 (2024). Indicates rupee somewhat overvalued in real terms despite nominal depreciation.
Suryamitra Skill Development Programme is for:

Suryamitra (2015, National Institute of Solar Energy): 600-hour residential program for solar PV technicians. Target: 50,000 Suryamitras by 2020 (achieved). Skill Council for Green Jobs (SCGJ) implements. Employment in solar companies, installers. Supports solar mission's job creation. ~30,000 trained.
UDAY (Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana) is for:
Financial turnaround of power distribution companies

UDAY (20 November 2015): revive debt-stressed discoms (power distribution companies). States take over 75% of discom debt (April 2016 - March 2019). Operational improvements: smart meters, feeder separation, reduction in AT&C losses. Mixed success - many discoms still loss-making. Revamped Reforms-based Linked Scheme (RDSS) 2021.
Total value of goods and services produced within a country

GDP: total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a year. India GDP 2024-25: ~$3.9 trillion (5th largest, after US, China, Germany, Japan). Aim: $5 trillion by 2027, $10 trillion by 2035.

India trade 2023-24: exports ~$437 billion, imports ~$678 billion. Trade deficit: ~$240 billion. Top partners: USA (largest, ~$118B), China (2nd, ~$118B). UAE, Russia, Saudi Arabia, Singapore others. Services exports: ~$325 billion. IT services ~$194 billion.

Sensex (BSE): crossed 80,000 (3 July 2024, intraday). Peak: ~85,978 (27 September 2024). Then declined. NIFTY 50 (NSE): crossed 25,000 (3 July 2024). India among top global performers. Reasons: GDP growth, earnings, FII inflows, retail participation (SIPs ~₹20,000 crore/month).
National Electric Mobility Mission Plan (NEMMP) targets how many EVs by 2020?

NEMMP 2020 (2013): target 6-7 million EVs (4-wheeler + 2-wheeler + buses) by 2020. Partially achieved. FAME (Faster Adoption + Manufacturing of Hybrid + Electric Vehicles): FAME-I (2015-19, ₹895 crore), FAME-II (April 2019, ₹10,000 crore, 5 years): subsidies for EVs (2W, 3W, 4W, buses), charging infrastructure. PLI for ACC batteries.

Bull market: rising prices (optimism, buying). Bear market: falling (pessimism, selling). Origin: bull attacks by horns upward, bear swipes paws downward. India longest bull market: 2003-08 (Sensex 3000 to 21000). 2020-24: bull market (post-COVID recovery).
India is world's largest producer of:

India largest producer of: milk (24% global, ~230M tonnes/year - Operation Flood/Verghese Kurien), pulses, jute, mango, banana, ginger, turmeric, black pepper. 2nd largest: rice, wheat, sugar, fruits, vegetables, tea, cotton, groundnut. Largest exporter: rice (~40% global), spices, beef (carabeef).
Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) provides:

PMJJBY (9 May 2015): life insurance ₹2 lakh. Premium: ₹436/year (auto-debit from bank). Age: 18-50 years. Death due to any cause. ~17 crore enrolled (2024). 5-year life insurance policy (renewable). PMSBY (PM Suraksha Bima Yojana): accident insurance ₹2 lakh, ₹20/year.
Pension Fund Regulatory and Development Authority (PFRDA) was established in:

PFRDA: established 2013 (PFRDA Act). Chairman: Deepak Mohanty (2024). Regulates NPS (National Pension System), APY (Atal Pension Yojana). NPS launched Jan 2004 (govt employees), 2009 (all citizens). Tier I + Tier II accounts. Corpus ~₹12 lakh crore (2024).
India's GDP at PPP (Purchasing Power Parity) is:

India GDP (PPP, 2024): ~14 trillion international dollars - 3rd largest (after China, USA). Nominal GDP: ~$3.9 trillion - 5th largest. PPP adjusts for cost of living differences. Per capita PPP: ~$9,000 (vs ~$2,800 nominal). World's poorest large economy per capita.
GNP differs from GDP by including:

GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). NFIA = income earned by citizens abroad - income earned by foreigners domestically. India's NFIA: positive (remittances ~$125 billion in 2023-24, world's largest).

Primary Deficit = Fiscal Deficit - Interest Payments. Shows government's borrowing for current operations (excluding past debt servicing). If zero: government borrowing only for interest payments. India: positive but small (govt borrowing more than just interest).

Stagflation: stagnation (low/no growth) + high inflation + high unemployment. Keynesian theory struggled to explain (Phillips curve broken). 1970s oil shocks caused global stagflation. India 1970s, recent concerns. Solution: supply-side reforms + monetary tightening (difficult).
Kisan Credit Card (KCC) was introduced in:

KCC (1998, Vajpayee government): short-term credit to farmers. PM-KISAN convergence (Jan 2020): 2% interest subvention, up to ₹3 lakh. Concessional 3% for prompt repayment. PM-KISAN beneficiary can get KCC. ~7.5 crore KCC issued (2024). Now covers dairy, fisheries (2018-19 extension).
MGNREGA provides how many days of guaranteed wage employment per year?

MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005): provides 100 days of wage employment per rural household per year. Legal right. Started 2 February 2006 (200 districts, expanded 2008). Largest social security program worldwide.
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) was enacted in:

IBC 2016: enacted May 2016. Time-bound resolution of insolvency (180+90 days). Insolvency + Bankruptcy Board of India (IBBI). NCLT (National Company Law Tribunal) - adjudicates. Recovered ~₹3+ lakh crore. Major reform - reduced NPAs.替代SARFAESI Act for corporate defaults.
Consumer Price Index (CPI) base year in India is:

CPI base year: 2012. Released by NSO (National Statistical Office, MoSPI). Earlier separate CPIs: Rural, Urban, Agricultural Labourers, Industrial Workers. Combined CPI (Rural + Urban) since 2011. CPI used for: monetary policy, inflation targeting, dearness allowance (DA) for govt employees.
Local Area Banks (LABs) were allowed in:

LABs: private sector, 1996 (radius of 50 km, 3 contiguous districts). Capital: ₹5 crore. Aim: rural banking. 4 LABs: Coastal Local Area Bank (Vijayawada), Capital Local Area Bank (Phagwara), Krishna Bhima Samruddhi (Mahbubnagar), Subhadra Local Area Bank (Kolhapur). No new licenses since 2000.
Fiscal Deficit of Government of India (2023-24) was:

Fiscal Deficit 2023-24 (revised): ~5.6% of GDP. Budget estimate was 5.8%. Target 2024-25: 4.9%. Target 2025-26: 4.5% (under consolidation path). FRBM Act (2003) targets: 3% fiscal deficit, 40% debt-GDP. Pandemic peak: 9.2% (2020-21).
Services sector contributes what percentage to India's GDP?

Services sector: ~53% of GDP (largest), ~30% of workforce. Major: IT, finance, real estate, healthcare, tourism, education, communication. India's services export: $325 billion (2023-24). IT alone: $194 billion.
Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) became statutory in:

SEBI: established 1988 (administrative), became statutory 1992 (SEBI Act). HQ Mumbai. Chairman: Tuhin Kanta Pandey (2025). Regulates: stock markets, mutual funds, FIIs, merchant bankers, brokers. Insiders trading, takeover code, listing norms. Powers enhanced after Harshad Mehta scam (1992).
CPI components with highest weight in India:

CPI weights (2012 base): Food + beverages 45.86%, Pan/Tobacco 2.38%, Clothing 6.53%, Housing 10.07%, Fuel 6.84%, Misc (health, education, transport) 28.32%. Food dominant - high food inflation hits poor most. Core CPI (excludes food + fuel): ~3-4%.
GDP at current prices is called:

Nominal GDP: at current market prices (no inflation adjustment). Real GDP: adjusted for inflation (using base year, currently 2011-12 for India). PPP GDP: adjusted for purchasing power parity. India: 5th by nominal, 3rd by PPP GDP.

Deflation: negative inflation (general price level falling). Rare, more dangerous than inflation (delays purchases, depresses economy). Japan: 'lost decade' (1990s-2000s) due to deflation. Disinflation: slowing of inflation rate (still positive, e.g., 8% → 5%). Stagflation: stagnation + inflation.
India is the world's largest democracy by:

India: world's largest democracy. ~97 crore voters (2024 LS elections). 543 LS seats. Voter turnout: ~67% (2019). 2024: ~64% turnout. BJP (NDA) won 240+ seats (Modi 3rd term). 5-year term. Federal parliamentary democratic republic.
Jal Jeevan Mission aims to provide:
Functional Household Tap Connection to every rural household by 2024

JJM (15 August 2019): Har Ghar Jal. Goal: Functional Household Tap Connection (FHTC) to every rural household (55 lpcd). Originally by 2024, target ~15 crore households. As of 2024: ~75% rural households have FHTC. ~₹3.6 lakh crore budget.
Inflation indexing bonds (IIBs) are designed to:

IIBs: principal + interest adjusted for inflation (CPI). India issued June 2013 (Wholesale Price Index based). Later discontinued. Inflation-indexed National Savings Securities (CIINSS): launched Dec 2013 (CPI based). Popularity low. Inflation-protected savings option.
National Mineral Policy was revised in:

National Mineral Policy 2019: replaces 2008 policy. Key changes: 1) exploration priority (private sector), 2) auctions (transparency), 3) ease of doing business, 4) sustainable mining, 5) mining trust fund (district mineral foundation). MMDR Act 2015 (Mines + Minerals Development + Regulation): auction-based mineral concessions.
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY) provides:

PMSBY (9 May 2015): accident insurance. Death/disability due to accident: ₹2 lakh. Partial disability: ₹1 lakh. Premium: ₹20/year. Age 18-70. Auto-debit. ~43 crore enrolled (2024). PMJJBY (life) + PMSBY (accident) + APY (pension) - social security triad.
LPG connections to women from BPL families

PMUY (1 May 2016): free LPG connections to women from BPL households. Original target: 5 crore (achieved). Extended: 8 crore (achieved 2021). Ujjwala 2.0 (2021) - 1 crore more with first refill + stove free. Reduced indoor air pollution.

Core inflation: excludes food + fuel (volatile, supply-side). Reflects underlying demand-pull inflation. RBI monitors both. India core CPI: ~3-4% (2024). USA core PCE: Fed's preferred measure. Core helps identify long-term inflation trends.
Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on:

SBM (Swachh Bharat Mission, 2 October 2014 - Gandhi's birthday). SBM-Gramin + SBM-Urban. Goal: Open Defecation Free (ODF) India by 2 October 2019 (achieved). 11 crore+ toilets built. SBM 2.0 (2021-26): ODF Plus (solid/liquid waste management).

SBM 2.0 (1 October 2021 - October 2025): ₹1.41 lakh crore. Focus: ODF sustainability + solid waste management. SBM-G: rural. SBM-U: urban. AMRUT 2.0 (water supply). ODF declared 2019 (rural). SBM-G Phase II (2020-25): ODF Plus - villages become ODF + manage waste. Open defecation still persists in some areas (NFHS data).
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme aims to:
Boost domestic manufacturing in key sectors

PLI Scheme (April 2020): boost domestic manufacturing in 14 sectors - electronics, pharma, telecom, auto, textiles, food processing, white goods, steel, advanced chemistry cell, specialty steel, drones, etc. ₹1.97 lakh crore outlay. Atmanirbhar Bharat.
Smart Cities Mission was launched to develop how many smart cities?

Smart Cities Mission (25 June 2015): develop 100 smart cities (selected through challenge). 5-year mission (extended to 2025). ₹100 crore per city per year (central + state equal). Area-based development + pan-city initiatives. ~₹2 lakh crore projects.
HRIDAY (Heritage City Development + Augmentation Yojana) is for:

HRIDAY (21 January 2015): heritage city development. 12 cities: Ajmer, Amravati, Amritsar, Badami, Dwarka, Gaya, Kanchipuram, Mathura, Puri, Varanasi, Velankanni, Warangal. ₹500 crore (100% Central funding). Completed 2019. Projects: heritage infrastructure, urban revival, tourism.
Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme covers how many sectors?

PLI Scheme (April 2020, ₹1.97 lakh crore, ~$26 billion): 14 sectors - electronics, pharma, telecom, auto + auto components, textiles, food products, white goods, steel, advanced chemistry cell, specialty steel, drones, semiconductors, IT hardware, medical devices. Boost Make in India, manufacturing, exports.
Repo rate is currently (as of Dec 2024):

Repo rate (Dec 2024): 6.5%. Held since Feb 2023 (8 consecutive pauses). MPC's stance: 'withdrawal of accommodation'. Repo: RBI lends to banks against govt securities (current rate). Reverse repo (3.35%): banks lend to RBI. MSF (7.5%): emergency bank borrowing.
Agriculture contributes ~18% to India's GDP but employs:

Agriculture: ~18% GDP, ~46% workforce. Disproportionate - low productivity. Services: ~53% GDP, ~30% workforce. Industry: ~29% GDP, ~24% workforce. Need: shift workforce from agriculture to manufacturing/services (structural transformation).
PM Vishwakarma Yojana is for which group?

PM Vishwakarma Kaushal Samman (PM-VIKAS, 17 Sep 2023): traditional artisans/craftspeople (18 trades - barber, washerman, carpenter, mason, etc.). Recognition, collateral-free loan up to ₹3 lakh (1st ₹1 lakh, 2nd ₹2 lakh), skill training, toolkit, digital empowerment.
Inflation in India is mainly measured by which index?

CPI: primary measure of inflation since 2014 (RBI adopted CPI for monetary policy). Earlier WPI used (since 1990s). WPI excludes services (60% of GDP). CPI reflects retail prices consumers pay. Components: food (~45%), fuel, clothing, housing, etc.
WTO (World Trade Organization) was established in:

WTO: established 1 January 1995 (replaced GATT 1947). HQ: Geneva. 164 members. India founding member. Director-General: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala (Nigeria). Doha Round (2001- stalled). Disputes via dispute settlement body.
India's IT sector contributes approximately what percentage to GDP?

IT sector: ~8% of India's GDP, ~25% of exports ($254 billion 2023-24 - IT + BPM). Employs ~55 lakh directly. Indian IT companies: TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL, Tech Mahindra. NASSCOM (industry body). Cities: Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Chennai, Pune, NCR. Growth: digital transformation, AI.
PM Vishwakarma Yojana provides interest subvention up to:

PM-Vishwakarma: collateral-free loan up to ₹3 lakh (first tranche ₹1 lakh, second ₹2 lakh). Interest subvention 5% (for prompt repayment). Convergence with Mudra Yojana for higher loans. Free toolkit, skill training, digital empowerment.
Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana provides:
Free food grains to ~81 crore beneficiaries

PMGKAY (launched during COVID-19, March 2020): free food grains (rice, wheat, pulses) to NFSA beneficiaries (~81 crore). Continued beyond COVID. Now integrated with NFSA: free food grains to Antyodaya + Priority households (since 1 Jan 2023).
Jan Dhan Yojana is related to:

PM Jan Dhan Yojana (28 Aug 2014): financial inclusion. Zero-balance bank accounts with RuPay debit card, accident insurance (₹2 lakh), overdraft facility (₹10,000). Guinness World Record - 1.5 crore accounts in 1 week.
India's rank in Global Hunger Index 2024 was:

GHI 2024: India ranked 105 out of 127 (worse than neighbors: Bangladesh 84, Pakistan 109, Sri Lanka 89, Nepal 68). GHI indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, child mortality. India's score 27.3 (serious).

PM-AASHA (Pradhan Mantri Annadata Aay SanraksHan Abhiyan, September 2018): ensures MSP to farmers. Components: 1) PSS (Price Support Scheme) - procurement of pulses + oilseeds, 2) PDPS (Price Deficiency Payment Scheme) - direct payment if market price < MSP, 3) PPSS (Pilot Private Procurement + Stockist Scheme). Limited success.
Bank Rate differs from Repo Rate in:
Bank Rate is for short term
Bank Rate has no collateral (Repo has govt securities)

Bank Rate: RBI's long-term lending rate (no collateral, no repurchase agreement). Currently: 6.75% (Repo + 0.25%, same as MSF). Bank Rate = MSF. Repo: against govt securities (with buyback). Repo used routinely; Bank Rate historically + signal.
GST (Goods and Services Tax) was implemented in India from:

GST: launched 1 July 2017. 'One Nation, One Tax'. Replaced multiple indirect taxes (VAT, excise, service tax, etc.). 4 slabs initially: 5%, 12%, 18%, 28%. GST Council (Article 279A) governs. 101st Constitutional Amendment enabled.
Crop Insurance Scheme PMFBY was launched in:

PMFBY (PM Fasal Bima Yojana, 13 January 2016, replaced MNAIS + NAIS + Weather): crop insurance. Premium: 2% (kharif), 1.5% (rabi), 5% (horticulture) of sum insured - balance by govt. Covers natural calamities, pests, diseases. Loanee farmers mandatory. ~5.5 crore farmers (annual). Restructured 2020. PMFBY 2.0 (2024 - enrolment voluntary).
National Food Security Act (NFSA) was passed in:

NFSA 2013: entitled ~67% population (75% rural, 50% urban) to subsidized food grains (5 kg/person/month). Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY, 2000): poorest 2.5 crore families - 35 kg/family/month at ₹1-3/kg. PMGKAY (2024): free food grains under NFSA. ₹2 lakh crore/year. Food Corporation of India (FCI) procures, distributes.
The Reserve Bank of India was established in:

RBI established: 1 April 1935 under RBI Act 1934. Nationalized: 1 January 1949. Central bank of India. Governor: Sanjay Malhotra (25th, since Dec 2024). Issues currency, monetary policy, regulates banks, manages forex.
Digital India programme was launched on:

Digital India (1 July 2015): 9 pillars - broadband highways, universal mobile access, public internet access, e-governance, e-Kranti (electronics delivery), information for all, electronics manufacturing, IT training, early harvest programmes. Aadhaar, UPI, BharatNet, DigiLocker, e-Hospital, e-BIZ. India's digital economy ~10% of GDP.
Unemployment rate in India (2023-24) is approximately:

Unemployment: PLFS (Periodic Labour Force Survey). 2023-24: ~3.2% (usual status). Youth unemployment higher (~10-15%). Female LFPR: ~37% (low - declining 2005-2018, recovering since). CMIE methodology: ~7-8%. USA: ~4%, China: ~5%, Spain: ~12%.
Indian rupee depreciation against USD means:

Rupee depreciation: 1 USD buys more rupees (e.g., ₹70 → ₹75). Causes: trade deficit, FII outflows, dollar strength, high oil prices (India imports). Impact: imports expensive (oil, gold), exports competitive, inflation. 2024: ~₹83-85 per USD.
Long-term investment in foreign company with control

FDI: investment in foreign enterprise with control (≥10% voting stock). Long-term, stable. FPI (Foreign Portfolio Investment): stocks/bonds, no control, volatile. India FDI 2023-24: ~$71 billion (down ~3%). Top sectors: services, computer, telecom.
India's national debt to GDP ratio (2024) is approximately:

India debt-GDP (2023-24): ~81.9% (Centre 58.2%, States 28.9%). Among highest among emerging economies. USA: ~123%, Japan: ~260%, China: ~83%. FRBM target: 60%. Rising due to COVID spending. High debt → interest burden (~20% of central expenditure).
Aadhaar Act 2016 (Targeted Delivery of Financial + Other Subsidies, Benefits + Services) was passed as:

Aadhaar Act 2016: passed as Money Bill (March 2016, bypassed Rajya Sabha). Legal backing to Aadhaar (UIDAI established 2009). SC upheld validity (September 2018, Puttaswamy vs UoI) - restricted mandatory use. ~135 crore enrolments (2024). Privacy concerns addressed: data protection. PDP (Personal Data Protection) Act 2023.
Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Gramin (PMAY-G) target was:

PMAY-G (1 April 2016): target 2.95 crore houses by 2022 (achieved). Earlier Indira Awaas Yojana (IAY, 1985-2016) merged. ₹1.20 lakh assistance (plain), ₹1.30 lakh (hills/NE). 60:40 Centre:State (90:10 for hills/NE). PMAY-G 2.0 (2024-29): 2 crore more houses. ~3 crore houses built in 8 years.
PMAY-Gramin aims to construct houses in rural areas with how much assistance?

PMAY-G (PM Awas Yojana - Gramin): rural housing. ₹1.20 lakh (plain), ₹1.30 lakh (hills/North East). Cost shared 60:40 (Centre:State) - plain, 90:10 for hills/NE. Target: 2.95 crore houses (2016-22). Achieved. PMAY-G 2.0 (2024-29): 2 crore more houses. Convergence: MGNREGA, SBM-G (toilet).
UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik) scheme is for:

UDAN (21 October 2016, Regional Connectivity Scheme): affordable regional flights. 'Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik' (Common citizen flies). RCS-UDAN: cap ₹2500 for 1-hour flight (~500 km), 50% seats subsidized. Viability Gap Funding (VGF) from govt + airport operators. 14 underserved airports (target). 600+ routes, 100+ airports operationalized. Extended till 2030.
PMAY-Urban provides interest subsidy under CLSS for which income groups?

PMAY-U CLSS (Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme): EWS/LIG (income up to ₹6 lakh): 6.5% subsidy on loan up to ₹6 lakh. MIG-I (₹6-12 lakh): 4% subsidy on ₹9 lakh loan. MIG-II (₹12-18 lakh): 3% on ₹12 lakh. CLSS for MIG ended March 2021. PMAY-U 2.0 (2024-29): 1 crore more houses for EWS/LIG/MIG.
FDI inflows into India (2023-24) were approximately:

FDI 2023-24: ~$71 billion (slight decline from $71.4 billion in 2022-23). Top sources: Mauritius, Singapore, USA, Netherlands, Japan. Top sectors: services, computer software, telecom, trading, automobile. India among top FDI destinations (UNCTAD).
The fiscal year in India runs from:

Indian fiscal year: 1 April - 31 March. Union Budget presented on 1 February (since 2017, advanced from last working day of February). Railway Budget merged with Union Budget in 2017 (separate since 1924).
BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money) app was launched on:

BHIM (30 December 2016, PM Modi): UPI-based payment app. NPCI developed. Named after Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. Features: send/receive money, QR code payments, balance check. Multilingual. ~5 crore downloads. Free. Other UPI apps: Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm. UPI: ~16 billion transactions/month (Sept 2024).

MSF: emergency borrowing facility for banks (overnight) from RBI. Repo rate + 0.25% (currently 6.75%). Banks can borrow up to 2% of NDTL. Used when inter-bank liquidity tight. Different from Repo (against govt securities only, MSF even on lower quality securities).
Self-Help Groups (SHGs) credit linkage program is implemented by:

SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (1992, NABARD): financial inclusion + women empowerment. SHGs (10-20 women) save + borrow from banks (no collateral). Day-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission) implements. ~13 lakh SHGs (2024). Women ~85%. Micro-finance. Bandhan, Bharat Microfinance examples.

NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture + Rural Development): established 12 July 1982. HQ Mumbai. Chairman: Shaji KV (2025). Apex development bank for agriculture + rural credit. Came after recommendation of Sivaraman Committee. Refinances RRBs, cooperative banks. Manages Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF).
PM Mudra Yojana provides loans up to:

PM Mudra Yojana (8 April 2015): loans to micro/small businesses (non-corporate, non-farm). Three categories: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishore (₹50,001-5 lakh), Tarun (₹5-10 lakh). No collateral. ~45 crore loans given (2024), ~₹25 lakh crore disbursed. Women: ~70% beneficiaries.
Current Account Deficit (CAD) is financed by:

CAD: trade + services + transfers (remittances). Financed by capital account surplus (FDI, FPI, ECB, NRI deposits). India CAD 2023-24: ~0.7% of GDP (manageable). Sustainable if <2.5% of GDP. Higher CAD → currency depreciation pressure.
The 'Digital India' program was launched on:

Digital India (1 July 2015): 9 pillars - broadband highways, universal mobile access, e-governance, e-Kranti, information for all, electronics manufacturing, IT training, early harvest, job creation. Aadhaar, UPI, BharatNet components.
Payments Banks require minimum capital of:

Payments Banks: ₹100 crore minimum capital. Cannot lend (no credit risk). Deposit limit: ₹2 lakh per customer (raised from ₹1 lakh in April 2021). Accept deposits, payments, remittances, sell insurance/mutual funds. 6 PBs: Airtel Payments, India Post Payments, Paytm Payments, Fino, Jio, NSDL.

Bharatmala (31 July 2017): largest highways program (~66,000 km approved, ₹5.35 lakh crore). Phases I (34,800 km) + II. Components: economic corridors, border + coastal roads, expressways, greenfield projects. Implementing: NHAI. Target: 2 km/day highway construction (achieved 36+ km/day in 2023-24).

ARCs: buy NPAs from banks at discount. SARFAESI Act 2002 enabled. ARCIL first (2003). 28+ ARCs. Help banks clean balance sheets. Issue Security Receipts (SRs) to banks. Recover from borrowers. ARC framework strengthened post-IBC.

GST Council (Article 279A): Union Finance Minister (Chair) + State Finance Ministers + Union MoS Finance. Voting: Centre 1/3, States 2/3. Quorum: 50%. Decisions by 3/4 majority. Set up September 2016. 16th GST Council meeting June 2017 - finalized rates.
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY provides health cover of:

PM-JAY (PM Jan Arogya Yojana, 23 Sep 2018): world's largest govt-funded health insurance. ₹5 lakh per family per year. Covers ~10.74 crore families (bottom 40% based on SECC 2011). Free secondary + tertiary care at empanelled hospitals. Cashless. ~7 crore treatments given (2024).老年人~70+ extension 2024 (all seniors).
Building bridges across rivers + railway crossings

Sethu Bharatam (4 March 2016): eliminates railway level crossings by constructing Road Over Bridges (ROBs) + Road Under Bridges (RUBs). Target: 1500+ level crossings eliminated (achieved 2018). ₹50,000 crore outlay. Indian Railways + NHAI share cost. Reduces accidents + delays. ~1900 bridges built.
CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio) is kept where?

CRR: banks keep with RBI (no interest). Currently 4.5% (since May 2022). Effective from 7 August 2024: 4.5%. Earlier reduced to 3% during COVID (March 2020). SLR: kept with banks themselves. Both are reserves (not for lending). CRR controls liquidity immediately.

NBFCs: shadow banking. Registered under Companies Act. RBI regulates (limited - deposit-taking NBFCs, asset finance). Examples: Bajaj Finance, Muthoot Finance, Cholamandalam. IL&FS crisis 2018 - revealed risks. NBFCs ~25% of credit system. Don't accept demand deposits (most). Cheaper regulations than banks.
PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan was launched on:

PM Gati Shakti (13 October 2021): ₹100 lakh crore infrastructure master plan. Integrates 16 ministries (rail, road, port, airport, power, telecom). Geographic Information System (GIS) platform for project planning. Reduces delays, overlapping. National Logistics Policy (17 September 2022): complementary. Reduce logistics cost (13%→8% of GDP).
Non-Performing Asset (NPA) is a loan where:

NPA: loan where interest or principal installment overdue 90+ days (90 DPD norm, RBI). 3 categories: Sub-Standard (90 days-1 year), Doubtful (1-3 years), Loss (3+ years, written off). Gross NPA: ~3% (2024, improved from 11% in 2018). Net NPA: ~1%. IBC, IBC helped recovery.
Soil Health Card scheme was launched in:

Soil Health Card (19 February 2015): provides soil health to farmers (every 2 years, free). 12 parameters tested (N, P, K, micronutrients, pH, etc.). Recommendations for fertilizer use. ~24 crore cards distributed (2 cycles). Reduces fertilizer misuse. Soil Health Management scheme.
GST Council's 'Cess' on luxury + sin goods is called:

Compensation Cess: GST cess on 28% items (luxury, sin goods - tobacco, aerated drinks, pan masala, cars, SUVs). States get compensation for 5 years (2017-22) for revenue loss due to GST. Cess fund: ₹1+ lakh crore. Extended: March 2026 (to repay loan taken for compensation).
Small Finance Banks (SFBs) require minimum capital of:

SFBs: minimum paid-up capital ₹200 crore (raised from ₹100 crore, 2018). Promoter's stake: minimum 40% (5 years), then 26%. Mandatory: 75% loans to priority sector (vs 40% for commercial). 50% branches in unbanked rural areas. 12 SFBs: AU, Equitas, Ujjivan, etc.
BRICS originally consisted of which countries?
Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa
Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa
Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa

BRICS: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa (S joined 2010). BRIC coined by Goldman Sachs (Jim O'Neill, 2001). Expanded 2024: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE joined (Saudi Arabia considering). ~45% world population, ~35% GDP (PPP).
Manufacturing contributes approximately what to India's GDP?

Manufacturing: ~17% of GDP. Target: 25% by 2025 (National Manufacturing Policy 2011, Make in India 2014). ~12% workforce. PLI scheme ($26B, 14 sectors) to boost. Automotive, pharma (largest generic exporter), textiles, electronics. China +1 strategy, COVID supply chain diversification - India opportunity.
Direct LPG subsidy transfer to consumer's account

PAHAL (DBTL - Direct Benefit Transfer of LPG, 1 January 2015): LPG subsidy transferred directly to consumer's bank account (with Aadhaar). World's largest DBT. ~25 crore beneficiaries. Saved ~₹50,000 crore/year (subsidy savings, ghost connections removed). Give It Up campaign (Modi, 2015): gave up subsidy for poor.
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) were established in:

RRBs: established 2 October 1975 (RRB Act 1976). Sponsors: PSBs. Capital: Centre 50%, State 15%, Sponsor Bank 35%. Aim: rural credit, agriculture, small industries. 43 RRBs (after amalgamation, was 196). 700+ crore customers. Sponsor + RBI + NABARD supervise.
Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) in India (2023) is:

LFPR (2023-24): ~57.9% (urban lower). Female LFPR: ~41.5% (rising, was 23% in 2018). Male LFPR: ~78%. Rural female LFPR higher than urban (agriculture). India's female LFPR among lowest in world (vs world avg ~50%). Self-employment high in rural.
Unnat Jyoti by Affordable LEDs for All (UJALA) is for:
Distribution of LED bulbs at low cost

UJALA (1 January 2015): replace incandescent bulbs with LED bulbs. EESL (Energy Efficiency Services Limited) implements. Cost: ₹10/bulb (subsidized from ₹400 earlier). 36+ crore LED bulbs distributed (2024). Saves ~50 billion kWh/year electricity, reduces bills + emissions. SLN (Street Light National Programme) - LED streetlights.
National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) was passed in:

MGNREGA (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act): passed September 2005, effective 2 February 2006 (200 districts, expanded nationally 2008). 100 days of wage employment per rural household per year. Legal right. ~15 crore active workers. ₹344/day average wage (2024). Women ~57%. Largest social security program globally.
MGNREGA wage rates are revised based on:

MGNREGA wages: indexed to CPI-AL (Agricultural Labourers). States: ₹200-₹350/day (2024-25). Haryana highest (~₹350), Madhya Pradesh lowest (~₹220). Activists demand CPI-Rural (higher). Wage paid through DBT (bank/post office). ~15 crore workers. Avg days of employment: ~50/household (vs 100 guaranteed).
Goods and Services Tax Network (GSTN) is:

GSTN: Section 8 (not-for-profit) private company. 49% government (Centre 24.5%, States 24.5%), 51% private (banks, institutions). Manages GST IT system. N. Chandrasekaran chairman (since 2021). Provides registration, returns, invoicing, e-way bill infrastructure.
Airtel Payments Bank was the first to start operations in:

Airtel Payments Bank: first PB to start (12 January 2017). Bharti Airtel subsidiary. India Post Payments Bank (IPPB): launched 1 September 2018 (rural focus). Paytm Payments Bank (PPBL): RBI restrictions 2024 (after March 2024, no deposits accepted, closing down).
Skill India Mission aims to train how many youth by 2022?

Skill India (15 July 2015, World Youth Skills Day): PMKVY (PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana) - short-term training. NSDC (National Skill Development Corporation). Target: 40 crore skilled by 2022 (revised). NSQF (National Skills Qualifications Framework).

PM-KISAN (24 Feb 2019): ₹6000/year per family to small + marginal farmers (up to 2 hectares). 3 installments of ₹2000 (4-monthly). DBT to bank accounts. ~8 crore beneficiaries. 19 installments released (2024). ₹3.46 lakh crore disbursed. Excludes: income tax payers, institutional farmers.

EXIM Bank (Export-Import Bank of India): established 1982. HQ Mumbai. Apex institution for financing foreign trade. Chairman: Harsha Bangari (2025). Provides: buyer's credit, supplier's credit, lines of credit (LOC) to foreign governments. Operates through BRICS bank (NDB), AIIB.
National Waterways Act 2016 declared how many national waterways?

National Waterways Act 2016: declared 111 national waterways (earlier only 5: Ganga, Brahmaputra, West Coast Canal, etc.). IWAI (Inland Waterways Authority of India, 1986) develops. National Waterway 1: Ganga (Allahabad-Haldia, 1620 km). NW 2: Brahmaputra (Dhubri-Sadiya, 891 km). Cost-effective + eco-friendly freight transport. Target: 1% (now) to 5% by 2030 of total freight.

PM-SVANIDHI (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi, 1 June 2020): launched during COVID. Street vendors get loans: ₹10,000 (initial), up to ₹30,000 (2nd), ₹50,000 (3rd). No collateral. 7% interest subsidy. Cashback on digital transactions. ~80 lakh vendors (target), ~50 lakh loans given.

PM-KMY (Sep 2019): pension scheme for small + marginal farmers (18-40 years). ₹3000/month at age 60. Contribution: ₹55-200/month (age-based). Matching govt contribution. Joint with LIC. Auto-debit from PM-KISAN account. ~50 lakh enrolled (2024).

Banking Regulation Act 1949: regulates banking companies. RBI supervises. Provisions: licensing, capital requirements, cash reserve, liquid assets, restrictions on loans, audits. Cooperative banks: brought under RBI supervision (1965 amendment, effective 1 March 1966). UCBs - dual control (RBI + State).
Percentage of deposits banks must keep in liquid assets

SLR: percentage of Net Demand + Time Liabilities (NDTL) that banks must maintain in liquid assets (cash, gold, govt securities). Currently: 18% (reduced from 23% in 2010). CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio): 4.5% (kept with RBI, no interest). Both RBI tools to control liquidity.
GST Council Compensation Cess duration has been extended to:

Compensation Cess: extended till March 2026 (was March 2022). Reason: repay ₹2.69 lakh crore back-to-back loan (borrowed in 2021-22 for compensation to states). After loan repayment: cess will be merged with GST revenue or new use. Decision: GST Council.
India is the world's largest producer of:

India largest producer of: milk (~24% of global, ~230 million tonnes/year), pulses, jute, mango, banana, ginger, turmeric, black pepper. 2nd largest: rice, wheat, sugar, fruits, vegetables, tea. Largest exporter of: rice, spices.
Government's revenue expenditure exceeds revenue receipts

Revenue Deficit = Revenue Expenditure - Revenue Receipts. Indicates government's current income insufficient for current expenses (borrowing for consumption). Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue Deficit - Grants to States for creation of capital assets. Target: 0%.
Stock market indices: NIFTY 50 represents which exchange?
NIFTY 50: NSE index, top 50 companies across 22 sectors. Base: 1000 (1 Nov 1995). Sensex: BSE, top 30 companies (1986). NSE: 1992 (incorporated), 1994 (trading). BSE: Asia's oldest (1875).
India's GDP growth rate in 2023-24 was approximately:

India GDP growth 2023-24: 8.2% (real GDP). FY 2024-25 estimate: ~6.5-7%. India fastest growing major economy. IMF, World Bank project 6.5-7% for FY26. China: ~5%, USA: ~2.5%. India to be 3rd largest economy by 2027.
eNAM (National Agriculture Market) was launched in:

eNAM (14 April 2016): online trading platform for agricultural commodities. Integrates APMC (Agricultural Produce Market Committee) mandis. ~1400+ mandis (2024, 23 states + 4 UTs). ~1.8 crore farmers, ~2.5 lakh traders. Increase farmer prices, reduce intermediaries. 200+ commodities traded.
India's services sector growth is mainly driven by:

Services sector: ~53% GDP, growing fastest. Components: IT/BPM, finance (banking, insurance), telecom, real estate, professional services, tourism, healthcare, education. ~30% workforce. India services exports: $325B (2023-24). IT/BPM alone: $254B.
The Human Development Index (HDI) is published by:

HDI: published by UNDP (since 1990). Composite index: life expectancy, education (mean years of schooling, expected years), per capita income. India ranked 134 (2023-24) out of 193. Top: Switzerland, Norway, Iceland.
The 'Lender of Last Resort' in India is:

RBI: 'Lender of Last Resort' - provides emergency funds to banks in crisis. Prevents bank runs. Also: banker to government, custodian of forex reserves, issues currency, controller of credit. Currency chest, public debt management.
Stand-Up India scheme provides loans to:

Stand-Up India (5 April 2016): loans ₹10 lakh-1 crore to SC/ST + Women entrepreneurs for setting up greenfield enterprise. 7 years repayment. Refinance: SIDBI. Scheduled Commercial Banks implement. ~2 lakh loans given (2024). Manufacturing, trading, services.

Direct taxes (paid directly to govt): Income Tax, Corporate Tax, Capital Gains Tax. Indirect taxes (passed on): GST (goods + services), Customs duty, Central Excise (limited after GST). Direct tax: ~50% of Centre's tax revenue (2023-24). CBDT (direct) + CBIC (indirect) under Revenue Department.
RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has how many members?

MPC (Monetary Policy Committee): 6 members - RBI Governor (Chair), Deputy Governor (monetary policy), RBI Executive Director, 3 external members (appointed by Government for 4 years). Decisions by majority. Governor has casting vote in tie. Set up 2016.
PM Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) provides:
Free food grains to ~81 crore beneficiaries

PMGKAY (launched during COVID-19, March 2020): free food grains (rice, wheat, pulses) to NFSA beneficiaries (~81 crore people - Antyodaya + Priority households). Integrated with NFSA from 1 January 2024: free food grains (5kg/person/month) under NFSA. ~₹2 lakh crore annual cost. World's largest food security program.
Inflation in India is measured by:

CPI: primary measure of inflation (RBI targets 4% ±2%). WPI: wholesale prices (no services). CPI components: food, fuel, clothing, housing, etc. Earlier WPI used as main ( till 2014). RBI shifted to CPI in 2014.

Trade deficit: imports > exports. Trade surplus: exports > imports. India has chronic trade deficit in goods. Trade surplus in services. Current Account Deficit (CAD): includes trade + services + remittances. CAD 2023-24: ~0.7% of GDP.
Skill India Mission aims to train youth under PMKVY:

PMKVY (PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana, 15 July 2015, World Youth Skills Day): short-term training (NSQF aligned). NSDC (National Skill Development Corporation). 726 PMKVY centers. ~1.4 crore trained (2024). Target: 4 crore skilled by 2022 (revised). NSQF (National Skills Qualifications Framework).
Atal Pension Yojana (APY) provides pension from age:

APY (9 May 2015): pension scheme for unorganized sector (18-40 years). Pension ₹1000-5000/month at age 60. Govt co-contribution (50% of total, max ₹1000/year) for non-tax payers. Auto-debit from bank account. Subscriber's spouse continues after death. ~6 crore subscribers (2024). PFRDA manages.
First sale of company's shares to public

IPO: company first sells shares to public. Listed on stock exchange. SEBI regulates (Prospectus). Recent large IPOs: LIC (₹21,000 crore, May 2022), Paytm (₹18,300 crore, Nov 2021), Hyundai India (₹27,870 crore, Oct 2024 - largest in India). Oversubscription common in bull markets.
Sagar Mala Programme + Bharatmala + Sagarmala together aim to:

Sagarmala (port-led development) + Bharatmala (highways) + Dedicated Freight Corridors (rail): integrated logistics. Reduce logistics cost (~13% of GDP to 8% target). Multi-modal transport. PM Gati Shakti (October 2021): National Master Plan - integrates 16 ministries for infrastructure planning. ₹100 lakh crore investment target.
Free LPG connections to BPL women

PMUY (1 May 2016): free LPG connections to women from BPL households. Original target: 5 crore (achieved). Extended: 8 crore (achieved 2021). Ujjwala 2.0 (10 August 2021): 1 crore more with first refill + stove free. Migrants included. ~10 crore beneficiaries (2024). Reduced indoor air pollution.
