Market phases: Pullback (5-9.99% decline), Correction (10-19.99%), Bear market (20%+ from peak). Bull market: rising trend. India: longest bull market 2003-2008 (5 years). 2008 crash: ~60% decline. 2020 COVID crash: ~38% (then recovered). 2024-25: consolidation phase.
Coastal Economic Zones (CEZs) under Sagarmala Programme:

Sagarmala Programme (25 March 2015): port-led development along India's coastline. Components: port modernization, port-led industrialization (CEZs), coastal community development, enhanced connectivity. 14 CEZs (planned): linked to 12 major ports. ~535 projects, ₹3.5 lakh crore investment. Min of Ports, Shipping + Waterways.
Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) resolution timelines are:

IBC timeline: 180 days (extendable by 90 days = 270 total, or 330 with extensions). Committee of Creditors (CoC) decides resolution. Liquidation if no resolution. Resolution Professional (RP) manages debtor. IBC has resolved ~700+ cases, recovered ~₹3+ lakh crore.
Saubhagya scheme (Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana) is for:

Saubhagya (September 2017): electrify all willing households (rural + urban). Free electricity connection: BPL households, ₹500 for APL (EWS). Earlier Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY). 2.8 crore connections (achieved 2018). 100% village electrification (28 April 2018, Leisang village, Manipur). '24x7 Power for All' programme.
India's largest bank by assets is:

SBI: largest bank (assets ~₹50 lakh crore, 2024). 22,000+ branches, 58,000 ATMs. Founded 1955 (imperial Bank nationalized). Government: ~57% stake. HDFC Bank: largest private (after HDFC merger July 2023, ~₹30 lakh crore). ICICI 2nd private.

DigiLocker (February 2015): digital document wallet. Issued by MeitY. Citizens get 1 GB free storage. Government documents (Aadhaar, PAN, driving license, education certificates, etc.) available in digital format. Legally valid under IT Act 2000. ~30 crore users (2024). ~600+ document types. Used for KYC, verification.

Cosmopolitan bank: operates across borders, global presence. RBI's vision: develop some Indian banks as cosmopolitan. SBI, ICICI, HDFC, Axis expanding overseas. 2024: RBI gave 'on-tap' universal banking license (corporate + NBFCs can apply, ₹1000 crore capital).
Generative AI like ChatGPT is based on which architecture?
Transformer (2017, Google paper 'Attention is All You Need')

Transformer architecture: introduced by Google researchers (2017, paper 'Attention is All You Need'). Revolutionized NLP. Self-attention mechanism. Basis for: GPT (Generative Pre-trained Transformer), BERT, Claude, Gemini, LLaMA. GPT-1 (2018), GPT-3 (2020, 175B params), GPT-4 (2023). Vaswani et al.
Pinaka multi-barrel rocket launcher has which range?

Pinaka (named after Shiva's bow): MBRL system. 12 rockets/launcher, fired in 44 seconds. Warheads: fragmentation, incendiary, anti-tank mines, bunker buster. Pinaka-I: 40 km range. Pinaka-II: 60 km. Pinaka-ER (Extended Range): 90 km. Guided Pinaka: precision. Used in Kargil (1999), tested successfully.

Cochin International Airport (CIAL, Kerala): first 100% solar-powered airport (August 2015). Solar plant: 12 MW (later expanded to 40+ MW). 46,150 solar panels. Produces more than consumed - exports surplus to grid. ~₹62 crore investment, payback 6 years. Model for other airports.
BrahMos missile can be launched from:

BrahMos: supersonic cruise missile (Mach 2.8-3.0). India-Russia JV (DRDO + NPO Mashinostroyenia). Named: Brahmaputra + Moskva rivers. Variants: Land (mobile launcher), Air (Su-30MKI - 2.5 tonne), Ship (vertical launch), Submarine (torpedo tube). Range: 290-800 km (extended). Hypersonic BrahMos-II under development.

Covishield: developed by Oxford University + AstraZeneca. Manufactured in India by Serum Institute of India (Pune, world's largest vaccine maker). Adenovirus vector (chimpanzee). Used in India (vaccinated ~60% population). Covaxin: Bharat Biotech (inactivated).
Chandrayaan-3 successfully landed on Moon on:

Chandrayaan-3 (14 July 2023 launch): Vikram lander soft-landed on 23 August 2023. Pragyan rover deployed. Landing spot: 'Shiva Shakti Point' (70°S). First landing on Lunar South Pole region. India became 4th country to land on Moon (after USSR, US, China).
Plastic waste to fuel technology converts plastic into:

Plastic-to-fuel: pyrolysis (thermal decomposition in absence of oxygen) converts plastic waste to liquid fuel similar to diesel/petrol. ~1 kg plastic → ~700-800 ml fuel. CSIR-IIP Dehradun developed technology. Reduces plastic pollution + provides fuel. Pilots in many cities.
Bt cotton contains gene from which bacteria?

Bt cotton: genetically modified cotton with gene from Bacillus thuringiensis. Produces Bt toxin → kills bollworm (cotton pest). India's only approved GM crop (2002). Reduces pesticide use. Controversies: yields, farmer suicides, Monsanto monopoly.
Telemedicine service eSanjeevani was launched in:

eSanjeevani: National Telemedicine Service. 2 variants: 1) eSanjeevani AB-HWC (doctor-to-doctor, 2019, for HWCs), 2) eSanjeevani OPD (patient-to-doctor, April 2020, during COVID). ~14 crore consultations (2024). Free. Implemented by C-DAC + MoHFW. Multilingual. Used in: rural areas, prisons, elderly. AIIMS + state health departments.
Defence Industrial Corridors in India are at:

Defence Industrial Corridors: 2 announced (2018). 1) UP (Bundelkhand) - Aligarh, Agra, Jhansi, Lalitpur, Chitrakoot. 2) Tamil Nadu - Chennai, Tiruchirappalli, Coimbatore, Salem, Hosur. Promote defence manufacturing (MSMEs, jobs). Investments ~₹3,000+ crore each. Aimed at reducing defence imports (~60% to 30% target by 2025).
Agni-V is which type of missile?

Agni-V: ICBM. Solid-fueled, 3-stage. Range: 5000-5500+ km. First test 19 April 2012. Can carry nuclear warhead (~1.5 tonnes). MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle) tested April 2024. 8th in Agni series.
Golden Rice was approved for cultivation in:

Golden Rice: genetically engineered rice with β-carotene (vitamin A precursor). Ingo Potrykus + Peter Beyer (1999). Vitamin A deficiency: ~250 million children worldwide. Philippines approved 2021 (first). India: not approved (concerns: yield, alternative interventions). Bangladesh: trial. Criticized: low β-carotene levels, IP issues, GM concerns.
Right to Privacy as Fundamental Right was recognized in:

Puttaswamy vs UoI (24 August 2017, 9-judge bench, unanimous): recognized Right to Privacy as fundamental right under Articles 14, 19, 21. Overruled earlier Kharak Singh (1962) + ADM Jabalpur (1976). 'Privacy includes informational privacy, bodily integrity, decisional autonomy'. Basis for: Aadhaar verdict (2018), DPDP Act (2023), Section 377 struck down (Navtej Singh Johar, 2018).
India's 3-stage nuclear program was conceived by:

Homi Bhabha's 3-stage nuclear program: 1) PHWR (natural uranium, U-235 fission, produces Pu-239), 2) Fast Breeder Reactor (Pu-239 + Th-232 → U-233), 3) Thorium reactors (U-233). Aim: utilize India's vast thorium reserves (largest in world, ~25% global). Stage 1: operational (22 reactors). Stage 2: PFBR under commissioning (Kalpakkam). Stage 3: ~2050 target.
Apache AH-64E helicopters are manufactured by:

Apache AH-64E (I): US Boeing manufactured attack helicopter. IAF: 22 (2015-2020). Army Aviation: 6 more ordered. ~$3 billion deal. ~90% Indian work share for follow-on (Tata Boeing Aerospace, Hyderabad). Replaces Mi-35. Heavy attack helicopter. Air-to-ground, anti-tank.
Nuclear power plants in India use which main fuel?

Nuclear plants use U-235 (fissile). India's 3-stage nuclear program: Stage 1 - PHWR (natural uranium, U-238 + U-235). Stage 2 - FBR (plutonium-239 from U-238 + thorium blanket). Stage 3 - Thorium (Th-232 → U-233). India has world's largest thorium reserves.

ISRO HQ: Bengaluru (Antariksh Bhavan). Chairman: V. Narayanan (2025). Founded 15 August 1969 (Indian National Committee for Space Research - INCOSPAR earlier 1962). First chairman: Vikram Sarabhai. Department of Space (PM as minister in-charge). Annual budget: ~₹13,000 crore (2024-25).
Wind energy capacity in India is mainly concentrated in:

Wind energy: India 4th largest globally (~44 GW installed, 2024). Top states: Gujarat (~10 GW), Tamil Nadu (~10 GW, pioneer), Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka. Onshore mostly. Offshore planned (Tamil Nadu, Gujarat coasts).

IoT: network of physical objects embedded with sensors, software, connectivity. Examples: smart homes, wearables, smart city, industrial automation. India IoT market growing rapidly. Standards: MQTT, CoAP. Security concerns (DDoS via compromised devices).
Pumped storage hydroelectric project (PSP) is mainly for:

PSP: stores energy. Pumps water from lower to upper reservoir when power surplus (off-peak). Releases water through turbines during peak demand. Examples: Purulia (West Bengal, 900 MW), Kadamparai (Tamil Nadu, 400 MW), Srisailam (Telangana-AP, 1670 MW, Left Bank Power House). Critical for renewable energy integration. India target: ~10 GW PSP by 2032.
First test-tube baby in India was:

India's first IVF baby: Kanupriya Agarwal (alias Durga), born 3 October 1978 in Kolkata. Developed by Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay (1931-1981) - recognition came posthumously. World's first IVF baby: Louise Brown (UK, 25 July 1978, Patrick Steptoe + Robert Edwards, Nobel 2010). Mukhopadhyay's work predated Edwards but wasn't recognized.
DRDO (Defense Research and Development Organization) was established in:

DRDO: formed 1958 (merger of DTDP + TDE). Under Ministry of Defense. Chairman: Sameer V. Kamat (2025). 50+ labs across India. Develops missiles, aircraft, electronics, naval systems. Recent: Astra missile, Arjun tank, Akash SAM, Pinaka MBRL.

5G: three bands - low (sub-1 GHz), mid (1-6 GHz), high (mmWave 24-40 GHz). India: deployed October 2022 (Jio + Airtel). Speed: 100 Mbps - 10 Gbps. Use cases: eMBB (broadband), URLLC (low-latency: autonomous vehicles), mMTC (IoT).
Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC) is at:

SDSC SHAR (Sriharikota High Altitude Range): ISRO's launch site. Andhra Pradesh, on barrier island. ~80 km north of Chennai. 2 launch pads. All major launches: PSLV, GSLV, LVM3. Named after Satish Dhawan (ISRO Chairman 1972-84, 'father of experimental fluid dynamics research in India').
National Medical Commission (NMC) replaced which body in 2020?

NMC (25 September 2020): replaced MCI (established 1933, MCI Act 1956). NMC Act 2019. 4 autonomous boards: UG, PG, Ethics, Assessment + Rating. Common NEET (entrance), NEXT (exit/licensing). 50% seats in private colleges capped fee. National Exit Test (NEXT): replaces NEET-PG, FMGE. President: BN Gangadhar (2025).
Which Indian satellite is used for tele-education?

EDUSAT (GSAT-3): launched 20 Sep 2004 by GSLV-F01. India's first thematic satellite dedicated exclusively for educational services. Connects schools, colleges, universities through virtual classrooms. Used for distance education.

Samudrayaan (5 Oct 2021 announced): India's first manned ocean mission. Manned submersible 'Matsya6000' to depth of 6000m. NIOT (Chennai) building. Will explore deep sea minerals, marine biodiversity, polymetallic nodules. ~₹4000 crore.
Department of Biotechnology (DBT) was established in:

DBT: established 1986 (under Ministry of Science + Technology). Set up on recommendation of Scientific Advisory Committee (SAC, PM Indira Gandhi). Secretary: Rajesh S. Gokhale (2025). Autonomous bodies: ICGEB (New Delhi component), NII, THSTI, inStem. Promotes: biotech research, industry, education. Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC) - biotech startups.
Rafale fighter jets were purchased from:

Rafale: French Dassault Aviation. India: 36 jets (September 2016, ~€7.8 billion). 4.5 generation, twin-engine, multirole. Delivered 2020-2022. IAF squadrons: 17 Squadron 'Golden Arrows' (Ambala), 101 'Falcons' (Hasimara). Equipped with Meteor (long-range air-to-air), Scalp (cruise missile), Hammer (precision bomb).
Blockchain technology is best suited for:

Blockchain: distributed ledger. Cryptographic linking of 'blocks' of transactions. Decentralized, immutable. Use cases: cryptocurrencies (Bitcoin, Ethereum), supply chain, land records, voting, identity. Hyperledger Fabric, Ethereum popular.
Wind energy capacity of India (2024) is approximately:

Wind capacity (2024): ~44.6 GW. India: 4th largest globally (after China, USA, Germany). Top states: Gujarat (~10 GW), Tamil Nadu (~10 GW, pioneer), Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Karnataka. Onshore mostly. Offshore planned (Tamil Nadu, Gujarat coasts). First wind turbine: 1986 (Veraval, Gujarat). MNRE: Solar Energy Corporation of India (SECI) auctions.
Generative AI like ChatGPT is based on:

GenAI: AI that creates new content (text, images, code, audio). Based on LLMs (transformer architecture, 2017 Google paper). ChatGPT (OpenAI, Nov 2022) made it mainstream. Indian LLMs: BharatGPT, Krutrim, Sarvam AI. GPT-4, Claude, Gemini.
IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion + Authorization Center) was established in:

IN-SPACe (June 2020, autonomous body under Department of Space): promotes + authorizes private space activities. Chairman: Pawan Goenka (2024). Single-window for private space companies (Skyroot, Agnikul, Pixxel, Bellatrix). Approves launches, satellite operations. India Space Policy 2023: enables private sector. ~150+ startups in space sector (2024).
Editor's Guild of India was founded in:

Editor's Guild of India: founded 1978. Non-partisan organization of editors. Voice of press freedom. Investigates press violations. Criticizes govt censorship, attacks on journalists. Recent: controversy over report on Manipur (resignations 2023). President: Kamal Jain (2024). Members: ~150 editors of major newspapers, magazines.
Which is India's first indigenously developed supercomputer?

PARAM 8000: India's first supercomputer (1991), developed by C-DAC (Pune, founded 1988). In response to US denial of Cray supercomputer (post-1980s nuclear sanctions). 1 GigaFLOP. Series continued: PARAM 10000, Padma, Yuva, Siddhi-AI, Ganga, Pratyush, Mihir.

DRDO (Defense Research + Development Organisation): formed 1958 (merger of Technical Development Establishment + Directorate of Technical Development + Defence Science Organisation). 50+ labs. Under Ministry of Defence. Chairman: Sameer V. Kamat (2025). Develops missiles (Agni series), aircraft (LCA Tejas), tanks (Arjun), UAVs, naval systems.

Nag (means 'snake' in Sanskrit): 3rd generation anti-tank guided missile (ATGM). Range: 4-7 km. 'Fire-and-forget' (top attack mode). Helina (helicopter-launched): Dhruv helicopters. Nag Missile Carrier (NAMICA) - ground launcher. Inducted 2020. Replaces Russian Konkurs, French Milan.

CRISPR-Cas9: 'genetic scissors'. Bacterial defense system adapted for gene editing. Precise cuts at specific DNA sequences. Discovered: Doudna + Charpentier (Nobel 2020). Applications: sickle cell, cancer immunotherapy, agriculture. Ethical concerns (germline editing).
Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) was established in:

ICMR: established 1911 (as Indian Research Fund Association, renamed 1949). HQ New Delhi. Apex body in India for biomedical research. Under Department of Health Research (Ministry of Health + Family Welfare). Director General: Rajni Bahl (2024, additional charge). 27 national institutes. Develops: drugs, diagnostics, vaccines, public health guidelines.
Machine Learning differs from Deep Learning in:

AI (artificial intelligence): broad field. ML (machine learning): subset of AI. Algorithms learn from data without explicit programming. DL (deep learning): subset of ML. Uses deep neural networks (many layers). Examples: image recognition (CNN), NLP (Transformer), speech (RNN). Famous: AlphaGo (DeepMind 2016, beat Lee Sedol).
INS Vikrant (IAC-1) is which type of vessel?

INS Vikrant (IAC-1): India's first indigenous aircraft carrier. Built by Cochin Shipyard. Commissioned 2 September 2022. ~45,000 tonnes. STOBAR (Short Take-Off But Arrested Recovery). MiG-29K, Tejas Navy. Named after 1961 Vikrant (decommissioned 1997).
GSLV (Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle) is mainly used for:
Launching heavy communication satellites to GEO

GSLV: ISRO's heavy launcher. Capacity: ~5000 kg to LEO, ~2500 kg to GTO. Variants: Mk I, Mk II (with indigenous cryogenic engine), Mk III (LVM3 - heaviest). GSLV Mk III (LVM3): launched Chandrayaan-2 (2019), Chandrayaan-3 (2023). Cryogenic upper stage: developed after US denied technology.
Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre (LPSC) is at:

LPSC: ISRO's liquid propulsion R&D centre. Main: Thiruvananthapuram. Subunits: Mahendragiri (Tamil Nadu - test facilities), Bengaluru (engine development). Develops: liquid engines (Vikas - workhorse, CE-20 cryogenic), propulsion systems for launch vehicles + satellites. ISRO Inertial Systems Unit (IISU): Thiruvananthapuram.

Insulin: discovered by Frederick Banting + Charles Best (University of Toronto, 1921). First patient: 14-year-old Leonard Thompson (January 1922). Nobel Prize 1923 (Banting + Macleod, controversial - Best excluded). Before insulin: diabetes was death sentence. Eli Lilly produced commercially (1923). Recombinant insulin (1982, Genentech).
Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act was passed in:

DPDP Act 2023 (Digital Personal Data Protection Act): enacted 11 August 2023. Based on Justice BN Srikrishna Committee (2017) + Srikrishna Committee (2019). Rights: access, correction, erasure. Consent for personal data processing. Significant data fiduciaries (higher obligations). Data Protection Board of India (adjudication). Rules under drafting (2024).
India's largest nuclear power plant is at:
Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu, 2000 MW capacity, 6000 MW planned)

Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant (KKNPP, Tamil Nadu): largest in India. Built with Russian collaboration (VVER-1000 reactors). 2 units (2000 MW, operational). 4 more units under construction (6000 MW total when complete). Mapped to 3-stage nuclear program. Coastal (Gulf of Mannar). Controversies (local protests). Commissioned 2013 (Unit 1), 2016 (Unit 2).
Stem cell therapy is approved in India for:

Stem cells: undifferentiated cells. Therapies: leukemia (bone marrow transplant), sickle cell, thalassemia. Regenerative: spinal cord injury, diabetes (clinical trials). India: ICMR guidelines. Approved: bone marrow transplant (oncology, hematology). Other uses: clinical trials only. Ethics: embryonic stem cells controversial.
Project 75 (Scorpene submarines) is being built by:

Project 75: 6 Scorpene-class diesel-electric submarines. Built by Mazagon Dock Limited (MDL, Mumbai) with French Naval Group (formerly DCNS). Kalvari, Khanderi, Karanj, Vela, Vagsheer (commissioned 2023). 6th: Vagsheer. ~₹23,000 crore. Conventional submarines. Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) to be added later. Project 75I: 6 more (Pipavav - L&T selected 2023).
ISRO Telemetry, Tracking + Command Network (ISTRAC) is at:

ISTRAC: Bengaluru. ISRO's mission control + tracking network. Provides ground stations for satellite control. Stations: Bengaluru, Lucknow, Sriharikota, Port Blair, Thiruvananthapuram. Also: Brunei, Biak (Indonesia). Mission Control Centre (MCC) + Launch Control Centre (LCC) for space missions.
Internet subscribers in India (2024) are approximately:

Internet India (TRAI, 2024): ~936 million subscribers (broadband). Wireless: ~880 million. Wireline: ~40 million. Mobile internet: dominant. ~50% urban, ~30% rural penetration. Top ISPs: Jio, Airtel, VI, BSNL. Mobile-first country. BharatNet: ~2 lakh gram panchayats connected. ~₹100-500/month data plans.
Council of Scientific + Industrial Research (CSIR) was established in:

CSIR (26 September 1942): established. HQ New Delhi. Largest publicly funded R&D organization in India. 37 national labs, 39 centres. Director General: N Kalaiselvi (2025, first woman DG). Fields: aerospace (NAL), chemicals (IICT, CLRI), drugs (CDRI), food (CFTRI), mining (CIMFR), genomics (IGIB), oceanography (NIO).

Ethereum (2015, Vitalik Buterin): introduced smart contracts. Turing-complete programming language (Solidity). Decentralized apps (dApps). ERC-20 tokens. ETH cryptocurrency. Transitioned from PoW to PoS (Merge, September 2022) - reduced energy consumption by 99.95%. Other platforms: Solana, Cardano, BSC.
India's first indigenously built nuclear reactor is:

Apsara: India's first nuclear reactor (4 August 1956, BARC Trombay). Swimming pool type, 1 MW. Designed + built by Indians. Used for research. Decommissioned 2009, restart 2018 as Apsara-U. Other reactors: Cirus (Canada-India, 1960), Dhruva (1985).
Blockchain technology was first described in:

Blockchain: Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudonym, real identity unknown) described in Bitcoin whitepaper (October 2008). 'Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System'. Genesis block (3 January 2009). Distributed ledger: blocks chained cryptographically. Decentralized, immutable. Smart contracts (Ethereum 2015). India: RBI exploring CBDC. Crypto regulated by PMLA.
Hydroelectric capacity of India is approximately:

Hydroelectric (2024): ~47 GW (large + small hydro ~5 GW = ~52 GW total). Top states: Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu (pumped hydro). Largest plant: Koyna (Maharashtra, 1960 MW). Bhakra Nangal (Punjab), Nathpa Jhakri (Himachal). Hydro share: ~12% of total installed capacity (~440 GW). Pumped storage: ~5 GW. North East potential untapped.

Aditya-L1 (2 September 2023): India's first solar mission. Halo orbit around L1 Lagrangian point (~1.5 million km from Earth, between Earth and Sun). 7 payloads - study solar corona, photosphere, chromosphere, CMEs. ISRO launched on PSLV-C57.
S-400 Triumf missile system was purchased from:

S-400 Triumf (NATO: SA-21 Growler): Russian long-range surface-to-air missile system. India: 5 regiments (~$5.4 billion, October 2018). 3 delivered (2024). Range: 40-400 km. Targets: aircraft, missiles, drones. CAATSA sanctions: USA threatened, India went ahead. 5th gen fighter-like capabilities.

Prasar Bharati (India's Public Service Broadcasting): established 23 November 1997 (Prasar Bharati Act 1990). Doordarshan (TV, started 15 September 1959), All India Radio (AIR, 1936). 1000+ TV transmitters, 415 AIR stations. 12 Indian + 11 foreign languages. 'Free to air'. Chairman: Navneet Kumar Sehgal (2024).
The National Supercomputing Mission aims to install how many supercomputers?

NSM (2015, ₹4500 crore): install 70+ supercomputers (~70 PetaFLOPs) by 2025. Steered by MeitY + DST. Implemented by C-DAC + IISc Bangalore. Phase I-III completed. Param Siddhi-AI (AI-specific, 210 AI-PF). 'Make in India' supercomputers.
Protein subunit COVID vaccine (India, Biological E)

Corbevax (Biological E. Limited, Hyderabad): protein subunit COVID-19 vaccine. Receptor-binding domain (RBD) of spike protein. Adjuvant: CpG 1018 + alum. Approved emergency use India (December 2021). For 12+ age group. ~₹400/dose (cheaper). WHO approved emergency use (June 2022). Technology from Baylor College of Medicine (Texas Children's Hospital - patent-free).
Electric Vehicles (EVs) use which type of battery?

EV batteries: mostly Li-ion (high energy density, rechargeable). Other types in development: solid-state, sodium-ion. India EV market growing rapidly - 2-wheelers (Ola, Ather), 4-wheelers (Tata, Mahindra). FAME-II scheme (₹10,000 crore), PLI for ACC batteries.
Spectrum auction in India is conducted by:

Spectrum auctions: DoT conducts. TRAI recommends reserve prices. TDSAT (Telecom Disputes Settlement + Appellate Tribunal) - appellate body. Last major auction: August 2022 (5G, ~₹1.5 lakh crore). Jio, Airtel, Vi. Spectrum bands: 700 MHz, 800 MHz, 900 MHz, 1800 MHz, 2100 MHz, 2300 MHz, 2500 MHz, 3300 MHz, 26 GHz.
INS Vikramaditya was acquired from which country?

INS Vikramaditya (commissioned 16 November 2013): acquired from Russia. Originally Baku/Admiral Gorshkov (Kiev class). Free transfer; ~$2.35 billion refit cost. STOBAR configuration. ~45,000 tonnes. 26 MiG-29K fighters. Homeport: Karwar (Karnataka). India's only operational carrier till INS Vikrant 2022.
Quantum computing uses which unit of computation?

Quantum computer: uses qubits (quantum bits). Superposition (0+1 simultaneously), entanglement (correlated qubits). Exponential speed for some problems. India's National Quantum Mission (April 2023, ₹6000 crore). IBM, Google, Microsoft, IonQ leaders.
Geothermal energy potential in India is highest at:

Geothermal potential India: ~10,000 MW. Major sites: Puga Valley (Ladakh), Tattapani (Chhattisgarh), Manikaran (Himachal), Surajkund (Jharkhand), Cambay (Gujarat). ONGC pilot project at Puga (Ladakh, 2022). Estimated ~1000 MW potential at Puga. Mostly untapped. Drilling challenges.
Stem cells are unique because they:
Are found only in bone marrow
Can differentiate into various cell types

Stem cells: undifferentiated cells that can self-renew and differentiate. Types: embryonic (pluripotent, can become any cell), adult (multipotent, like bone marrow HSCs), induced pluripotent (iPSCs, reprogrammed adult cells). Uses: leukemia, regenerative medicine.

DNA fingerprinting: developed by Sir Alec Jeffreys (University of Leicester, 1984). Uses variable number tandem repeats (VNTRs). Each person's pattern unique (except identical twins). Used in: paternity disputes, criminal investigations, identifying remains.
Green Hydrogen Mission was launched in:

National Green Hydrogen Mission (4 January 2023): ₹19,744 crore (2022-32). Target: 5 MMT (million metric tonnes) green H₂ production by 2030. Reduces ₹1 lakh crore+ fossil fuel imports. Reduces 50 MMT CO2 emissions/year. Sectors: refineries, fertilizer, steel, mobility. MNRE implements. PLI for electrolyzer manufacturing.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) was first conceptualized by:

Alan Turing (1950, 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence'): introduced 'Turing Test' for AI - can machine think? 'Imitation Game'. Term 'Artificial Intelligence' coined by John McCarthy (1956, Dartmouth Conference). Early AI: 1950s-70s. AI winters (1974-80, 1987-93). Modern AI: deep learning, neural networks.
Indian Genome Project (also called GenomeIndia) aims to sequence:

GenomeIndia: launched January 2020, ₹150 crore. Sequenced 10,000 Indian genomes (April 2024). 20 institutions. Data available to researchers. Useful for: personalized medicine, disease prediction, drug development. ~80% of genetic variations in Indian population are unique (founder effects, endogamy).
National Quantum Mission (NQM) was approved in:

NQM (19 April 2023, ₹6003.65 crore, 2023-31): develop quantum computers (20-50 qubits by 2026, 50-1000 qubits by 2031). Quantum communications (2000 km). Quantum random number generation. Quantum sensing + metrology. Quantum materials. DST (Department of Science + Technology) implements. Hub-and-spoke model.
CAR-T cell therapy (Chimeric Antigen Receptor) is for:

CAR-T cell therapy: genetically modifies patient's T-cells to target cancer. Approved: Novartis Kymriah (2017, USA), Gilead Yescarta. India: NexCAR19 (ImmunoACT, 2023) - indigenous, ~₹30-40 lakh (vs ~$400,000 abroad). Treats: B-cell lymphoma, leukemia. 'Living drug'. Side effects: cytokine release syndrome.
Artificial Intelligence (AI) is best described as:

AI: development of computer systems performing tasks requiring human intelligence - reasoning, learning, problem-solving, perception, language understanding. Types: Narrow (ANI), General (AGI), Super (ASI). Subfields: ML, DL, NLP, Computer Vision, Robotics.
AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft) is India's:

AMCA: 5th generation stealth fighter (under development). ADA + HAL. Twin-engine, all-weather. First flight: ~2025-26 target. Induction: ~2032-35. Features: stealth, supercruise, advanced avionics. ~₹15,000 crore project. India's first indigenous stealth fighter.
Digital Rupee (CBDC) pilot was launched by RBI in:

Digital Rupee (e₹): RBI's Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). Wholesale (e₹-W): launched 1 November 2022 (govt bonds settlement). Retail (e₹-R): launched 1 December 2022 (8 cities). Different from UPI + cryptocurrencies. Legal tender. Backed by RBI. Anonymity for small transactions. Now in 16+ cities (2024).

SAC: Ahmedabad. Develops space applications - meteorology, remote sensing, satellite communication, geo-information systems. Instruments for Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan, INSAT, GSAT. Indian National Satellite system (INSAT) meteorological payloads. Bhaskara (1979, 1981) - early experimental Earth observation satellites.
Tehri Dam is on which river?

Tehri Dam (Uttarakhand): on Bhagirathi river (one of Ganga's source rivers). ~260.5m high (tallest dam in India). Earth + rockfill dam. Commissioned 2006. Power: 1000 MW (later 400 MW added - 2400 MW planned total). Reservoir: 42 sq km. Displaced ~100,000 people. Controversial (Himalayan ecology, earthquake risk).

Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana (PMBJP, 2008, expanded 2015): generic medicines at 50-90% discount. ~10,000+ Jan Aushadhi Kendras (2024). ~2000 medicines + surgical items. BPPI (Bureau of Pharma PSUs of India) implements. Saves ~₹5000+ crore annually to citizens. Available: all therapeutic categories. ~₹1 lakh crore savings (cumulative).

Aryabhata: launched 19 April 1975 by Soviet Kosmos-3M from Kapustin Yar. Named after mathematician Aryabhata. Built by ISRO. Orbited for ~17 years. 26 April 1975 reentry. Marked beginning of Indian space program.

ChatGPT (30 November 2022): OpenAI's chatbot based on GPT-3.5. Reached 1 million users in 5 days, 100 million in 2 months (fastest ever). Sparked AI race. GPT-4 (March 2023), GPT-4 Turbo (Nov 2023), GPT-4o (May 2024), GPT-4o mini (July 2024), o1, o3 (2024-25). Competitors: Claude (Anthropic), Gemini (Google), LLaMA (Meta).

INS Chakra: Akula-class nuclear attack submarine (SSN). Leased from Russia. INS Chakra I (1988-1991): first Indian nuclear sub. INS Chakra II (2012-2021): returned to Russia. INS Chakra III: Akula class, leased 2025 for 10 years (~$3 billion deal). India building own SSN (under Project 77).
Smallpox was eradicated in which year (WHO certified)?

Smallpox eradication: WHO declared 8 May 1980. Last natural case: 26 October 1977 (Ali Maow Maalin, Somalia, survived). Last death: Janet Parker (1978, lab accident, Birmingham UK). Edward Jenner: smallpox vaccine (1796, cowpox). 10-year WHO eradication campaign (1967-77, ~$300 million). Only human disease eradicated. Samples kept: CDC (USA), VECTOR (Russia).

Prithvi (named after Hindu goddess of earth): short-range ballistic missile. Variants: P-I (army, 150 km), P-II (air force, 250 km), P-III (navy, 350 km), Dhanush (naval, 350-600 km). Liquid-fueled. Indigenous. Can carry nuclear/conventional warheads. Project Devil (1970s) - precursor.
SSLV (Small Satellite Launch Vehicle) is for:

SSLV: ISRO's smallest rocket. ~34m tall, 120 tonne, can carry 500 kg to LEO / 300 kg to SSO. First developmental flight (7 Aug 2022) - partial failure. First successful (10 Feb 2023 - EOS-07). Low-cost (~₹10-30 crore), quick turnaround (72 hours).

Penicillin: discovered by Alexander Fleming (September 1928, St Mary's Hospital London). From Penicillium notatum mold. Mass production: Howard Florey + Ernst Chain (Oxford, WWII). First antibiotic. Saved millions. Nobel 1945 (Fleming + Florey + Chain). Antibiotic resistance now major threat (AMR - 'silent pandemic').
Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine was developed by:

Sputnik V (Gam-COVID-Vac): Russian COVID-19 vaccine. Gamaleya Research Institute (Moscow). First registered COVID-19 vaccine (11 August 2020 - before Phase III trials complete). Adenoviral vector (Ad26 + Ad5 - 2 doses). 91.6% efficacy (Lancet). India: Dr Reddy's manufactured. ~75 countries approved. Russian domestic use.
HAL Dhruv (Advanced Light Helicopter - ALH) is:

Dhruv (ALH): multirole twin-engine helicopter. HAL designed + built. ~6 tonne. Variants: Mk I/II/III/IV. Used by Army, Air Force, Navy, Coast Guard, civil. ~330 produced (2024). ~80% indigenous. Rudra (ALH-WSI): armed variant. Prachand (LCH - Light Combat Helicopter): derived from ALH.
FAME-II (Faster Adoption + Manufacturing of Hybrid + Electric Vehicles) scheme had outlay of:

FAME-II (April 2019, 5 years, ₹10,000 crore): subsidies for EVs. 7000 e-buses, 5 lakh e-3W, 55000 e-4W passenger + 10 lakh e-2W. Charging infrastructure (~3000 stations). 80% budget for demand incentives. Ended March 2024 (extended). Replaced by EMPS (Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme, ₹500 crore, 2024).
NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) satellite is for:

NISAR: joint NASA-ISRO mission. Launch: 2025. Cost ~$1.5 billion. World's most expensive Earth observation satellite. Studies: ecosystems, ice, earthquakes, volcanoes, sea level rise. L-band (NASA) + S-band (ISRO) SAR. 12-day repeat cycle.
Largest solar power plant in world is:

Bhadla Solar Park (Jodhpur, Rajasthan): world's largest solar park. ~2245 MW capacity. Spread over 14,000 acres. Phased: 2015-2020. ₹10,000 crore investment. Hot region (~50°C). Other large: Pavagada (Karnataka, 2050 MW), Kurnool (Andhra, 1000 MW), Charanka (Gujarat, 730 MW).
Bt cotton is India's only approved GM crop. What does Bt stand for?

Bt cotton (2002 approved): contains gene from Bacillus thuringiensis (soil bacterium). Produces Bt toxin (Cry protein) - kills cotton bollworm. Reduces pesticide use. India: ~95% of cotton area is Bt. Controversies: yields plateau, farmer suicides, Monsanto monopoly. Other GM: Bt brinjal (moratorium 2010), GM mustard (DMH-11, approved 2022 - contested).

BharatNet (2011, earlier NOFN): connect 2.5 lakh Gram Panchayats with broadband. Originally target 2015, extended. ~2 lakh GPs connected (2024, optic fibre). ~6 lakh km OFC laid. Fibre-to-the-Home (FTTH) extended to ~6 lakh villages (Aug 2024). Modes: State-led, CPS, PPP. ~₹40,000 crore spent. CSCs, WiFi hotspots at GPs.
DNA fingerprinting in India was first used in:

DNA fingerprinting India: Dr. Lalji Singh ('Father of Indian DNA fingerprinting'). CCMB Hyderabad. First used: 1988 Calcutta HC paternity dispute. Famous: Rajiv Gandhi assassination (1991, identified remains). Nithari killings (2006). Aarushi Talwar case (2008). DNA Technology (Use + Application) Regulation Bill - pending.

Antrix (1992, Bengaluru): commercial arm of ISRO. Markets ISRO's services (launch services, satellite leasing, remote sensing data). PSLV commercial launches (foreign satellites). Earned ~₹500 crore/year. Recent: New Space India Limited (NSIL, 2019) - another commercial arm, owns satellites, launches them.
Cloud computing model where user pays per use is:

Cloud computing: on-demand IT resources over internet. Models: IaaS (Infrastructure - AWS EC2), PaaS (Platform - Heroku), SaaS (Software - Gmail, Office 365). Deployment: Public (AWS, Azure, GCP), Private, Hybrid. Pricing: pay-as-you-go, reserved, spot. India: AWS Mumbai (2016), Azure (multiple), Jio Cloud, ESDS. Hybrid cloud: most common.

ISO 27001: international standard for Information Security Management System (ISMS). Risk-based approach. Controls: 114 in Annex A. Certifies organizations handling sensitive data. India: RBI mandates for banks. CERT-In empanelled auditors. Companion: ISO 27002 (code of practice), 27017 (cloud security), 27018 (PII in cloud).
Aadhaar was launched as a 12-digit unique identity number in:

Aadhaar: launched 28 January 2009 (UIDAI formed). 12-digit unique identity number. First Aadhaar: 29 September 2010 (Ranjana Sonawane, Maharashtra). Nandan Nilekani first Chairman. Now world's largest biometric ID system (>135 crore). Free. SC upheld (2018). Used for: DBT, banking, mobile, PAN, passport, voter ID.
Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY was launched on:

PM-JAY (PM Jan Arogya Yojana, 23 Sep 2018): world's largest govt-funded health insurance. ₹5 lakh per family per year. Covers 10.74 crore families (bottom 40% based on SECC 2011). Free secondary + tertiary care at empanelled hospitals. Cashless. ~7 crore treatments given (2024). ~30 crore beneficiary cards (2024). New expansion: seniors 70+ (2024).
mRNA vaccine technology was first widely used for:

mRNA vaccines: Pfizer-BioNTech + Moderna (2020, COVID-19). Lipid nanoparticle delivers mRNA into cells. Cells produce spike protein - immune response. Quick development (1 year, fastest vaccine ever). Earlier research: Katalin Karikó + Drew Weissman (Nobel Medicine 2023). Future: cancer, HIV, malaria (under development). Cold chain: -70°C (Pfizer), -20°C (Moderna).
C-17 Globemaster III is used by Indian Air Force as:

C-17 Globemaster III (Boeing): strategic airlift aircraft. IAF: 10 (purchased 2011-2014, ~$4.1 billion). Heavy cargo (77 tonnes), paratroopers, vehicles, humanitarian missions. Homebase: Hindon (Ghaziabad). Replaced IL-76 (Russian). Used in evacuation (Afghanistan 2021, Sudan 2023, Ukraine 2022).

Akash (means 'sky' in Sanskrit): medium-range mobile SAM. Range 25-45 km. Multi-target capability. 3 missiles per launcher. Radars: Rajendra (tracking). Can engage aircraft, helicopters, UAVs, missiles. Air Force + Army versions. Exported to Armenia (2023, ~$230 million). 96% indigenous.
BrahMos missile is jointly developed by India and:

BrahMos: supersonic cruise missile. Joint venture: India (DRDO) + Russia (NPO Mashinostroyenia). Named after rivers Brahmaputra + Moskva. Speed: Mach 2.8-3.0 (~3700 km/h). Range: 290-800 km. Variants: land, air, ship, sub-launched.

Golden Rice: genetically engineered to produce β-carotene (precursor of Vitamin A) in endosperm. Combats vitamin A deficiency (blindness). Ingo Potrykus + Peter Beyer (1999). Philippines approved in 2021 (first country). India: not approved.

ISRO HQ: Bengaluru (Antariksh Bhavan). Chairman: V. Narayanan (2025). Founded 15 August 1969 (INCOSPAR earlier in 1962). First chairman: Vikram Sarabhai ('father of Indian space program'). ISRO under Department of Space (PM as minister in-charge).
5G technology was commercially launched in India on:

5G India launch: 1 October 2022 (PM Modi at IMC 2022). Airtel + Jio first. Coverage: all major cities + many towns (2024). Speed: 100 Mbps - 1 Gbps (vs 4G ~10-50 Mbps). Latency: 1 ms (vs 4G 50 ms). Use cases: eMBB (broadband), URLLC (autonomous vehicles, industrial IoT), mMTC (smart cities, IoT). 6G target: 2030.
Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) is at:

PFBR (Bhavini, Kalpakkam): India's first fast breeder reactor (500 MW). Built by Bhartiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam (BHAVINI). Criticality achieved 2024. Uses Pu-239 + U-238. Breeds more fuel than consumes. Stage 2 of Bhabha's 3-stage program. ~₹5,600 crore. Delayed ~10 years. Two more PFBRs planned (500 MW each).
Defense exports of India (2023-24) were approximately:

Defence exports 2023-24: ₹21,083 crore (record, ~$2.6 billion). From ₹686 crore (2013-14) - 30x increase. 100+ Indian companies exporting. To 85+ countries. Products: BrahMos (Philippines), Pinaka (Armenia), Akash (Armenia), Tejas, Kalyani artillery. Target: ₹50,000 crore by 2028-29.
Tarapur Atomic Power Station (TAPS) was India's first nuclear power plant. Commercial operation began in:

TAPS (Tarapur, Maharashtra): India's first nuclear power plant. 2 BWR reactors (160 MW each). Commercial: 28 October 1969. Built by USA (GE). Later TAPS-3, 4 (PHWR, 540 MW each, 2006). Oldest operating nuclear power plant. Under IAEA safeguards. Tarapur Atomic Power Station 1+2 = 320 MW total.
Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) is used for:

QKD: secure cryptographic key distribution using quantum mechanics. Eavesdropping detected (Heisenberg uncertainty). BB84 protocol (Bennett + Brassard, 1984). India: 1st inter-city QKD link between Delhi and Vadodara (2022, ~1150 km, DRDO). Used for: defence, banking, government communication. Unbreakable (in principle).
Private sector participation in all space activities

Indian Space Policy (April 2023): enables private sector. ISRO focuses on R&D + deep space. New Space India Limited (NSIL, 2019): govt PSU for commercial operations. IN-SPACe (2020): regulates + promotes private. Indian National Space Promotion + Authorization Centre. Skyroot Aerospace (first private launch - Vikram-S, Nov 2022).
TrueNat test for COVID-19 was originally developed for:

TrueNat: originally developed by Molbio Diagnostics (Goa) for TB detection (2016). Repurposed for COVID-19 (May 2020, ICMR approved). Portable, battery-operated. Results in 60 mins. Used in rural areas (no labs). CSIR-IGIB collaborated. Capacity: 1000+ tests/day. India's first point-of-care molecular test.

Astra (means 'weapon' in Sanskrit): beyond visual range air-to-air missile (BVRAAM). Range: 80-110 km (Astra Mk 1), 160 km (Mk 2 in development). All-weather, day/night. Solid-fueled. Integrated on Su-30MKI, Tejas, MiG-29. ~6.5 m long, 154 kg. ~90% indigenous. Export orders.
Genome sequencing means determining the order of:
Nucleotides (A, T, G, C) in DNA

Genome sequencing: determining the order of nucleotides (A-Adenine, T-Thymine, G-Guanine, C-Cytosine) in DNA. Human Genome Project (1990-2003): first complete human genome (~3 billion base pairs, ~20,000-25,000 genes). Next Generation Sequencing (NGS): faster, cheaper. ~$200/genome (2024, vs $3 billion in 2003). India: GenomeIndia (10,000 genomes completed 2024).
CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing technology was awarded Nobel Prize in:

CRISPR-Cas9 (Nobel Chemistry 2020): Jennifer Doudna (USA) + Emmanuelle Charpentier (France). Bacterial immune system. Targets specific DNA sequence - cuts, edits. Applications: sickle cell disease (Casgevy approved 2023), cancer immunotherapy, agriculture, livestock. Ethics: human embryo editing (He Jiankui controversy 2018).
Tejas is which type of aircraft?

Tejas: India's indigenous LCA. Single-engine, multirole, delta wing. Designed by Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA), built by HAL. Mark 1A inducted by IAF (March 2024). Navy variant (LCA Navy) tested. Mark 2 in development. Replacing MiG-21.
Trishul missile (named after Shiva's trident) is:

Trishul: short-range SAM (9 km). Developed 1983-2008. Project closed 2008 (technological obsolescence). Replaced by Akash + SpyDer (Israel). Quick Reaction SAM (QRSAM) - newer indigenous system. Trishul lessons learned used in Akash + other projects.
Indian pharmaceutical industry is world's largest by:

India pharma: world's largest by volume (~20% global generics), 3rd largest by value (~$50 billion). 'Pharmacy of the world'. Top generic suppliers: Sun Pharma, Dr Reddy's, Cipla, Lupin, Aurobindo. Vaccines: Serum Institute (world's largest). ~60% of global vaccine production. Exports to 200+ countries. ~$25 billion exports (2023-24).

Balakot airstrike (26 Feb 2019): IAF Mirage 2000 jets crossed LoC, struck Jaish-e-Mohammed training camp at Balakot, Pakistan. Response to Pulwama attack (14 Feb 2019, 40 CRPF killed). Next day: dogfight, Wing Commander Abhinandan captured, returned.

Phishing: fraudulent emails/messages trick users into revealing sensitive info (passwords, OTPs, credit cards). Variants: Spear phishing (targeted), Whaling (executives), Vishing (voice), Smishing (SMS). India: high incidents (cyber crime up 5x in 5 years). CERT-In (Computer Emergency Response Team India). Anti-phishing: awareness, MFA, DMARC, antispam.
Press Council of India (PCI) was established in:

PCI (Press Council Act 1965, established 1966): quasi-judicial body. Regulates print media ethics. 28 members (chairman + 27). 3-year term. Chairman: Ranjana Prakash Desai (2022-25). Cannot penalize (advisory only). Press freedom - 2nd most free in South Asia after Nepal (Reporters Without Borders 2024). India rank: 159/180 (2024, dropped).
Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) is at:

I4C (Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre): MHA. Established 2018. ₹415 crore scheme. Components: National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit, National Cyber Crime Reporting, National Cyber Crime Training, National Cyber Crime Ecosystem Management. Cyberdost handle (@Cyberdost). 1930 helpline (cyber fraud reporting). National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP).
Aadhaar Act 2016 was upheld by Supreme Court in:

Justice K.S. Puttaswamy vs Union of India (September 2018, 5-judge bench): upheld Aadhaar Act 2016 as constitutional. But: struck down Section 57 (private entity use). Restricted mandatory linking to: PAN, bank account, mobile. Not mandatory for: school admissions, CBSE NEET, etc. Recognized Right to Privacy as fundamental right (Puttaswamy I, August 2017).
Quantum supremacy was first claimed by:

Quantum supremacy: Google claimed (October 2019, Nature paper). Sycamore processor (53 qubits) solved in 200 seconds what classical would take 10,000 years (claimed). IBM disputed (could be 2.5 days with classical). China (Jiuzhang photonic, December 2020, ~200 seconds vs billions of years for classical). Quantum advantage: practical uses beyond supremacy.
India's first 5G lab was set up at:

IIT Madras 5G Testbed: India's first indigenous 5G testbed. ₹230 crore project. 8 IITs (Madras lead). Completed June 2022. Allows startups, industry to test 5G products. Enables: 5G networks, IoT, smart manufacturing. Reduced 5G rollout cost. 'Make in India' boost. Tata Teleservices, Reliance Jio used.
Tidal energy potential in India is highest at:
Gulf of Khambhat + Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat)

Tidal energy: India potential ~12,500 MW. Top sites: Gulf of Khambhat (~7000 MW), Gulf of Kutch (~1200 MW), Sundarbans (~100 MW), Hooghly (~300 MW). First tidal power plant: planned at Mandavi (Gujarat, 50 MW). Demonstrator: Durgaduani Creek (Sundarbans, 3.75 MW). Costly + ecological concerns. Mostly untapped.
Green Hydrogen is hydrogen produced using:

Green Hydrogen: produced by electrolysis of water using renewable electricity. No CO2 emissions. India's National Green Hydrogen Mission (Jan 2023, ₹19,744 crore): 5 MMT production by 2030. Other types: Grey (fossil), Blue (fossil + CCS), Pink (nuclear).
Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) is at:

VSSC: Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala. Major ISRO centre. Named after Vikram Sarabhai (ISRO founder). Develops launch vehicles (PSLV, GSLV, LVM3, RLV). Facilities: rocket launchers, propellants, sounding rockets. Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS, 1963) - first ISRO facility, near VSSC.

LCA Tejas: designed by ADA (Aeronautical Development Agency, Bengaluru, 1984). Built by HAL (Hindustan Aeronautics Limited). Light Combat Aircraft (4.5 generation). Single-engine, delta wing. Mk 1A inducted March 2024. Navy variant (LCA Navy) tested. Mk 2 in development (medium weight fighter, GE F414 engine).
Cybersecurity attacks where attacker locks files + demands ransom are called:

Ransomware: malware encrypts victim's files, demands ransom (usually cryptocurrency). Famous: WannaCry (May 2017, 200,000+ systems in 150 countries), Petya/NotPetya (2017). Recent: Colonial Pipeline (USA 2021, paid $4.4M), AIIMS Delhi (2022), Kaseya. Prevention: backups, patches, employee training, antivirus, network segmentation.
Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) is operational name:

NavIC (formerly IRNSS): 7 satellites (3 GEO + 4 GSO). Coverage: India + 1500 km beyond. Operational since 2018. 8th satellite (NVS-01) launched May 2023. Accuracy: better than GPS in India. Used in vehicle trackers, fishing boats, emergency services. Free for civilian use. ~₹1,400 crore cost. NavIC-based watches released.
Chinook CH-47F helicopters are used for:

Chinook CH-47F (I): Boeing tandem rotor heavy-lift helicopter. IAF: 15 (2019-2020). ~₹6,000 crore. Used in: Siachen (high altitude), Leh-Ladakh, helicopter operations. Cargo (10 tonnes), troops (33-55). Replaces Mi-26. Crucial for Himalayan border (China) logistics.
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) was established in:

TRAI: established 20 February 1997 (TRAI Act). HQ New Delhi. Chairman: Anil Kumar Lahoti (2025). Regulates: tariffs, interconnection, quality of service, mobile number portability. Recommends: spectrum auction, licensing, mergers. TDSAT (Telecom Disputes Settlement + Appellate Tribunal) - appellate body (2000). Trai amends Act 2000.
India's largest solar power plant is:

Bhadla Solar Park (Jodhpur, Rajasthan): world's largest solar park, ~2245 MW capacity. Spread over 14,000 acres. Other major: Pavagada (Karnataka, 2050 MW), Kurnool (Andhra, 1000 MW), Charanka (Gujarat, 730 MW). India: 5th largest solar globally.
The 'Surgical Strike' of 2016 was conducted by:

Surgical Strikes (28-29 September 2016): Indian Army Special Forces (Para SF) conducted across Line of Control (PoK) against terrorist launch pads. Response to Uri attack (18 Sep 2016, 19 soldiers killed). 7 launch pads destroyed in 4-5 km deep.
India's first AI supercomputer is named:

PARAM Siddhi-AI (2020): India's first AI supercomputer. C-DAC developed. 210 AI PetaFLOPS (PF). 62nd fastest in world (Top500, Nov 2020). Used for: NLP, computer vision, weather, healthcare. 'National Supercomputing Mission' (2015, ₹4500 crore) - 70+ supercomputers (~70 PF) target.

NavIC (formerly IRNSS - Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System): 7 satellites (3 GEO + 4 GSO). Operational since 2018. Coverage: India + 1500 km beyond. 8th satellite (NVS-01) launched May 2023. Alternative to GPS. Used in vehicle trackers,渔民.

Bitcoin (BTC): created by Satoshi Nakamoto (pseudonym, real identity unknown). Genesis block mined 3 January 2009. First BTC transaction: 12 BTC to Hal Finney (12 January 2009). 21 million total supply (capped). Halving: every 4 years (next April 2028). Last BTC ~2140. Satoshi disappeared 2010-11. Elon Musk denied being Satoshi.

Gaganyaan (approved 2018): India's first human spaceflight. 3-member crew to LEO (Low Earth Orbit, 400 km) for 3 days. Test missions: TV-D1, TV-D2 (abort tests successful). Target: 2025-26. India to be 4th country with human spaceflight capability.

Polio vaccines: 1) Salk (IPV, injectable, inactivated virus, 1955), 2) Sabin (OPV, oral, attenuated virus, 1961). Sabin OPV: more common globally (easier, cheaper, herd immunity). India: Pulse Polio programme (1995). India polio-free: 13 January 2011 (last case, West Bengal). WHO certified India polio-free 2014. OPV used in India.
COVID-19 pandemic was declared by WHO on:

COVID-19: WHO declared Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) 30 January 2020. Pandemic 11 March 2020. Originated Wuhan, China (December 2019). SARS-CoV-2 virus. ~7 million deaths officially, ~20 million estimated (excess mortality). India lockdown: 25 March 2020. Vaccines: Covishield, Covaxin, Corbevax, Sputnik V. WHO declared end of emergency 5 May 2023.
5G technology offers which speed improvement over 4G?

5G vs 4G: 5G ~10 Gbps peak (vs 4G ~100 Mbps). Latency: 1 ms (5G) vs 50 ms (4G). Use cases: eMBB (broadband), URLLC (autonomous vehicles), mMTC (IoT). 5G launched in India October 2022 (Jio + Airtel). 6G expected by 2030.
Sardar Sarovar Dam is on which river?

Sardar Sarovar Dam (Gujarat): on Narmada river. ~163m high. Concrete gravity dam. Commissioned 2017 (PM Modi). Power: 1450 MW (River Bed Power House + Canal Head Power House). Irrigation: 18 lakh hectares (Gujarat), drinking water to 4 crore people (Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra, MP). Narmada Bachao Andolan (Medha Patkar, NBA) protested.
The first test-tube baby in India was:

India's first IVF baby: Kanupriya Agarwal (alias Durga), born 3 October 1978 in Kolkata. Developed by Dr. Subhash Mukhopadhyay (1931-1981) - recognition came posthumously. World's first IVF: Louise Brown (UK, 25 July 1978).
Insulin production through recombinant DNA technology was first commercialized by:

Recombinant human insulin: 1978 Genentech developed, 1982 Eli Lilly commercialized (Humulin). First genetically engineered product. Used bacteria (E. coli) to produce human insulin. Replaced animal insulin (pigs, cows - allergies, supply issues). India: Biocon, Wockhardt, Lupin produce. ~150 million diabetics globally.
Solar capacity of India (2024) is approximately:

Solar capacity (Oct 2024): ~85 GW (achieved). Target 100 GW by 2022 (revised to 2026). Largest solar parks: Bhadla (Rajasthan, 2245 MW - world's largest), Pavagada (Karnataka, 2050 MW), Kurnool (1000 MW). Rooftop: ~10 GW. India: 5th largest solar globally. Target: 280 GW by 2030. 500 GW non-fossil by 2030.
Lithium-ion battery manufacturing in India is supported by PLI scheme worth:

PLI for ACC (Advanced Chemistry Cell) battery manufacturing: ₹18,100 crore. 50 GWh capacity (5-year). Bidders: Reliance, Ola, Exide, Amara Raja, Tata Chemicals. Target: reduce imports (~$2 billion/year), EV ecosystem. 5 GWh reserved for niche technologies. Ola's Gigafactory (Tamil Nadu, 100 GWh planned).
UPI (Unified Payments Interface) was launched by:

UPI (11 April 2016): launched by NPCI (National Payments Corporation of India). Built on IMPS infrastructure. Real-time inter-bank transfer (24x7). Apps: BHIM, Google Pay, PhonePe, Paytm. ~16 billion transactions/month (Sept 2024, ~₹20 lakh crore). Adopted in: Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, France (Eiffel Tower), UAE, Singapore, Mauritius.
PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle) is mainly used for:
Launching Earth observation + small satellites to polar orbits

PSLV: ISRO's most reliable rocket. ~60 launches (1993-2024, 4 failures). Capacity: 1750 kg to 622 km SSO. Variants: PSLV-CA, PSLV-G, PSLV-XL. Famous missions: Chandrayaan-1 (2008), Mangalyaan (2013). Workhorse for small + medium satellites. PSLV-C37 (Feb 2017): launched 104 satellites (record).
Indian Genome Project (Indian Genomic Variation Database) was launched in:

IGV project: 2003 (CSIR-led). Studied genetic diversity across Indian populations. GenomeIndia Project (2020, ₹150 crore): sequence 10,000 Indian genomes. April 2024: 10,000 genomes completed, available to researchers. Personalized medicine applications.

INS Arihant (commissioned August 2016): India's first nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN). Built under Advanced Technology Vessel (ATV) project. 6000 tonne. Nuclear reactor: 80 MW. Carries K-15 (Sagarika, 750 km) and K-4 (3500 km) missiles.
CERT-In (Computer Emergency Response Team - India) is under:

CERT-In: national nodal agency for cyber incidents. Established 2004. Under MeitY. Director General: Sanjay Bahl (2024). Coordinates: cyber incident response, early warning, vulnerability notes. Mandates: report cyber incidents within 6 hours (April 2022 directive). VPN providers must keep logs 5 years. ~1.4 million cyber incidents reported 2023.
Agni missile series has how many variants?

Agni series (named after Vedic fire god): Agni-I (700-1250 km), II (2000-3000), III (3500-5000), IV (4000), V (5000-5500+ km, ICBM), VI (under development, 10000+ km). Solid-fueled. Can carry nuclear warhead. Agni-P (2021): new variant with new technologies. MIRV tested (April 2024, Agni-V).
Bhakra Nangal Dam is on which river?

Bhakra Nangal: on Sutlej river. Bhakra Dam (Himachal Pradesh) + Nangal Dam (Punjab). ~226m high (Bhakra) - one of world's highest gravity dams. 1963 (commissioned). Power: ~1400 MW (Ganguwal, Kotla). irrigates Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan. 'New Temple of Resurgent India' (Nehru). Largest Indian dam before Tehri (2006).
Prachand (LCH - Light Combat Helicopter) was inducted by IAF in:

Prachand (means 'fierce' in Sanskrit): India's indigenous Light Combat Helicopter (LCH). Inducted October 2022 (Jodhpur, Air Force Day). HAL designed + built. Twin-engine, 5.8 tonne. Capabilities: anti-tank, air-to-air, combat search + rescue. High altitude operations (Siachen). ~150 ordered (IAF + Army).
Kudankulam reactors are of which type?

VVER-1000 (Vodo-Vodyanoi Energetichesky Reaktor): Russian pressurized water reactor. Water-cooled, water-moderated. Kudankulam: 6 units planned (1000 MW each). First criticality: Unit 1 (July 2013). Operational: Units 1+2 (2000 MW). Construction: Units 3-6 (4000 MW, ~₹50,000 crore). IAEA safeguards.
Ayurveda is recognized as alternative medicine system originating in:

Ayurveda ('science of life'): ancient Indian medical system (~5000 years old). Tri-dosha: Vata, Pitta, Kapha. Founders: Charaka (Charaka Samhita, internal medicine), Sushruta (Sushruta Samhita, surgery - 'father of surgery'). AYUSH Ministry (2003, Dept; 2014, Ministry). AYUSH: Ayurveda, Yoga, Unani, Siddha, Sowa-Rigpa, Homoeopathy. WHO collaborating centres.
National Solar Mission aims to achieve how much solar capacity by 2022 (originally)?

Jawaharlal Nehru National Solar Mission (2010): originally 20 GW by 2022. Revised (2015) to 100 GW by 2022. Achieved ~64 GW (2023). 100 GW target by 2022 not met. Mission includes rooftop (40 GW), ground (60 GW). India targets 500 GW non-fossil by 2030.

INSAS (Indian Small Arms System, 5.56mm, 1998): replaced by SIG716i (US, 7.62mm) + AK-203 (India-Russia JV at Korwa, Amethi). ~73,000 SIG716i (signed 2019). 6 lakh+ AK-203 to be made in India. Carbine: JVPC (Joint Venture Protective Carbine, developed by ARDE + Godrej).

Covaxin: India's indigenous COVID-19 vaccine. Developed by Bharat Biotech (Hyderabad) + ICMR (NIV Pune). Whole-virion inactivated. Approved emergency use 3 Jan 2021. Phase III trials showed 77.8% efficacy. Used in India, exported to many countries.
First indigenous COVID-19 testing kit was developed by:

MyLab Discovery Solutions (Pune, March 2020): first indigenous COVID-19 RT-PCR testing kit approved by ICMR. ~₹1200/test (vs ₹4500 imported). Reduced to ~₹200. Founder: Hasmukh Rawal. ~1 crore tests/month capacity. Kit: Pathodetect. India exported testing kits to 100+ countries. Reduced test cost during pandemic.

INS Vikrant (R11, 1961-1997): India's first aircraft carrier. Acquired 1961. Originally HMS Hercules (UK Majestic class). Played key role in 1971 Indo-Pak war. Decommissioned 31 January 1997. Museum ship (till 2012). Scrapped 2014-15. New INS Vikrant (IAC-1): commissioned 2 September 2022 - first indigenous aircraft carrier.
International Yoga Day is celebrated on:

International Day of Yoga: 21 June. UN declared 11 December 2014 (PM Modi's address to UN General Assembly September 2014). First celebrated 21 June 2015. ~190 countries participate. June 21: longest day in Northern Hemisphere (summer solstice). India has 1.5 million+ trained yoga teachers. Svyasa, Isha, Art of Living major yoga institutions.
Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is also called:

IOD: 'Indian Niño'. Difference in sea surface temperature between western (Arabian Sea) + eastern (Bay of Bengal/Indonesia) Indian Ocean. Positive IOD: warmer west → stronger monsoon. Negative IOD: weaker monsoon. Discovered by Saji et al (1999, Nature). Forecasts help monsoon prediction. Independent of ENSO but can amplify/dampen.

Eutrophication: excess nutrients (N, P) from fertilizers, sewage → algal bloom → algae die, decompose → oxygen depletion → fish death, dead zones. Lake restoration: aeration, nutrient removal, biomanipulation. Examples: Lake Erie (North America), Gulf of Mexico dead zone (~15000 sq km), Bengaluru lakes (frequent fires).
National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) targets PM reduction by:

NCAP (January 2019): India's national air quality programme. Original target: 20-30% reduction in PM10 + PM2.5 by 2024 (vs 2017). Revised (September 2022): 40% reduction by 2026. 132 non-attainment cities (didn't meet NAAQS). City-specific action plans. CPCB monitoring. ~₹6000 crore outlay.
El Niño phenomenon affects Indian monsoon by:

El Niño (warm phase ENSO): warming of eastern equatorial Pacific (>0.5°C above normal). Correlates with weaker Indian SW monsoon → drought. La Niña (cold phase): stronger monsoon. ENSO (El Niño Southern Oscillation). IMD monitors Pacific for monsoon forecast. Significant El Niño years: 2002, 2004, 2009, 2014, 2015, 2023.
Greenhouse gases (GHG) cause global warming by:

GHG: allow short-wave solar radiation to pass through but absorb long-wave infrared (heat) re-emitted by Earth's surface → trap heat. Major GHG: CO2 (~76% of warming, ~422 ppm 2024), CH4 (28x CO2 potent), N2O (265x), CFCs (1000s of times). Industrial Revolution: +1.2°C global avg temperature. Paris Agreement: limit to 1.5°C.

Plastic-to-fuel: pyrolysis (thermal decomposition in absence of oxygen). Converts plastic waste to liquid fuel (~700-800 ml/kg plastic). Similar to diesel/petrol. CSIR-IIP Dehradun developed technology. Reduces plastic pollution + provides fuel. Pilots in: Pune, Indore, Bengaluru, Chennai. Scaling up: challenge. Emission concerns if not controlled.

Markhor (Capra falconeri): wild goat with distinctive spiral horns. India: Kashmir (Hemis National Park - Ladakh is wrong, Markhor in Kashmir Valley). Actually: Markhor in J&K - Kazinag NP, Hirpura WLS. Endangered IUCN. Population: ~200-300 in India. State animal of J&K. Threats: poaching, habitat loss.

Carbon neutrality / Net Zero: anthropogenic CO2 emissions = anthropogenic removals (over a period). Achieved by: emission reduction + carbon sequestration (forests, CCS) + carbon offsets. Companies/countries pledge. India 2070, China 2060, EU 2050, USA 2050, Bhutan already carbon negative.
COP (Conference of Parties) is the supreme decision-making body of:
UNFCCC (UN Framework Convention on Climate Change)

COP: supreme body of UNFCCC (1992, Rio Earth Summit). Meets annually. COP21 (Paris, 2015), COP26 (Glasgow, 2021), COP28 (Dubai, 2023 - first global stocktake, fossil fuel phase-down agreed). COP29 (Baku, 2024). COP30 (Belém, Brazil, 2025).
Western Ghats is one of how many biodiversity hotspots in India?

India's 4 biodiversity hotspots: 1) Himalayas (entire range), 2) Western Ghats (UNESCO World Heritage 2012), 3) Indo-Burma (NE India + Andaman), 4) Sundaland (Nicobar Islands, geologically part of SE Asia). Together: significant endemic flora + fauna. Hotspot concept: Norman Myers (1988).
Conservation International identified how many biodiversity hotspots globally?

Biodiversity hotspots: 36 globally (Conservation International). Cover ~2.3% Earth's land but contain ~50% plant species (endemic). Myers (1988): 10 hotspots. Mittermeier et al (1999, 2004): expanded to 25 then 34. Latest: 36 (2024). Hotspots: South America (Andes, Atlantic Forest), Africa (Madagascar, Cape Floristic), SE Asia, etc.
Asiatic Lion is found only in:

Asiatic Lion (Panthera leo persica): found only in Gir Forest National Park + Wildlife Sanctuary (Junagadh, Gujarat). Population: ~670 (2020 census, up from ~180 in 1974). IUCN: Endangered. ~1412 sq km protected area. Maldharis (pastoral community) co-exist. Kuno Palpur (MP) was prepared for translocation (rejected by Gujarat).
IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) was established in:

IPCC: established 1988 by WMO (World Meteorological Organization) + UNEP (UN Environment Programme). HQ Geneva. Scientific assessments of climate change. Reports: FAR (1990), SAR (1995), TAR (2001), AR4 (2007), AR5 (2013-14), AR6 (2021-23). Shared 2007 Nobel Peace Prize with Al Gore. AR6: 'unequivocal' human influence.
Dugong (Sea Cow) in India is found in:
Gulf of Mannar + Palk Bay + Andaman + Nicobar

Dugong (Dugong dugon, Sea Cow): herbivorous marine mammal. Vulnerable IUCN. India: Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu), Palk Bay (Tamil Nadu), Gulf of Kutch (Gujarat), Andaman + Nicobar. State animal of Andaman + Nicobar. ~250 in India (200+ in Andaman). Threats: fishing nets, seagrass loss, boat collisions. India's only herbivorous marine mammal.
How many Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were adopted by UN in 2015?

SDGs: 17 goals, 169 targets, adopted by UN (Sep 2015, replaced MDGs 2000-15). Goals: no poverty, zero hunger, health, education, gender, water, energy, work, infrastructure, inequality, cities, consumption, climate, oceans, land, peace, partnerships. By 2030.
India's first climate change assessment report was published by:

Assessment of Climate Change over Indian Region (June 2020, MoES): India's first climate change report. By Centre for Climate Change Research (CCCR), Indian Institute of Tropical Meteorology (IITM, Pune). Key findings: India avg temp rose 0.7°C (1901-2018), will rise 4.4°C by 2100 (RCP 8.5). Monsoon declining. Sea level + cyclones rising.
World Wildlife Fund (WWF) was founded in:

WWF (World Wildlife Fund): founded 11 September 1961 in Morges, Switzerland. Now: World Wide Fund for Nature (1986, except USA + Canada). Logo: giant panda (Chi-Chi, London Zoo). Founder: Julian Huxley, Victor Stolan, Max Nicholson, Peter Scott. HQ: Gland, Switzerland. India: WWF-India (1969). Mission: stop degradation of natural environment.

Brundtland Report (1987, 'Our Common Future'): World Commission on Environment + Development. Chair: Gro Harlem Brundtland (former Norwegian PM). Defined sustainable development: 'meets needs of present without compromising ability of future generations to meet their own needs'. Three pillars: economic, social, environmental. Basis for Rio Earth Summit 1992.
Mangroves are salt-tolerant trees found in:

Mangroves: salt-tolerant (halophytes) trees in intertidal zones of tropical coastlines. Adaptations: pneumatophores (breathing roots), viviparous germination. India mangrove cover: ~4,992 sq km (ISFR 2021), increase. Sundarbans (largest), Andaman, Gujarat, Maharashtra. Cyclone protection.
Saltwater Crocodile in India is found in:

Saltwater crocodile (Crocodylus porosus): largest living reptile. India: Sundarbans (West Bengal), Andaman + Nicobar Islands, Bhitarkanika (Odisha). Bhitarkanika: highest density of saltwater crocodiles in India (~1700+). Protected: Schedule I of Wildlife Protection Act 1972. Vulnerable IUCN.
Climate Finance target of $100 billion/year by 2020 was set at:

$100 billion/year climate finance: pledged by developed countries at COP15 (Copenhagen 2009). To support developing countries' climate action. Target 2020. Not met (extended to 2025). Actual: ~$80 billion (2020). COP26: doubled adaptation finance by 2025. Loss + Damage Fund: operationalized COP28 (2023) - $792 million initial pledges.

PM10: ≤10 μm. Larger particles. Settles in upper respiratory tract. Sources: dust, construction, industrial. India standard: 100 μg/m³ (24-hour avg). WHO: 45 μg/m³ (2021). Mostly outdoor dust + industrial. PM2.5 (smaller) more dangerous. Both contribute to AQI calculation.
Biosphere reserves in India are designated by:

Biosphere Reserves: designated by UNESCO under Man + Biosphere (MAB) Programme (1971). Three zones: Core (legal protection, no human activity), Buffer (limited), Transition (human settlements). India has 18 (2024). First: Nilgiri (1986). Latest: Panna (2020). 12 of India's are in UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
Carbon credits are tradable certificates representing:
One tonne of CO2 equivalent reduced/removed

Carbon credits: 1 tonne CO2-equivalent emission reduction. Traded in carbon markets. Compliance markets: CDM (Clean Development Mechanism, Kyoto), EU Emissions Trading System (EU ETS). Voluntary markets: companies, individuals. India: BSE Carbon, MCX. Domestic Carbon Credit Trading Scheme (2023, Energy Conservation Act amendment).
Sundarbans mangroves are shared by which countries?

Sundarbans: world's largest contiguous mangrove forest. Spans India (West Bengal, ~40%) + Bangladesh (~60%). ~10,000 sq km (India: 4260 sq km, Bangladesh: 6017 sq km). UNESCO World Heritage (1987, Indian part; 1997, Bangladesh part). Famous for: Royal Bengal Tigers, Sundari trees. Vulnerable: climate change, sea level rise, oil spills.
Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework was adopted in:

Kunming-Montreal GBF (19 December 2022, COP15, CBD): adopted. Replaced Aichi Targets (2010-20). 4 goals + 23 targets by 2030. Key: 30x30 (protect 30% land + sea by 2030), reduce pesticides, restore 30% degraded ecosystems, $30 billion/year finance to developing countries. India supported. 'Biodiversity Paris Agreement'.
Which is India's largest biosphere reserve?

Gulf of Mannar Biosphere Reserve (Tamil Nadu, 1989): largest in India (~10,500 sq km). Includes 21 islands, coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass beds. Dugong, sea turtles, dolphins. India's first marine biosphere reserve. UNESCO designated (2001). Gulf of Mannar Marine NP (~560 sq km).
Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) for clean water is:

BOD: oxygen consumed by microorganisms decomposing organic matter in water (5 days, 20°C). Clean water: BOD <5 mg/L. Moderately polluted: 5-15 mg/L. Polluted: 15-30 mg/L. Sewage: 200-600 mg/L. Industrial: >1000 mg/L. Used as water quality indicator. Ganga Action Plan aims to reduce BOD.

India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2021 (FSI): forest cover 21.71% (7,13,789 sq km), tree cover 2.91% (~95,777 sq km). Total: 24.62%. National Forest Policy 1988 target: 33% (geographical area). Increases: mangroves (~49 sq km), very dense forest. Decreases: NE states (1400+ sq km), forest encroachment.

Project Elephant: launched 1992. Aim: protect elephants + habitat, address human-elephant conflict. ~30 elephant reserves across India. Population: ~30,000 (2017 census). Asian elephant (Elephas maximus). India has ~60% of global Asian elephant population.
World's largest rookery of Olive Ridley turtles is:

Gahirmatha Marine Wildlife Sanctuary (Odisha): world's largest rookery of Olive Ridley turtles. Bhitarkanika coast. ~5 lakh females nest annually (arribada, mass nesting). 35 km beach. Marine WLS (1997). Olive Ridley: smallest sea turtle, ~50 kg. Threats: fishing nets, lights, beach erosion. Hatching success: ~50%.
Dissolved Oxygen (DO) for healthy aquatic life is:

Dissolved Oxygen (DO): oxygen dissolved in water. Healthy: >5 mg/L (supports fish + aquatic life). Trout: >8 mg/L. Carp: 4 mg/L. Below 4 mg/L: stress. Below 2 mg/L: hypoxia (fish death). Depletion: BOD, eutrophication, temperature rise. Sources: atmosphere, photosynthesis. Cold water holds more DO.
Project Tiger was launched in which year?

Project Tiger: launched 1 April 1973 by PM Indira Gandhi. First tiger reserve: Corbett (Uttarakhand). Aim: protect Bengal tigers. Tiger population: 1972 (~1800) → 2018 (~2967) → 2022 (~3682, ~75% world). 54 tiger reserves (2024). NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority) established 2005. International Tiger Day: 29 July.
Sustainable development meets present needs without compromising:
Future generations' ability to meet their needs

Sustainable Development: defined in Brundtland Report (1987, 'Our Common Future'). 'Development that meets the needs of the present without compromising future generations'. Three pillars: economic, social, environmental. UN SDGs (17, 2015-30) operationalize it.
One-horned Rhinoceros is mainly found in:

Indian Rhinoceros (Rhinoceros unicornis): ~75% in Kaziranga NP (Assam). Other: Pobitora WLS (Assam, highest density), Orang NP (Assam), Manas NP (Assam), Jaldapara + Gorumara (West Bengal), Dudhwa TR (UP - reintroduced). Population: ~4000 (2024, ~75% of world). Vulnerable IUCN. Poaching: rhino horn for traditional medicine.
The Van Mahotsav is celebrated in which month?

Van Mahotsav (Forest Festival): celebrated first week of July. Started 1950 by K.M. Munshi (then Union Minister for Agriculture). Mass tree plantation drive. Aims: increase forest cover, awareness. Schools, colleges, NGOs participate. Millions of saplings planted.

Net Zero / Carbon Neutrality: anthropogenic CO2 emissions = anthropogenic removals (over a year). Achieved by: emission reduction + carbon sequestration (forests, CCS) + carbon offsets. India: 2070 (PM Modi, COP26 Glasgow 2021). China: 2060. EU + USA: 2050. Bhutan + Suriname: already carbon negative. Global: 2050 needed for 1.5°C target.
Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) was opened for signature in:

CBD: opened for signature 5 June 1992 (Rio Earth Summit). Entered into force 29 December 1993. 196 parties. HQ Montreal. Objectives: 1) biodiversity conservation, 2) sustainable use, 3) fair + equitable benefit sharing. India: Biological Diversity Act 2002. Cartagena Protocol (biosafety, 2000), Nagoya Protocol (ABS, 2010), Kunming-Montreal GBF (2022).
National Water Mission (NWM) under NAPCC aims to:
Conserve water + reduce wastage + equitable distribution

NWM (2011, NAPCC): National Water Mission. Goals: 1) Water conservation, 2) Waste water reduction, 3) Equitable distribution. 20% improvement in water use efficiency by 2017. State Water Policy, basin-level management. MoJS (Ministry of Jal Shakti) implements. Catch the Rain campaign (2021).
Ozone layer is found in which atmospheric layer?

Ozone layer: stratosphere (~15-35 km altitude). O3 molecules absorb UV radiation (UV-B, UV-C). Montreal Protocol (1987): phased out CFCs (chlorofluorocarbons). Hole recovering - expected by 2066 (Antarctica). India: phased out CFCs (2010), HCFCs by 2030.

Carbon footprint: total GHG emissions (CO2-equivalent) caused by individual/organization/event/product, expressed in tonnes CO2-eq/year. Includes: transport, food, energy, goods. India per capita: ~2 tonnes (vs US ~15, world ~4.5). Reduce: renewable energy, EVs, public transport, vegetarian diet, recycling. Online calculators available.
Segregation at source (3 bins: wet, dry, hazardous)

SWM Rules 2016 (replaced 2000 rules): segregation at source (wet, dry, hazardous - 3 streams). User charges for collection. Door-to-door collection mandatory. Bulk generators (>100 kg/day). Phased ban on open burning. Landfill only for inert waste (10% of total). C&D waste rules 2016, e-waste rules 2016, bio-medical waste rules 2016.
Loss + Damage Fund was operationalized at:

Loss + Damage Fund: COP28 (Dubai, December 2023). Operationalized after COP27 (Sharm el-Sheikh, 2022) agreed in principle. For developing countries most vulnerable to climate impacts (small island states, least developed countries). Pledges: $792 million (initial). Host: World Bank (interim). Criticized as too small vs actual needs (~$400 billion/year by 2030).
International Solar Alliance (ISA) was launched by India + France in:

ISA (30 November 2015, COP21, Paris): launched by PM Modi + French President Hollande. HQ: Gurugram, India. First treaty-based international organization headquartered in India. 120+ member countries (solar-rich, between Tropics of Cancer + Capricorn). 7th General Assembly September 2024 (New Delhi). President: India.
Carbon sink is a natural or artificial reservoir that:
Absorbs more carbon than it releases

Carbon sinks: absorb CO2 from atmosphere. Natural: oceans, forests, soil, wetlands. Artificial: carbon capture + storage (CCS). India's forests: ~7 GtC stored. Blue carbon (coastal: mangroves, seagrass, salt marshes) - high efficiency. Aim: carbon neutrality by 2070.
WHO's recommended annual PM2.5 limit (2021) is:

WHO Air Quality Guidelines (September 2021): PM2.5 annual average 5 μg/m³ (halved from 10 μg/m³ in 2005). PM2.5 24-hour: 15 μg/m³. PM10: 15 μg/m³ (annual), 45 μg/m³ (24-hour). NO2: 10 μg/m³ (annual). India PM2.5 standard: 40 μg/m³ (annual) - 8x WHO limit. Most Indian cities exceed both.

Nilgiri Tahr (Nilgiritragus hylocrius): endemic to Western Ghats. State animal of Tamil Nadu. Endangered IUCN. ~3000 left. Found in: Eravikulam NP (Kerala, ~750+ - largest population), Mukurthi NP (Tamil Nadu), Anaimalai Hills, Nilgiri Hills. Stocky goat-antelope. Sacred to Todas (Nilgiris tribe).

Chilika Lake: India's first Ramsar site (1 October 1981). Asia's largest brackish water lagoon (Odisha, ~1165 sq km). Removed from Montreux Record (threatened sites list) in 2002 due to restoration. Famous for Irrawaddy dolphins, migratory birds (Nalabana bird sanctuary).
Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) was established in:

CPCB: established September 1974 under Water (Prevention + Control of Pollution) Act 1974. Apex body for pollution control. Under MoEFCC. HQ New Delhi. Chairman: Prashant Gargava (2024). 7 zonal offices. Coordinates State Pollution Control Boards (SPCBs). Implements: Air Act 1981, Environment Protection Act 1986, Water Act 1974.
Non-attainment cities under NCAP are those:
Exceeding National Ambient Air Quality Standards

Non-attainment cities: those that don't meet National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) 2009. 132 cities under NCAP (2024). Major: Delhi, Mumbai, Kolkata, Chennai, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Patna, etc. Required to develop City Action Plans (CAP). CPCB + State Pollution Control Boards monitor.

Gangetic Dolphin (Platanista gangetica): India's National Aquatic Animal (declared 2009). Endangered (IUCN). Found in Ganga, Brahmaputra, Indus river systems. Blind (uses echolocation). National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG): conservation focus. Vikramshila Gangetic Dolphin Sanctuary (Bhagalpur, Bihar).
Which is the largest biosphere reserve in India?

Gulf of Mannar (Tamil Nadu, 1989): largest biosphere reserve in India (~10,500 sq km). Includes 21 islands, coral reefs, mangroves, seagrass beds. Dugong (sea cow), sea turtles, dolphins. India's first marine biosphere reserve. UNESCO designated 2001.
How many Ramsar sites does India have (2024)?

Ramsar sites (wetlands of international importance): India has ~85 (December 2024). Joined Ramsar Convention 1 February 1982. First: Chilika (Odisha, 1981) + Keoladeo (Rajasthan, 1981). Largest: Sundarbans Wetland (~4230 sq km). 13 new sites added in 2024. 2 February: World Wetlands Day. Ramsar Convention: Ramsar, Iran (1971).
IPCC's AR6 (2021-23) declared that climate change is:

IPCC AR6 (Sixth Assessment Report, 2021-23): 'It is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean, and land.' 1.1°C warming since 1850-1900. Limit to 1.5°C requires halving emissions by 2030, net zero CO2 by 2050. Working Group I (2021, science), II (2022, impacts), III (2022, mitigation), Synthesis (March 2023).
Indian Elephant is found in how many states/UTs (2024)?

Indian Elephant (Elephas maximus indicus): ~30,000 (2017 census, synchronized). Found in ~15 states/UTs - South India (Karnataka, Kerala, TN, AP - largest), Northeast (Assam, Arunachal, Meghalaya, etc.), East (WB, Odisha, Jharkhand), North (Uttarakhand, UP), Andaman (introduced - reintroduced). National Heritage Animal (2010). Project Elephant (1992).
Microbeads are banned in cosmetics in India since:

Microbeads ban: India banned microbeads (≤5mm) in personal care products + cosmetics under Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 (effective 2018). Microbeads used as exfoliants (face wash, toothpaste). Non-biodegradable → microplastic pollution. US ban: 2017 (Microbead-Free Waters Act 2015). UK, Canada, others followed.
The 'Paris Agreement' on climate change was adopted in:

Paris Agreement: adopted 12 December 2015 at COP21 (Conference of Parties). Entered into force 4 November 2016. Goal: limit global warming to well below 2°C, ideally 1.5°C above pre-industrial. India's NDCs: 45% emission intensity reduction by 2030, net-zero by 2070.
Biological Oxygen Demand (BOD) is a measure of:

BOD: oxygen consumed by microorganisms decomposing organic matter in water (5 days, 20°C). Higher BOD = more organic pollution. Clean water: BOD < 5 mg/L. Sewage: BOD > 300 mg/L. Ganga Action Plan aims to reduce BOD.
REDD+ (Reducing Emissions from Deforestation + forest Degradation) is a:

REDD+: UNFCCC mechanism. Developed countries pay developing countries for reducing deforestation + forest degradation, sustainable forest management, conservation, enhancement of carbon stocks. India: submitted forest reference level. UN-REDD Programme: FAO, UNDP, UNEP. India involved in pilot projects.

Coral bleaching: corals expel symbiotic algae (zooxanthellae) due to stress (warm water >1°C above normal, pollution, salinity). Corals turn white, may die if stress continues. Great Barrier Reef: mass bleachings 2016, 2017, 2020, 2022. Bleaching = loss of color, not death.
Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM) aims to provide:
Functional Household Tap Connection (55 lpcd to every rural household)

JJM (15 August 2019): Har Ghar Jal. Goal: FHTC to every rural household (55 lpcd - litres per capita per day). Originally by 2024 (extended). ~75% achieved (15 crore households). Cost: ~₹3.6 lakh crore. Implemented by states. Convergence: SBM, MGNREGA. AMRUT: urban counterpart (water supply). Water quality monitoring: JJM Water Quality Management Information System (WQMIS).
