Hangul (Kashmir Stag, Cervus hanglu hanglu): Critically Endangered IUCN. Found in Dachigam National Park (~141 sq km, near Srinagar). Population: ~250-300 (2023, declining from ~5000 in 1940s). State animal of J&K. Subspecies of Central Asian Red Deer. Threats: habitat loss, poaching, livestock grazing.

Agenda 21: comprehensive action plan for sustainable development. Adopted at Rio Earth Summit (1992). 40 chapters, ~600 pages. Covers: social + economic dimensions, conservation + management of resources, strengthening major groups, means of implementation. Local Agenda 21: cities implement. 21st century agenda. Reaffirmed at Rio+20 (2012).
Clean Ganga Fund (CGF) accepts donations for:

Clean Ganga Fund (CGF, 2014): accepts contributions from individuals, NRIs, PIOs, organizations for Ganga rejuvenation. Donations: 100% tax exemption (Section 80G). Used: NMCG activities - sewage treatment, river cleaning, ghats, biodiversity, afforestation, awareness. ~₹700+ crore collected (2024). Donors can track projects.
Snow Leopard is found in how many Indian states/UTs?

Snow Leopard (Vulnerable IUCN): found in 5 Himalayan states/UTs - Ladakh (~50% of India's population), Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh. ~500-700 in India. Project Snow Leopard launched 2009. Protected in: Hemis NP (Ladakh), Great Himalayan NP (HP), Nanda Devi NP, Kibber WLS (HP), Dibang WLS (Arunachal).
DDT concentration increasing up food chain

Biomagnification: toxin concentration increases at higher trophic levels. Example: DDT (pesticide) → plankton → small fish → big fish → bird (eagle). Top predators most affected. DDT in bird eggshells → thin shells, population decline (Silent Spring, Rachel Carson 1962).

Kyoto Protocol: adopted 11 December 1997 (COP3, Japan). Entered into force 16 February 2005. Binding emission targets for developed countries (Annex I). Doha Amendment (2012). USA never ratified. Replaced by Paris Agreement (2015). Clean Development Mechanism (CDM).
India's forest cover as percentage of geographical area (ISFR 2021) is approximately:

India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2021 (FSI): forest cover 21.71% (7,13,789 sq km), tree cover 2.91% (~95,777 sq km). Total: 24.62%. National Forest Policy 1988 target: 33% (geographical area). Increases: mangroves, very dense forest. Decreases: NE states, forest encroachment.
Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 banned single-use plastic items below which thickness?

PWM Rules 2016: minimum thickness 50 microns (vs earlier 40). EPR for producers. PWM Amendment Rules 2022: banned identified single-use plastic items (effective 1 July 2022) - ear buds, cutlery, straws, etc. Compostable/biodegradable plastics exempted.
Great Indian Bustard is also state bird of:

Great Indian Bustard (GIB): state bird of Rajasthan (since 1981). Population: ~150 (2023). Found in: Desert NP (Rajasthan), Kutch (Gujarat), Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh. Critically Endangered IUCN. Threats: habitat loss (grasslands), power lines (collision). Recovery Programme for GIB, Lesser Florican, Bengal Florican (MoEFCC, 2015).
Vultures in India declined sharply due to:

Vulture decline: 99%+ decline in 1990s-2000s (3 Gyps species: White-rumped, Long-billed, Slender-billed). Cause: diclofenac (NSAID given to cattle). Vultures eat carcasses, kidney failure. India banned diclofenac for vet use (2006). Meloxicam: safer alternative. Vulture breeding centres (Pinjore, Haryana; Buxa, WB; Rani, Assam). Captive breeding releases: ongoing.
First biosphere reserve of India is:

Nilgiri BR: first biosphere reserve of India (1986, in 3 states - Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka). Spans ~5520 sq km. Includes: Mudumalai, Bandipur, Nagarhole, Silent Valley, Wayanad WLS + NPs. UNESCO designated (2000). Lion-tailed Macaque, Nilgiri Tahr habitats. Multi-state cooperative management.
Joint Forest Management (JFM) program was started in:

JFM (1988, MoEF circular): partnership between Forest Department + local communities for forest protection + regeneration. Village Forest Committees. Communities get share in forest produce (usufructs). Origin: Arabari (West Bengal, 1972, Ajit Banerjee). Now Van Suraksha Samitis.
Acid rain is mainly caused by which gases?

Acid rain: caused by SO2 (sulphuric acid) and NOx (nitric acid) emissions from fossil fuels, industries. pH < 5.6. Effects: lake acidification (fish death), forest damage, building corrosion. First identified by Robert Angus Smith (1872, Manchester).
Circular economy is based on which principle?

Circular economy: closed-loop system. Reduce, Reuse, Recycle (3Rs) + Refuse, Rethink, Repair, Refurbish, Remanufacture, Repurpose. Alternative to linear 'take-make-dispose' economy. EU, China leaders. India: 12 SWM Rules 2016, EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility).

BEE (Bureau of Energy Efficiency, 2002): star rating 1-5 for appliances. Higher stars = more efficient. Mandatory for ACs, refrigerators, geysers, TVs, fans, pumps, etc. Saves electricity, reduces bills, carbon emissions. Star labeling program.

Project Tiger: launched 1 April 1973 by Indira Gandhi. First tiger reserve: Corbett (Uttarakhand). Aim: protect Bengal tigers. Tiger population: 1972 (~1800) → 2018 (~2967) → 2022 (~3682, ~75% of world). 54 tiger reserves (2024). NTCA (National Tiger Conservation Authority).
Forest Rights Act 2006 is also called:
Scheduled Tribes + Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act

FRA 2006 (effective 31 December 2007): recognizes forest rights of Scheduled Tribes + other traditional forest dwellers. Rights: 1) Land (up to 4 hectares, cultivated before 13 December 2005), 2) Use (NTFP), 3) Habitat + habitation (PTG), 4) Governance + management (community forest resources). Gram Sabha consent for diversion.

Rio Earth Summit (3-14 June 1992, UN Conference on Environment + Development, 'Earth Summit'): produced 1) Rio Declaration (27 principles), 2) Agenda 21 (action plan), 3) UNFCCC (UN Framework Convention on Climate Change), 4) CBD (Convention on Biological Diversity), 5) Statement of Forest Principles. 172 governments, 108 heads of state.

Paris Agreement (12 December 2015, COP21): adopted. Entered into force 4 November 2016. Goal: limit warming well below 2°C (preferably 1.5°C) above pre-industrial. NDCs (Nationally Determined Contributions): each country sets target. India: net zero by 2070, 45% emission intensity reduction by 2030 vs 2005, 50% non-fossil electricity by 2030. Global stocktake every 5 years.
Total greenhouse gas emissions caused by individual/event/product

Carbon footprint: total GHG emissions (CO2 equivalent) caused by an individual, organization, event, product. Expressed in tonnes CO2-eq per year. India per capita: ~2 tonnes (vs US ~15, world avg ~4.5). Can be reduced: renewable energy, EVs, public transport, vegetarian diet.
Plastic Waste Management Rules 2016 mandated EPR for:

PWM Rules 2016: EPR (Extended Producer Responsibility) for PIBO (Producers, Importers, Brand Owners). Manage plastic waste generated from their products. PWM Amendment Rules 2022 (16 February 2022): mandatory EPR registration, targets (20-100% by 2024-27), category-wise (rigid, flexible, multilayer, compostable). CPCB implements.

Atal Bhujal Yojana (ATAL JAL, December 2019, ₹6,000 crore, 5 years): sustainable groundwater management. World Bank funded (50%). 7 states: Gujarat, Haryana, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, UP. Focus: over-exploited + critical blocks. Community-led groundwater management. Panchayats involved. CGWB implements.
Compensatory Afforestation Fund Act (CAMPA) was enacted in:

CAMP Act 2016: established National + State Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA). Money collected when forest land diverted for non-forest purposes (Forest Conservation Act 1980). ₹54,000+ crore accumulated. National Authority chaired by Environment Minister.
Climate Vulnerability Index ranks India as:

India: highly vulnerable to climate change. Germanwatch Climate Risk Index: India 7th most affected (2021, vs 20th in 2019). Reasons: long coastline (7516 km), Himalayan glaciers, monsoon dependence, agriculture-dependent economy (~46% workforce). Heat waves, floods, cyclones increasing. NDMA, NAPCC, NMSHE (Himalayas) action plans.
Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) is sometimes called:

Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD): 'Indian Niño'. Difference in sea surface temperature between western (Arabian Sea) and eastern (Bay of Bengal/Indonesia) Indian Ocean. Positive IOD: stronger monsoon. Negative IOD: weaker monsoon. Discovered by Saji et al. (1999).
Air Quality Index (AQI) is calculated using how many pollutants in India?

India AQI (CPCB, 2014): 8 pollutants - PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb. Six AQI categories: Good (0-50), Satisfactory (51-100), Moderate (101-200), Poor (201-300), Very Poor (301-400), Severe (401-500). Diwali, stubble burning causes severe AQI in NCR.
Olive Ridley turtles nest at which Indian beach?

Olive Ridley sea turtles (Lepidochelys olivacea): mass nesting (arribada) at: 1) Gahirmatha (Odisha, ~5 lakh nests/year - largest), 2) Rushikulya (Odisha), 3) Devi River mouth (Odisha). Vulnerable IUCN. ~3,00,000+ turtles nest in Odisha. Other sites: Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu (Chennai), Andaman + Nicobar. Hatching: ~50 days.
Plastic pollution in oceans breaks into smaller particles called:

Microplastics: plastic particles <5 mm. From breakdown of larger plastics + microbeads in cosmetics. Found in oceans, fish, drinking water, even human blood. Concerns: ingestion by marine life, chemical absorption, food chain. India banned single-use plastic (2022).
Sangai (Brow-antlered Deer) is found only in:

Sangai (Panolia eldii eldii): brow-antlered deer. Endemic to Manipur. Found only on phumdis (floating islands) of Loktak Lake, in Keibul Lamjao National Park (world's only floating NP, ~40 sq km). Endangered IUCN. ~260 (2023, up from ~14 in 1975). State animal of Manipur. Threats: phumdi degradation, water level changes.
Mangroves are mainly found in which Indian states?

Mangrove cover India (ISFR 2021): ~4992 sq km. Top states: West Bengal (~2114 sq km, Sundarbans - largest), Gujarat (~1179 sq km, Kutch), Andaman + Nicobar (~616 sq km), Andhra Pradesh (~405 sq km). Increases: +17 sq km. Adaptations: pneumatophores (breathing roots), viviparous germination. Cyclone protection.
Perform Achieve + Trade (PAT) scheme is for:

PAT (2012, NMEEE under NAPCC): Perform, Achieve + Trade. Energy efficiency in energy-intensive industries (Designated Consumers, DCs). Cycle-based (PAT I-VII). Industries: power, steel, cement, aluminium, fertilizers, refineries, pulp + paper, textiles, chlor-alkali. Energy Saving Certificates (ESCerts) traded. BEE implements. ~25 million toe energy saved/cycle.
Ramsar Convention is for conservation of:

Ramsar Convention (1971, Iran): wetlands of international importance. India joined 1982. Currently 80+ Ramsar sites (2024, up from 26 in 2018). Largest: Sundarbans (4230 sq km). Latest additions: 13 new in 2024. 2 Feb: World Wetlands Day.

Clouded Leopard (Neofelis nebulosa): found in Northeast India - Namdapha NP (Arunachal Pradesh), Pakke WLS, Manas NP (Assam), Khasi Hills (Meghalaya). Vulnerable IUCN. ~10000 mature individuals (global, decreasing). Arboreal. Can open jaw 100° (largest of any cat). Dark cloud-like spots. State animal of Meghalaya.
Green Climate Fund (GCF) was established to:
Support developing countries in climate adaptation + mitigation

GCF: established at COP16 (Cancun, 2010). Operational 2015. World's largest climate fund. HQ Songdo, South Korea. Goal: $100 billion/year from developed to developing by 2020 (not met, extended to 2025). India: accessed projects. Fund: adaptation (50%), mitigation (50%). Private Sector Facility.

PM2.5: particulate matter ≤ 2.5 micrometers. Penetrates deep into lungs, bloodstream. Sources: vehicles, industries, biomass burning, construction. Major health risk: respiratory, cardiovascular diseases, premature death. India standards: 60 µg/m³ (24-hour avg).
National Ambient Air Quality Standards (NAAQS) are notified by:

NAAQS: notified by CPCB under Air (Prevention + Control of Pollution) Act 1981. Last revised 2009. 12 pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb, benzene, benzo(a)pyrene, arsenic, nickel. Industrial/residential/rural/sensitive area limits. National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) targets compliance.
Van Mahotsav (Forest Festival) is celebrated in:

Van Mahotsav: first week of July. Started 1950 by K.M. Munshi (then Union Minister for Agriculture + Food). Mass tree plantation drive. Aim: increase forest cover + awareness. Schools, colleges, NGOs participate. Millions of saplings planted. National Forest Policy 1988 target: 33% forest cover (currently ~22%).
Cap and Trade system for emissions:
Sets emission limits, allows trading of allowances

Cap + Trade: government sets cap (total emissions allowed). Issues allowances (1 tonne CO2-eq each). Companies trade allowances. Examples: EU ETS (largest, 2005), California-Quebec (WCI), China (national ETS 2021, world's largest by emissions covered). India: Carbon Credit Trading Scheme 2023 (initially voluntary, may become mandatory).
Toxins accumulating in single organism over time

Bioaccumulation: toxin (e.g., mercury, DDT) accumulates in single organism over its lifetime. Different from biomagnification (increases up food chain). Example: Minamata disease (mercury in fish, Japan 1950s). Lipophilic toxins bioaccumulate in fat.

Biosphere Reserves: designated by UNESCO under Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme (1971). Three zones: Core (legally protected, no human activity), Buffer (limited activity), Transition (human settlements). India has 18 (2024). First: Nilgiri (1986). Latest: Panna (2020).
World's first White Tiger was found in:

White Tiger (Mohan): captured by Maharaja of Rewa (Madhya Pradesh) in 1951. Mohan: founder of all captive white tigers worldwide. White colour: recessive gene (leucism, not albinism). Now: ~200 white tigers in captivity (Nandankanan, Bhubaneswar; Delhi Zoo). Last seen wild: 1958. All descended from Mohan. Mohan died 1970.

India's NDCs (updated 2022): 1) Net zero by 2070 (announced COP26, 2021). 2) 45% emission intensity reduction by 2030 (vs 2005). 3) 50% electricity from non-fossil sources by 2030. 4) 2.5-3 GtCO2e additional carbon sink by 2030. Panchamrit - 5 pledges.

Carbon tax: tax on CO2 emissions (per tonne CO2-eq). Aimed: discourage fossil fuels, internalize externalities. Examples: Sweden (~$130/tCO2, highest), Finland, UK (~£18/t), Canada, Singapore (~$5/t). India: no carbon tax, but coal cess (₹400/tonne, 2010, GST compensation fund). USA: no federal carbon tax (some states like California have cap-and-trade).

El Niño: warming of eastern equatorial Pacific (>0.5°C above normal). Part of ENSO (El Niño-Southern Oscillation). Affects global weather - drought in India/Australia, floods in Americas. La Niña: cooling. Forecast helps Indian monsoon prediction.
Sea level rise is caused by:

Sea level rise (NASA, 1993-2023): ~3.4 mm/year. ~110 mm rise since 1993. Causes: 1) Thermal expansion of warming ocean water (~50%), 2) Melting glaciers + ice caps (Greenland, Antarctica). IPCC AR6 (2021): 0.3-1.0 m by 2100. Threatens: island nations (Maldives, Tuvalu, Marshall Islands), coastal cities (Mumbai, Kolkata, NYC, Miami).

Lion-tailed Macaque (Macaca silenus, Wandaroo): endemic to Western Ghats (rainforests of Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu). Endangered IUCN. ~4000-5000 left. Distinctive silver-white mane. Old World monkey. Arboreal, frugivorous. Protected in Silent Valley NP (Kerala), Anamalai Tiger Reserve, Agumbe, Kudremukh NP.

Montreux Record: register of wetland sites in Ramsar List where changes in ecological character have occurred. 'Black list' of Ramsar sites. India: 2 sites - Keoladeo NP (Bharatpur, Rajasthan - added 1990, removed 2003), Loktak Lake (Manipur - added 1993). Chilika removed 2002 (improved). Periodic review + reporting.

Bioaccumulation: toxin (mercury, DDT) accumulates in single organism over lifetime. Biomagnification: toxin concentration increases at higher trophic levels (predators > prey). Example: DDT in fish-eating birds (eagles, brown pelicans) → thin eggshells, near extinction. Rachel Carson: Silent Spring (1962), started environmental movement.
Plastic pollution breaks into small particles called:

Microplastics: plastic particles <5 mm. Primary (manufactured - microbeads in cosmetics), secondary (breakdown of larger plastics). Found in: oceans (~5 trillion pieces), fish, drinking water, salt, even human blood + placenta. Concerns: ingestion by marine life, chemical absorption, food chain. India banned single-use plastic (1 July 2022).

Acid rain: pH <5.6 (normal rain slightly acidic due to CO2 dissolving). Causes: SO2 (sulphuric acid) + NOx (nitric acid) from fossil fuels, industries. Effects: lake acidification (fish death), forest damage, building corrosion, soil leaching. First identified: Robert Angus Smith (1872, Manchester). Acid rain programs: USA (1990), Europe.
Forest Conservation Act 1980 was renamed as:

Forest (Conservation) Act 1980: renamed Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 (2023 amendment). Aimed at: restricting diversion of forest land for non-forest purposes. Requires Central govt approval. 2023 amendment: allows some non-forest activities (border infrastructure, ecotourism) in forest areas within 100 km of borders.
Carbon credit is a tradable certificate representing:
One tonne of CO2 equivalent reduced/removed

Carbon credit: 1 tonne CO2-equivalent emission reduction. Traded in carbon markets. Compliance markets (CDM, EU ETS) + voluntary markets. India's carbon credit trading scheme (2023, under Energy Conservation Act). CCER, CER, VER. India largest CDM project host.
AQI (Air Quality Index) for India has how many categories?

AQI India (CPCB, 2014): 6 categories - Good (0-50), Satisfactory (51-100), Moderate (101-200), Poor (201-300), Very Poor (301-400), Severe (401-500). 8 pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb. CPCB monitors ~1500+ stations across India. NAQI (National Air Quality Index): launched September 2014.
IUCN Red List classifies species by:

IUCN Red List: classifies species by extinction risk. Categories: Least Concern (LC), Near Threatened (NT), Vulnerable (VU), Endangered (EN), Critically Endangered (CR), Extinct in Wild (EW), Extinct (EX). Updated regularly. India: ~1000+ species on list.
Snow Leopard is found in which Indian states/UTs?

Snow Leopard (Vulnerable IUCN): found in Himalayan region - Ladakh (~50% of India's population), Himachal, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh. ~500-700 in India. Project Snow Leopard launched 2009. Protected in Hemis NP (Ladakh), Great Himalayan NP (HP), Nanda Devi NP.
Forest Survey of India (FSI) is under which ministry?
Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

FSI: under MoEFCC. Established 1981. HQ Dehradun. Mandate: assess + monitor forest cover (using satellite data), prepare State of Forest Report (biennial since 1987), forest fire alerts, support state forest departments, training. ISFR published biennially. Uses: LISS-III satellite data (IRS Resourcesat-2).
Single-use plastic was banned in India from:

Single-use plastic ban (1 July 2022, MoEFCC): identified single-use plastic items - ear buds, cutlery, plates, cups, glasses, straws, thermocol decorations, wrapping films <50 microns, sticks for balloons, candy sticks, ice-cream sticks, polystyrene. PWM Rules 2022 amendment. Bio-based + biodegradable plastics exempted.
Western Ghats + forests of South India

Gaur (Indian Bison, Bos gaurus): largest bovine. Found in Western Ghats, forests of Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Goa. Also NE India. Vulnerable (IUCN). Largest populations in: Bandipur, Nagarhole, Mudumalai, Periyar Tiger Reserves. Karnataka has ~50% of India's Gaur population.
Jal Shakti Abhiyan (JSA) was launched in:

Jal Shakti Abhiyan (July 2019): water conservation campaign. Phase 1 (July-September 2019): 255 water-stressed districts in 36 states/UTs. 5 interventions: water conservation + rainwater harvesting, renovation of traditional + other water bodies, reuse + recharge structures, watershed development, intensive afforestation. 'Catch the Rain - When it falls, where it falls' (2021).
National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) was launched in:

NAPCC (30 June 2008): PM Manmohan Singh. 8 National Missions: 1) Solar, 2) Enhanced Energy Efficiency, 3) Sustainable Habitat, 4) Water, 5) Sustaining Himalayan Ecosystem, 6) Green India, 7) Sustainable Agriculture, 8) Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change. SAPCCs (State Action Plans) developed by all states.
MDGs (Millennium Development Goals) had how many goals?

MDGs (September 2000, Millennium Declaration, UN): 8 goals, 21 targets, 60 indicators. By 2015. 1) Eradicate extreme poverty + hunger, 2) Universal primary education, 3) Gender equality, 4) Reduce child mortality, 5) Maternal health, 6) HIV/AIDS, malaria, etc., 7) Environmental sustainability, 8) Global partnership. Replaced by SDGs (2015).
Peacock is the national bird of India since:

Indian Peacock (Pavo cristatus): National Bird of India (declared 1963). Found throughout Indian subcontinent. Males: iridescent blue neck, train (feathers). Cultural significance: vehicle of Kartikeya, Lord Krishna's feather. Protected: Schedule I of Wildlife (Protection) Act 1972. Breeding season: June-September (monsoon - dancing displays).
Biomagnification of DDT is classic example from:

Rachel Carson's 'Silent Spring' (September 1962): exposed DDT's ecological damage. DDT bioaccumulates in fatty tissues, biomagnifies up food chain. Top predators (eagles, peregrine falcons, brown pelicans) got near-lethal levels → thin eggshells → reproductive failure. USA banned DDT 1972. EPA established 1970. Started global environmental movement.
Sea level rise is mainly caused by:
Thermal expansion of water + melting ice

Sea level rise: ~3.4 mm/year (1993-2023, NASA). Causes: thermal expansion of ocean water (~50%), melting glaciers + ice caps (Greenland, Antarctica). IPCC: 0.3-1.0 m by 2100. Threatens: island nations (Maldives, Tuvalu), coastal cities (Mumbai, Kolkata, NYC).

Biodiversity: coined by Walter G. Rosen (1986) for the National Forum on BioDiversity (Washington DC, 1986). Popularized by E.O. Wilson (Harvard biologist, 'Father of Biodiversity'). Variability among living organisms at genetic, species, ecosystem levels.
Which is the most endangered species in India?

Great Indian Bustard (GIB): critically endangered IUCN. Population: ~150 (2023). Found in Rajasthan (Desert NP), Gujarat, Maharashtra. State bird of Rajasthan. Threats: habitat loss (grasslands), power lines. Conservation: breeding center at Sorsan, Rajasthan.
Fly ash is a byproduct of:

Fly ash: fine particles from coal combustion (thermal power plants). India produces ~230 million tonnes/year. Uses: cement, bricks, road embankments, agriculture (soil amendment, controversial). MoEF notification: 100% fly ash utilization. Fly ash bricks replace clay bricks (saves top soil).
National Parks in India require permission from which authority for any activity?

NBWL (National Board for Wildlife): headed by PM. State Board: by CM. Any activity in National Park/Tiger Reserve needs NBWL clearance. Wildlife Protection Act 1972 created framework. SC in Godavarman case extended forest protection. ~106 NPs in India (2024).

Red Panda (Ailurus fulgens): found in Eastern Himalayas. India: Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Darjeeling (West Bengal), Meghalaya. Endangered IUCN. ~10000 left globally. Arboreal, bamboo-eating. State animal of Sikkim. Padmaja Naidu Himalayan Zoological Park (Darjeeling): breeding program. Singalila NP (Darjeeling).
Biodiversity hotspot is a region with:

Biodiversity hotspots (Norman Myers, 1988): 2 criteria - 1) ≥1500 endemic vascular plant species (found nowhere else), 2) ≥70% habitat loss. 36 hotspots globally (Conservation International). India has 4: Himalayas, Western Ghats (both 1988), Indo-Burma, Sundaland (Nicobar Islands). Hotspots cover ~2.3% Earth but contain ~50% plant species.

SDGs (25 September 2015, UN General Assembly): 17 goals + 169 targets. Replaced MDGs (2000-15). By 2030. Themes: people (poverty, hunger, health, education, gender), planet (water, energy, climate, oceans, land), prosperity (work, infrastructure, inequality, cities, consumption), peace (institutions), partnership. India NITI Aayog SDG Index: 71 (2024).
Great Indian Bustard is found mainly in:

Great Indian Bustard (GIB, Ardeotis nigriceps): critically endangered IUCN. Population: ~150 (2023). Found in: Rajasthan (Desert NP, Pokhran), Gujarat (Kutch), Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka. State bird of Rajasthan. Threats: habitat loss (grasslands), power lines (collision), hunting. Conservation: breeding centres (Sorsan, Rajasthan; Kutch).
Eco mark or Ecomark is India's certification for:

Ecomark: India's ecolabel scheme (1991, BIS). Earthen pot logo. Given to products meeting environmental criteria + quality standards. 16 product categories: soaps, paper, paints, food, batteries, etc. Modeled on German Blue Angel, EU Ecolabel. Limited adoption.

PM2.5: particulate matter ≤2.5 micrometers (μm). Penetrates deep into lungs + bloodstream. Sources: vehicles, industries, biomass burning, construction. Major health risk: respiratory, cardiovascular diseases, premature death. India standard: 60 μg/m³ (24-hour avg, ~4x WHO). WHO: 15 μg/m³ (24-hour, 2021). Delhi winter PM2.5: 200-500+ μg/m³.
Joint Forest Management (JFM) was started in:

JFM (1988, MoEF circular): partnership between Forest Department + local communities for forest protection + regeneration. Village Forest Committees. Communities get share in forest produce (usufructs). Origin: Arabari experiment (WB, 1972, Ajit Banerjee). Now Van Suraksha Samitis. ~1.7 lakh JFM committees (2024), managing ~22 million hectares.
National Clean Air Programme (NCAP) aims to reduce PM pollution by:

NCAP (Jan 2019): India's first national air quality programme. 132 non-attainment cities (didn't meet NAAQS). Original target: 20-30% reduction in PM10+PM2.5 by 2024. Revised (2022): 40% reduction by 2026. City-specific action plans. CPCB monitoring.
COP (Conference of Parties) of UNFCCC meets how often?

COP: supreme decision-making body of UNFCCC (UN Framework Convention on Climate Change, 1992 Rio Earth Summit). Meets annually (since 1995). Famous: COP3 (Kyoto, 1997), COP21 (Paris, 2015), COP26 (Glasgow, 2021), COP28 (Dubai, 2023). COP29 (Baku, 2024), COP30 (Belém, Brazil, November 2025).
Carbon sink is a reservoir that:
Absorbs more carbon than it releases

Carbon sinks: absorb CO2 from atmosphere. Natural: oceans (~25%), forests (~30%), soil, wetlands. Artificial: carbon capture + storage (CCS). India's forests: ~7 GtC stored. Mangrove 'blue carbon': high efficiency. Goal: net zero by 2070. Afforestation, restoration, soil carbon sequestration important. Payout for avoided deforestation (REDD+).
Eco Mark (Ecomark) is India's certification for:

Ecomark: India's ecolabel scheme (1991, BIS). Earthen pot logo. Given to products meeting environmental criteria + BIS quality standards. 16 product categories: soaps, detergents, paper, paints, food, batteries, etc. Modeled on German Blue Angel, EU Ecolabel. Limited adoption. Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS) implements.
ECBC (Energy Conservation Building Code) is for:

ECBC (2007, BIS): Energy Conservation Building Code. For commercial buildings (connected load ≥ 100 kW / contract demand ≥ 120 kVA). Sets minimum energy standards. ECBC 2017 updated. ECO-Niwas Samhita (2018): for residential buildings. Mandatory in some states.
Global warming is mainly caused by increase in which gases?

Global warming: increase in Earth's average temperature due to greenhouse effect. Main gases: CO2 (75% of warming, ~422 ppm 2024), CH4 (28x more potent than CO2), N2O (265x), CFCs (1000s of times). Paris Agreement (2015): limit warming to 1.5°C.

COD: oxygen required to chemically oxidize all organic + inorganic matter (using dichromate). Higher than BOD (BOD is only organic + biological). COD/BOD ratio: ~1.5-2 (biodegradable), higher for industrial waste. Industrial effluent standards: 250 mg/L (discharge to surface water). Domestic sewage: 200-400 mg/L.

Namami Gange (May 2014): integrated Ganga conservation mission. ₹20,000 crore (2015-20). National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG, registered 2011). Implementing: 1) Sewage treatment infrastructure, 2) River surface cleaning, 3) Industrial effluent monitoring, 4) River front development, 5) Biodiversity, 6) Afforestation, 7) Public awareness, 8) Ganga Gram.
Nitrates and phosphates in water bodies

Eutrophication: excess nutrients (N, P) from fertilizers, sewage → algal blooms → algae die, decompose → oxygen depletion → fish death, dead zones. Lake restoration: aeration, nutrient removal. Example: Lake Erie (North America), Gulf of Mexico dead zone.
Wild Ass Sanctuary in India is at:

Indian Wild Ass Sanctuary: Little Rann of Kutch, Gujarat. ~4954 sq km. Population: ~6000+ (2020 census, up from ~3600 in 2014). Indian Wild Ass (Equus hemionus khur, Ghudkhur): endemic to South Asia. Endangered IUCN. Found only in Gujarat (Rann of Kutch). Other wild ass species: Tibetan Wild Ass (Kiang).

SBM-U 2.0 (1 October 2021): ₹1.41 lakh crore (5 years). Garbage-free cities (GFC). Components: 1) ODF++ (no visible faecal matter, safe fecal sludge management), 2) Water+ (no untreated sewage in drains/rivers), 3) GFC Star Rating (1-7 stars). City priorities. Convergence: AMRUT 2.0 (water), NMCG (Ganga).
Oldest human fossil in India was discovered in 2024. Where?

Hathnora skull: only known Homo erectus fossil in India (1982, Arun Sonakia). Recently CT scanned, ~250-350 ka (mid-Pleistocene). Found in Narmada valley, Madhya Pradesh. Suggests India was part of human migration path. Recent 2024 studies re-dated and analyzed.
India became the world's 5th largest economy in:

India became 5th largest economy (2022): surpassed UK. Currently ~$3.9 trillion (2024-25). Order (2024): US, China, Germany, Japan, India. Projected: 3rd largest by 2027 (surpassing Japan + Germany). Goal: developed country by 2047 ($30 trillion GDP target).
India's presidency of Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) was in:

SCO Summit 2023: 4 July 2023, virtual (hosted by India). Iran admitted as new member. Belarus joined in 2024. SCO started 2001 (Shanghai Five 1996). India joined 2017. Members: India, China, Russia, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, Iran, Belarus.
Statue of Unity is dedicated to:

Statue of Unity: world's tallest statue (182 m). Located at Kevadia, Gujarat (Narmada dam). Dedicated to Sardar Patel ('Iron Man of India', 1875-1950). Inaugurated 31 October 2018 (Patel's birthday). Bronze-clad. Made by Ram V. Sutar (sculptor). ~₹3000 crore.
RBI launched the e-Rupee (CBDC) pilot in:

Digital Rupee (e₹): Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC). Pilot launched: wholesale 1 Nov 2022 (govt bonds settlement), retail 1 Dec 2022 (8 cities). Different from UPI. Legal tender. Features: anonymity (small transactions), traceability. Both wholesale (e₹-W) and retail (e₹-R).
India's first underwater metro started in:

Kolkata Underwater Metro (East-West corridor, Howrah-Esplanade section): opened 13 March 2024 (PM Modi). Under Hooghly river (~520m tunnel, 32m deep). India's first underwater metro. Full corridor: Howrah-Salt Lake (~17 km). Replaced earlier 2023 opening (accident).
Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 faced significant opposition. Waqf Boards manage:

Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024: proposes reforms to Waqf Act 1995. Waqf Boards (Central + State) manage Muslim religious + charitable endowments. India has 3rd largest waqf properties (~8.7 lakh). Controversies: inclusion of non-Muslims in Boards, survey powers, dispute resolution.
Saudi Arabia-Iran détente was brokered by:

China brokered Saudi-Iran détente (10 March 2023, Beijing). Resumed diplomatic relations after 7 years (severed 2016). Both sides agreed to reopen embassies. Major diplomatic victory for China in Middle East. Failed to end Yemen war but reduced regional tensions. Egypt-Saudi-UAE grouping vs Iran-Turkey-Qatar (rivalry).

BRICS expansion (1 January 2024): Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE joined. Saudi Arabia invited but undecided (later reported as joined). Argentina declined (under Milei). BRICS+: 10 members now (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa + new 4 + Saudi). ~40% world GDP (PPP), 45% population, 30% land area.
Israel normalized diplomatic relations with which UAE-led group in 2020?

Abraham Accords (Sep-Dec 2020): Israel-UAE (15 Sep), Bahrain (15 Sep), Sudan (23 Oct), Morocco (10 Dec) normalized relations. Brokered by USA (Trump administration, Jared Kushner). First Gulf countries to recognize Israel. Morocco got US recognition of Western Sahara claim.
Pradhan Mantri Suryodaya Yojana (rooftop solar) was launched in:

PM Suryodaya Yojana (launched 22 January 2024): rooftop solar installation in 1 crore households. Reduces electricity bills (₹15,000-18,000/year). Subsidy: ₹30,000-78,000 (based on capacity). After Ram Mandir consecration. Aim: 40 GW rooftop solar. Originally 'PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana' (Feb 2024). ~5+ lakh installations (2024).
Droupadi Murmu became the first tribal President on:

Droupadi Murmu: 15th President of India (since 25 July 2022). First woman tribal President. First President from Odisha. Second woman President (after Pratibha Patil, 2007-12). Former Jharkhand Governor (2015-2021). BJP member. Santhal tribe. Born June 1958 at Mayurbhanj, Odisha. Tribal Chief Minister: Hemant Soren (Jharkhand).
One Nation, One Election proposal by Ram Nath Kovind committee recommends:

One Nation, One Election (High Level Committee, Ram Nath Kovind chair, March 2024 report): recommends simultaneous Lok Sabha + State Assembly elections (first phase). Also municipal + panchayat within 100 days. Needs constitutional amendment. Cost savings, governance continuity.
Saudi Arabia-Iran détente was brokered by which country in 2023?

China brokered Saudi-Iran détente (10 March 2023, Beijing). Resumed diplomatic relations after 7 years (severed 2016). Both sides agreed to reopen embassies. Major diplomatic victory for China in Middle East. Failed to end Yemen war but reduced regional tensions.
James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) was launched by NASA in:

JWST (James Webb Space Telescope): launched 25 December 2021 (Ariane 5, French Guiana). Replaced Hubble (1990). Largest space telescope (6.5m mirror). Orbit: L2 (1.5 million km). IR observations: early universe, exoplanet atmospheres, galaxy formation. First images July 2022.
Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) replaced IPC from:

New criminal laws (effective 1 July 2024): Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS, replaces IPC 1860), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS, replaces CrPC), Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA, replaces Evidence Act 1872). Modernization: digitization, forensics, citizen-centric.
Ram Mandir consecration (Pran Pratishtha) in Ayodhya was held on:

Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha: 22 January 2024, Ayodhya. PM Modi as chief yajman. Temple dedicated to Lord Ram Lalla. Built on site of disputed Babri Masjid (demolished 6 Dec 1992). Supreme Court verdict (Nov 2019). Architecture: Nagara style, pink sandstone.
Which Indian city hosted the 2023 Cricket World Cup final?

Cricket World Cup 2023: hosted by India (Oct-Nov 2023). Final: 19 November 2023, Narendra Modi Stadium (Ahmedabad, ~132,000 capacity, world's largest). Australia beat India by 6 wickets. India won all 10 league matches but lost final. Travis Head Player of Match.
FIFA World Cup 2026 will be hosted by:

FIFA World Cup 2026: hosted by USA, Canada, Mexico (June-July 2026). First time 48 teams (up from 32). 16 cities (11 USA, 2 Canada, 3 Mexico). Mexico third time hosting (1970, 1986 - first country to host 3 times). 104 matches total. Final: MetLife Stadium (NY/NJ).
India's first indigenously developed aircraft carrier INS Vikrant (IAC-1) was commissioned on:

INS Vikrant (IAC-1): commissioned 2 September 2022 (Kochi, PM Modi). India's first indigenous aircraft carrier. Built by Cochin Shipyard (~₹20,000 crore). ~45,000 tonnes. STOBAR (Short Take-Off But Arrested Recovery). MiG-29K, LCA Navy. Named after 1961 Vikrant (decommissioned 1997, scrapped). India became 6th country to build aircraft carrier.
WHO declared COVID-19 PHEIC over on:

WHO declared COVID-19 'no longer a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)' on 5 May 2023. End of pandemic's emergency phase. Originated Wuhan, China (December 2019). WHO declared pandemic 11 March 2020. ~7 million deaths officially, ~20 million estimated (excess mortality). Vaccines: ~13 billion doses administered globally.
AI Safety Summit 2023 was held at:

AI Safety Summit (1-2 November 2023, Bletchley Park, UK): where Alan Turing cracked Enigma code in WWII. 28 countries + EU signed Bletchley Declaration on AI safety. India, China, USA signed. Aim: cooperate on AI risks (especially frontier AI). Follow-up: Seoul (May 2024), France (February 2025). India participated.

COP28 (30 November - 13 December 2023): Dubai, UAE. Sultan Al Jaber (President, also ADNOC CEO - controversial). Outcomes: 1) Loss + Damage Fund operationalized ($792M initial pledges), 2) 'Transition away from fossil fuels' in energy systems (first time, weak wording), 3) Tripling renewable capacity by 2030, 4) Methane emissions reduction, 5) Global Stocktake (first, since Paris 2015).
Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Bill) was passed in:

Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Bill): passed September 2023 (106th Constitutional Amendment). 1/3rd reservation for women in Lok Sabha + state assemblies. 15 years implementation. Introduced in new Parliament building. To be implemented after delimitation (likely 2029).
BRICS expanded to include new members in:

BRICS expansion (1 January 2024): Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, UAE joined. Saudi Arabia invited but undecided. Argentina declined (under Milei). BRICS+: 10 members now (Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa + new). ~40% world GDP (PPP), 45% population.
Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024 faced opposition. Waqf Boards manage:

Waqf (Amendment) Bill 2024: proposes reforms to Waqf Act 1995. Waqf Boards (Central + State) manage Muslim religious + charitable endowments. India has 3rd largest waqf properties (~8.7 lakh). Controversies: inclusion of non-Muslims in Boards, survey powers, dispute resolution. Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) reviewed (2024).
T20 Cricket World Cup 2024 (men's) was won by:

T20 World Cup 2024 (men's, June, USA-West Indies co-hosted): India won (second T20 WC title, after 2007). Beat South Africa in final (29 June 2024, Barbados). Captain: Rohit Sharma. Virat Kohli Player of Match (final, 76 runs). Last matches for Rohit, Kohli, Jadeja in T20Is. India's first ICC trophy since 2013 Champions Trophy.
PM Vishwakarma Yojana was launched on:

PM Vishwakarma Yojana (PM-VIKAS, 17 Sep 2023, Vishwakarma Jayanti): for traditional artisans/craftspeople (18 trades - carpenter, mason, blacksmith, goldsmith, potter, etc.). Recognition, collateral-free loan ₹1+2 lakh, 5% interest subvention, skill training, toolkit, digital empowerment. ~5 crore beneficiaries.
Reliance Industries' Anant Ambani wedding was in:

Anant Ambani wedding: 12 July 2024 (Mumbai), to Radhika Merchant. Multi-day pre-wedding events (Jamnagar March, cruise May, Mumbai July). Costliest Indian wedding estimated (hundreds of crores). International celebrities attended (Justin Bieber, Rihanna, Kim Kardashian, John Cena). Business + political figures. Jio World Centre venue.
New Parliament building was inaugurated on:

New Parliament (28 May 2023): inaugurated by PM Modi. Built by Tata Projects (₹971 crore). Triangular shape (vs old circular). 645 Lok Sabha seats (888 if needed), 384 Raj Sabha (472 if joint). Banyan tree as central theme. Old building (1927) heritage building.
Which international summit focused on AI safety in 2023?

AI Safety Summit: 1-2 November 2023, Bletchley Park, UK (where Turing cracked Enigma code). 28 countries + EU signed Bletchley Declaration on AI safety. India, China, USA signed. Aim: cooperate on AI risks. Follow-up: Seoul 2024, France 2025.

India forex reserves (October 2024): $704.9 billion (record). 4th largest after China (~$3.3T), Japan (~$1.2T), Switzerland (~$0.9T). Components: FCA, gold, SDR, IMF reserve tranche. Supports rupee, ~12 months import cover. Gold reserves increasing (RBI buying). ~10% of GDP.
India's first space-based mission to study the Sun is:

Aditya-L1 (2 September 2023, PSLV-C57): India's first solar mission. Halo orbit around L1 Lagrangian point (~1.5 million km from Earth). 7 payloads (VELC, SUIT, SoLEXS, HEL1OS, ASPEX, PAPA, MAG). Study solar corona, photosphere, chromosphere, solar wind, CMEs. ISRO's first observatory class space-based mission. Reached L1 on 6 January 2024.
Anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule) was strengthened by:

91st Amendment (2003, Vajpayee government): strengthened anti-defection. Reduced size of Council of Ministers (max 15% of LS). Disqualified defectors from ministerial posts during remaining term. Removed split exception (1/3rd). Original: 52nd Amendment (1985, Rajiv Gandhi).
Which Indian was awarded Nobel Prize 2023?

Nobel Economics 2023: Claudia Goldin (Harvard, USA) - 'for having advanced our understanding of women's labour market outcomes'. First woman solo winner (others shared). Studied 200 years of women's workforce participation. Indian Nobel winners 21st century: Banerjee (2019), Satyarthi (2014), Kailash (2014 - shared with Malala).
India's stock market (Sensex) crossed which mark for first time in 2024?

Sensex crossed 80,000 (3 July 2024). Reached peak ~85,978 (27 Sep 2024). Then declined. NIFTY 50 crossed 25,000 (3 July 2024). India among top performing markets globally. Reasons: strong GDP growth, corporate earnings, FII inflows, retail participation (SIPs).
Neeraj Chopra won silver at Paris Olympics 2024 in:

Neeraj Chopra (Haryana): silver at Paris Olympics 2024 javelin (89.45m). Gold at Tokyo 2020 (87.58m, India's first Olympic gold in athletics). Arshad Nadeem (Pakistan) won gold (92.97m, Olympic record). First Indian with two individual Olympic medals.
Nobel Prize in Literature 2023 was awarded to:

Jon Fosse: Norwegian author (born 1959). Nobel Prize Literature 2023 - 'for his innovative prose and dramas which give voice to the unsayable'. Known for 'Septology'. Nynorsk (New Norwegian) language writer. Minimalist style. Plays widely performed worldwide.

Chandrayaan-3 landed 23 August 2023 at 6:04 PM IST. Vikram lander soft-landed near lunar south pole. Pragyan rover deployed. Landing site named 'Shiva Shakti Point' (PM Modi). National Space Day: 23 August (declared). First country to land near lunar south pole.

Russia-Ukraine war: Russia invaded Ukraine 24 February 2022. Largest European conflict since WWII. Causes: NATO expansion concerns, Ukraine's pro-West stance, Crimea 2014 annexation. Sanctions on Russia. India maintained neutral stance, purchased Russian oil (discounted). 2024: stalemate. Türkiye, China mediation efforts.

Russia-Ukraine war: Russia invaded Ukraine on 24 February 2022. Largest European conflict since WWII. Causes: NATO expansion concerns, Ukraine's pro-West stance, Crimea 2014 annexation. Sanctions on Russia. India maintained neutral stance, purchased Russian oil.

Sensex (BSE): crossed 80,000 (3 July 2024). Reached peak ~85,978 (27 September 2024). Then declined. NIFTY 50 crossed 25,000 (3 July 2024). India among top performing markets globally. Reasons: strong GDP growth, corporate earnings, FII inflows, retail participation (SIPs ~₹20,000 crore/month).

NATO expansion: Finland joined 4 April 2023 (32nd member, ending 70+ years neutrality). Sweden joined 7 March 2024 (32nd → 33rd member). Both applied after Russia-Ukraine war. NATO founded 4 April 1949, HQ Brussels, currently 32 members (after Sweden). Article 5: collective defense.
Ram Mandir consecration (Pran Pratishtha) was on:

Ram Mandir Pran Pratishtha (22 January 2024): Ayodhya. PM Modi as chief yajman. Temple dedicated to Lord Ram Lalla. Built on disputed Babri Masjid site (demolished 6 December 1992). Supreme Court verdict (9 November 2019). Architecture: Nagara style, pink sandstone, ~₹1800 crore cost. Trust: Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra.
Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani's son Anant Ambani married in:

Anant Ambani wedding: 12 July 2024 (Mumbai), to Radhika Merchant. Multi-day pre-wedding events (Jamnagar March, cruise May, Mumbai July). Costliest Indian wedding estimated (hundreds of crores). International celebrities attended. Business + political figures. Jio World Centre venue.

ChatGPT: launched 30 November 2022 by OpenAI. Reached 100 million users in 2 months (fastest ever). Based on GPT-3.5. ChatGPT Plus ($20/month) launched Feb 2023. GPT-4 (March 2023), GPT-4 Turbo (Nov 2023), GPT-4o (May 2024), GPT-4o mini (July 2024). Sparked AI race.
US presidential election 2024 was won by:

US Election 2024 (5 November): Donald Trump (Republican) defeated Kamala Harris (Democrat, replaced Biden July 2024). Trump became 47th President. Republicans won Senate + House. Trump second non-consecutive term (Grover Cleveland first, 1885-89, 1893-97). Jan 20, 2025 inauguration.
Cricket World Cup 2023 final was held at:

Cricket World Cup 2023 (hosted by India, Oct-Nov 2023). Final: 19 November 2023, Narendra Modi Stadium (Motera, Ahmedabad, ~1,32,000 capacity - world's largest cricket stadium). Australia beat India by 6 wickets. India won all 10 league matches but lost final. Travis Head Player of Match (137 runs).
WHO declared COVID-19 pandemic over (no longer PHEIC) on:

WHO declared COVID-19 'no longer a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC)' on 5 May 2023. End of pandemic's emergency phase. Originated Wuhan, China (Dec 2019). WHO declared pandemic 11 March 2020. ~7 million deaths officially, ~20 million estimated.
India's forex reserves crossed which milestone in 2024?

India forex reserves (Oct 2024): $704.9 billion (record). 4th largest (after China ~$3.3T, Japan ~$1.2T, Switzerland ~$0.9T). Components: FCA, gold, SDR, IMF position. Supports rupee, import cover (~12 months). Gold reserves increasing (RBI buying).
James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) was launched in:

JWST (James Webb Space Telescope): launched 25 December 2021 (Ariane 5, French Guiana). Replaced Hubble (1990). Largest space telescope (6.5m mirror). Orbit: L2 (1.5 million km). IR observations: early universe, exoplanet atmospheres, galaxy formation. First images July 2022. Cost: ~$10 billion (NASA, ESA, CSA). Named after James Webb (NASA admin 1961-68).
AI Safety Summit 2024 was held in:

AI Seoul Summit (21-22 May 2024): co-hosted by UK + South Korea. 'Seoul Declaration' on AI safety. 16 AI companies (OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Anthropic, etc.) signed Frontier AI Safety Commitments. Follow-up to Bletchley 2023. Next: France (Feb 2025). India participated.
Türkiye's name change from Turkey was officially adopted by UN in:

Türkiye: UN adopted name change 26 May 2022 (Türkiye Cumhuriyeti - Republic of Türkiye). Requested by President Erdoğan. Reasons: avoids bird + slang associations, reflects Turkish origin. Türkiye adopted in 2023 (English). Also 'Türkçe' language. Ankara capital (not Istanbul).
African Union was made permanent G20 member at:

AU admitted to G20 (9 September 2023, New Delhi): PM Modi's initiative. AU has 55 member states, ~1.4 billion population, $3 trillion GDP. Joined as 21st member of G20 (originally EU was 20th). Strengthened Global South representation. AU headquarters: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Current chair (2024): Mauritania.

IPL 2024: KKR (Kolkata Knight Riders) won (3rd title, after 2012, 2014). Beat SRH (Sunrisers Hyderabad) in final (26 May 2024, Chennai). KKR topped league stage. Captain: Shreyas Iyer. Mentor: Gautam Gambhir (KKR captain 2012, 2014). Player of Match: Mitchell Starc (KKR, 2/14 in final).
Nobel Peace Prize 2023 was awarded to:

Narges Mohammadi: Iranian human rights activist. Nobel Peace Prize 2023 - for fight against women's oppression in Iran. Currently in Iranian prison. 19th woman to win Peace Prize. Her children received on her behalf. 'Zan, Zendegi, Azadi' (Woman, Life, Freedom) movement.

Paris Olympics 2024: 26 July - 11 August. India won 6 medals: 1 silver (Neeraj Chopra - javelin), 5 bronze (Manu Bhaker - 10m air pistol + mixed team, Swapnil Kusale - 50m rifle 3P, hockey men, Aman Sehrawat - wrestling). Total medals: 6 (same as Tokyo 2020).
WHO declared mpox (formerly monkeypox) PHEIC in:

WHO declared mpox PHEIC second time on 14 August 2024 (first: July 2022 - ended May 2023). New variant (clade Ib) spread from DRC to neighboring African countries. Africa CDC declared continental PHEIC. India: screening at airports, 1 case reported (2024).

G20 Summit 2023: 9-10 September 2023, New Delhi (Bharat Mandapam). First G20 hosted by India. Theme: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (One Earth, One Family, One Future). African Union admitted as permanent member. Delhi Declaration consensus.
India's first woman tribal President is:

Droupadi Murmu: 15th President of India (since 25 July 2022). First woman tribal President. First President from Odisha. Second woman President (after Pratibha Patil, 2007-12). Former Jharkhand Governor. BJP member. Santhal tribe.

Israel-Hamas war: started 7 October 2023. Hamas launched Operation Al-Aqsa Flood - attacked southern Israel, ~1200 killed, ~250 hostages. Israel's response: invasion of Gaza, ~40,000+ killed (mostly civilians). Ceasefire Jan 2025. Humanitarian crisis, ICC/ICJ cases.
PM Vishwakarma Yojana and PM Suryodaya Yojana are aimed at:

PM Vishwakarma Yojana: traditional artisans (loans, training). PM Suryodaya Yojana: rooftop solar. Both launched 2023-24. Aim: Aatmanirbhar Bharat, livelihood support, energy transition. Targeted at unorganized sector, especially rural, women, SC/ST.
Hamas leader Yahya Sinwar was killed in:

Yahya Sinwar (Hamas leader in Gaza): killed 17 October 2024 by IDF in Rafah, Gaza. Mastermind of 7 October 2023 attack. Succeeded Ismail Haniyeh (killed July 2024 in Tehran). Death seen as major blow to Hamas. Continued conflict - hostage negotiations ongoing.
ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 was hosted by:

T20 World Cup 2024 (men's, June): co-hosted by USA + West Indies. India won (beat South Africa in final, 29 June, Barbados). Captain: Rohit Sharma. India's first ICC trophy since 2013. USA's first major ICC event. 20 teams participated. Final: Kensington Oval, Barbados. India's second T20 WC title (after 2007 inaugural).

COP29 (11-24 Nov 2024): Baku, Azerbaijan. Major focus: climate finance - New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG) of $300 billion/year by 2035 (up from $100 billion, but criticised as inadequate). Many leaders skipped. COP30 (2025): Belém, Brazil.
African Union was made permanent member of G20 during which summit?

AU admitted to G20 (9 September 2023, New Delhi): PM Modi's initiative. AU has 55 member states, ~1.4 billion population, $3 trillion GDP. Joined as 21st member of G20 (originally EU was 20th). Strengthened Global South representation.
Pradhan Mantri Suryodaya Yojana was launched in:

PM Suryodaya Yojana (launched 22 January 2024): rooftop solar installation in 1 crore households. Reduces electricity bills (₹15,000-18,000/year). Subsidy: ₹30,000-78,000 (based on capacity). After Ram Mandir consecration. Aim: 40 GW rooftop solar. Originally NM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana.
Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam (Women's Reservation Bill) passed in:

Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam: passed September 2023. 106th Constitutional Amendment. 1/3rd reservation for women in Lok Sabha + state assemblies. 15-year implementation. Introduced in new Parliament building (Special Session Sept 2023). To be implemented after delimitation (likely 2029 Lok Sabha elections).
Indian Premier League (IPL) 2024 was won by:

IPL 2024: KKR (Kolkata Knight Riders) won (3rd title, after 2012, 2014). Beat SRH (Sunrisers Hyderabad) in final (26 May 2024, Chennai). KKR topped league stage. Captain: Shreyas Iyer. Mentor: Gautam Gambhir (KKR captain 2012, 2014).
India hosted the Quad Summit in 2024 in:

Quad (Australia, India, Japan, USA): leaders' summit. 2024: scheduled for Delhi in Jan, postponed. Virtual Summit held 18 March 2024. 2023: Hiroshima (May, sidelines of G7). 2022: Tokyo (May). 2021: Washington (Sep, in-person), virtual (Mar).
One Nation, One Election proposal recommends:

One Nation, One Election (High Level Committee, Ram Nath Kovind chair, March 2024 report): recommends simultaneous Lok Sabha + State Assembly elections (first phase). Also municipal + panchayat within 100 days. Needs constitutional amendment. Cost savings, governance continuity. Opposition concerns: federalism, regional issues. Implementation: 2029 likely.
North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) added which countries in 2023-24?

NATO expansion: Finland joined 4 April 2023 (32nd member, ending 70+ years neutrality). Sweden joined 7 March 2024 (32nd → 33rd member). Both applied after Russia-Ukraine war. NATO founded 4 April 1949, HQ Brussels, currently 32 members (after Sweden).
Delimitation Commission redraws constituency boundaries based on:

Delimitation: redrawing constituency boundaries based on latest census. Currently frozen at 1971 census (until 2026, by 84th Amendment 2001). Next delimitation likely 2026+ based on 2031 census. Southern states concerned: may lose seats due to better population control. Women's reservation depends on this.

G20 Summit 2023: 9-10 September 2023, New Delhi (Bharat Mandapam, Pragati Maidan). First G20 hosted by India. Theme: 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam' (One Earth, One Family, One Future). African Union admitted as permanent member. Delhi Declaration consensus (Russia-Ukraine: avoided strong language). PM Modi handed presidency to Brazil (Lula).
Britain's new Prime Minister in July 2024 was from which party?

UK Election 4 July 2024: Labour (Keir Starmer) defeated Conservatives (Rishi Sunak - first PM of Indian origin, Oct 2022 - July 2024). Labour won 412 seats (Conservative 121, worst since 1832). Starmer became PM 5 July 2024 (56th). Reversed many Conservative policies (Rwanda deportation scrapped).
Saudi Arabia-Iran détente (2023) was brokered by:

China brokered Saudi-Iran détente (10 March 2023, Beijing). Resumed diplomatic relations after 7 years (severed 2016). Both sides agreed to reopen embassies. Major diplomatic victory for China in Middle East. Failed to end Yemen war but reduced regional tensions. Egypt-Saudi-UAE grouping vs Iran-Turkey-Qatar (rivalry).
T20 Cricket World Cup 2024 was won by:

T20 World Cup 2024 (men's, June, USA-West Indies co-hosted): India won (second T20 WC title, after 2007). Beat South Africa in final (29 June, Barbados). Captain Rohit Sharma. Virat Kohli Player of Match (final). Last matches for Rohit, Kohli, Jadeja in T20Is.
Which country hosted COP28 (climate summit) in 2023?

COP28 (30 Nov - 13 Dec 2023): Dubai, UAE. Sultan Al Jaber (President, also ADNOC CEO - controversial). Outcomes: Loss + Damage Fund operationalized, 'transition away from fossil fuels' in energy systems (first time), tripling renewable capacity by 2030, methane reduction.
